description: Let a bout go without a write-up: the learning is recorded as having happened and no break is earned. Use it only when the learner says the time went nowhere; a bout they did learn from should be written up, however briefly.
name: abandon_learning_bout

description: Legacy: add sources from the library to a companion record (a Notebook or a Goal) as approved seeds. Prefer add_notebook_sources for a Notebook and add_goal_sources for a timebound Goal, which check the kind of record they are given. Different from review_suggested_sources, which only approves sources ForeverLM already discovered. Find source IDs with search_sources_semantic (pass exclude_notebook_id so sources already in the goal never come back) or list_sources first. Sources already in the goal are skipped.

source_ids.description: Library source IDs to add as approved seeds.

name: add_companion_sources

description: Give the questions of a course's quizzes already written the pictures that make their points clear, without rewriting a question: ids, scores and Memory items stay. The slides of every lecture video the quizzes cover are captured first when they never were (capture_slides, default true; it reads the video and takes a while for a long course). Then one model call per quiz, on the learner's Lecture Quiz Writing route, picks for each question the lecture slide or the reading figure (printed on the reading's pages) that helps and whether it is shown with the question or held for the answer. Drawing is off by default: draw false adds only those source pictures. With draw true, the picker may instead brief a new picture where no slide or figure shows the point, up to 12 a quiz, and ForeverLM draws the briefs on the learner's image model. That paid route is refused until the learner has seen the request count, selected model and published maximum cost and explicitly agrees; then repeat it with confirm_drawings true and approved_spend_usd. A question no picture helps gets none, and a question with a picture keeps it unless replace is true. choose false skips the picks and only draws pictures already briefed, with the same confirmation. For a quiz you wrote yourself you can instead look at frames and pages with show_source_image, or draw with generate_image or keep a picture made elsewhere with save_image, and pin it with set_course_quiz_picture. Returns, quiz by quiz, how many questions got a picture and how many were drawn. cancel_ai_work stops a run; the pictures already chosen and drawn stay. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

capture_slides.description: Capture the slides of lecture videos that have none first (default true). False uses only slides already captured.

choose.description: Choose slides, figures and drawings for questions without a picture (default true). False only draws the pictures already briefed.

confirm_drawings.description: With draw true, pass true only after the learner has seen this tool's refusal with the maximum image-request count, selected model and published maximum cost and explicitly agreed. Pass that approval as approved_spend_usd too. Defaults false.

draw.description: Brief and draw separately billed generated pictures for questions no slide or figure shows, and draw those already briefed (default false). False chooses slides and figures only.

quiz_ids.description: Optional: only these quizzes, by the quiz_id get_course shows; default every quiz of the course.

replace.description: Choose again for questions that already have a picture (default false).

name: add_course_quiz_pictures

description: Put existing library sources on a timebound Goal — the app's drop of sources onto a Goal's row on the Goals tab. They join the Goal's approved pool at once (no discovery, no approval step), and a Goal tagged to a Notebook hands them on to that Notebook's pool too. Sources already on the Goal are skipped. Find ids with search_sources_semantic or list_sources; file new material with add_source first. A Notebook is refused — add_notebook_sources takes those. To place the sources on days, follow with assign_sources_to_day.

source_ids.description: Existing library source IDs to put on the Goal.

name: add_goal_sources

description: Add existing source IDs to an explicitly identified Notebook's persistent source context. To find candidates first, call search_sources_semantic with exclude_notebook_id set to this Notebook so sources already in it never come back as results. Sources already in the Notebook are skipped.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

source_ids.description: Existing source IDs to add

name: add_notebook_sources

description: Associate an existing paper source with a course lecture, as assigned reading or as a paper the lecture only cites. Assigned reading is a row of the course's path and is quizzed with its lecture; on a lecture with a video, a paper that is only cited has no row and opens from the video's Papers menu. Validates that source_id is an active paper and returns the durable lecture-item ID. Calling it for a paper already attached changes nothing unless assigned_reading is given, which sets how the paper stands.

assigned_reading.description: true when reading the paper is actually necessary for the course (the syllabus or lecturer assigns it, the lecture is built on it, or the learner asks); false when the lecture only cites it, as on a slide. Omitted, a new association is assigned reading and an existing one keeps its standing.

name: add_paper_to_lecture

description: Add a non-paper source written by someone else to the knowledge base. Its content is shown verbatim in the reader, not rendered as Markdown: for something you wrote yourself, such as a report or a synthesis, use create_doc instead. Papers must use import_paper_from_url, import_local_pdf_as_paper, or the ingest-only import_connector_paper so the mandatory paper models run. A Codex site (….chatgpt.site), a Claude artifact, a Google Doc or a ForeverLM site is refused too, whatever content is passed: ForeverLM links those pages rather than scraping them — a Codex site answers an anonymous fetch with its sign-in page — so call link_page with the url instead. Convoke query results (platform.convoke.bio) are refused as well: they are answers to a live query, not pages, and are never sources. For courses/books, specify parent_group as the display title or stable group ID; both require it, because course material outside a course is never listed and a chapter outside a book is a loose row with no cover. For meetings, parent_group names the recurring series (meeting group) the session belongs to and occurred_at is when it took place; without occurred_at a meeting is dated by the moment it was added. A YouTube playlist is a course, not a source: add_source refuses a playlist url, and import_youtube_playlist imports it. A podcast episode is source_type podcast, never video or article, and a link on a podcast host (podcasts.apple.com, Spotify, Overcast and the like) is filed as one whatever source_type says. ForeverLM reads an episode from its transcript, which it finds on Apple Podcasts, so content passed for a podcast is not kept: the learner confirms the episode in the app, or find_podcast_match and then resolve_podcast_match confirm it. A URL the learner removed, or a meeting series the learner removed, is not re-added: the result says so ("Not added: … removed by the learner"), and only the learner re-adding it in the app brings it back. Pass notebook_id to file the source in a Notebook as well — a Notebook id from list_notebooks (or a Goal id from list_goals) — as adding it from inside that Notebook in the app does; when the url is already in the library, that source joins the Notebook instead. notebook_id is used only as given (never the app's selection, never matched by title), is checked before anything is added, and is refused for ingest-only plugins and for a team's Notebook the learner can only read. The answer's last line, notebook_id_applied, says whether the source is in the Notebook. The source will appear in the app's Studio tab.

content.description: Full text content of the source (optional)

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook to file the source in as well: a Notebook id from list_notebooks, or a Goal id from list_goals. Omit to add to the library only.

occurred_at.description: When the meeting took place, ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-09-02T16:55:00Z). Meetings only; the Meetings tab dates and sorts by it.

parent_group.description: Course/book display title or stable group ID. Required when source_type is course or book. For source_type meeting: the recurring series, matched by meeting-group ID or title (case-insensitive) and created when it does not exist yet.

title.description: Title of the source

url.description: URL or file path of the source

name: add_source

description: Attach any source to a course lecture as a material. For paper sources, prefer add_paper_to_lecture so the source type is validated and duplicate associations are avoided.
name: add_source_to_lecture

description: Add several sources in one call (at most 50). Each item takes the same fields as add_source plus update_existing; an item whose url is a page ForeverLM links (a Codex site, Claude artifact, Google Doc or ForeverLM site) is refused per item, naming link_page, as add_source refuses it, and so is a Convoke query result (platform.convoke.bio); items whose canonical URL already exists are reported per item instead of failing the batch, and update_existing refreshes that existing source's content/title/author in place — and, for a meeting, its occurred_at and parent_group, so a re-push corrects the date and series of meetings first pushed without them. Returns a summary line plus one result line per item. Built for user-made plugins pushing a feed — use stable canonical URLs so repeated runs deduplicate, and keep the total payload under ~1 MB. notebook_id files every item that was added, updated or already there in that one Notebook as well (full-scope connections only); the answer's last line, notebook_id_applied, counts how many joined it.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook for the whole batch: a Notebook id from list_notebooks, or a Goal id from list_goals. Every item added, updated or already present joins it. Not available to ingest-only plugins.

sources.description: Items to add, in order. Maximum 50 per call.

content.description: Full text content of the source (optional)

occurred_at.description: When the meeting took place, ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-09-02T16:55:00Z). Meetings only; omitted, the meeting is dated by when it was added.

parent_group.description: Course/book display title or stable group ID. Required when source_type is course or book. For source_type meeting: the recurring series, matched by meeting-group ID or title (case-insensitive) and created when it does not exist yet.

title.description: Title of the source

update_existing.description: When the URL already exists, update its content/title/author — and a meeting's occurred_at and parent_group — in place instead of skipping (default false).

url.description: Canonical URL or file path — the dedup key. Keep it stable across runs.

name: add_sources

description: Integrate a textbook from the learner's library into a course as targeted reading: for each lecture, the sections of the book this learner should read with it (a run of pages within a chapter, or a whole chapter when it has no sections), and why, placed after the lecture in the course. The Textbook Readings model chooses them from the course title, each lecture's transcript, and the sections the book's own chapter files carry. When the learner has supplied About you, a course focus, or linked Notebooks, those further tailor the plan; when they have not, the course materials are sufficient and no personal background is inferred. Sections covering what the learner says they already know are left out, and a lecture the book adds nothing to gets no reading. Calling again with the same book replaces that book's readings; videos, quizzes and other books' readings stay. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key for one planning call and takes about a minute. Returns each reading with its lecture, chapter source_id, pages, item_id and reason. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

book.description: The book: its title as the library shows it, its book id, or the source_id of any of its chapters.

course_focus.description: Optional: what the learner needs from this course, in their own words. Saved for this course. At most 1000 characters.

learner_background.description: Optional: where the learner is coming from, in their own words: their background, what they know well, what is new to them. Saved as their About you, which every course reads. At most 4000 characters.

name: add_textbook_to_course

description: Make a linked page ForeverLM's own: in one call the linked Codex site, Claude artifact or Google Doc is unlinked into a Markdown Doc and published as a page on foreverlm.com, at the address the result returns, where write_doc and edit_doc with publish edit it from then on — from Codex, Claude or the app. The body is ForeverLM's text copy of the page unless markdown is passed; pass the page's real Markdown whenever you have it (Codex built the site, so it knows what is on it), because the text copy is what the rendered page said and not its source. readers and slug are publish_doc's. Refused for a Doc that is not a linked page, and — with nothing changed — when the Mac is not signed in with Apple. The original page is never touched; only ForeverLM's entry changes.

doc_id.description: Doc ID from list_docs, with kind codex_site, claude_artifact or google_doc.

markdown.description: Optional. The page's complete content as Markdown, used as the Doc's body instead of ForeverLM's text copy.

readers.description: Optional. Email addresses the page is shared with; omit or pass an empty list for a page anyone with the link can read.

slug.description: Optional custom address, the part after foreverlm.com/share/: 3–64 lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens.

name: adopt_page

description: Record the learner's answer to one question of a mnemonic reading, as the reading's own Forgot and Remembered do. The question's first answer keeps it as a Memory card at once, remembered or not, with that answer as its first (outcome kept), and the card review asks it again on its schedule. A question kept already is answered as the card review answers a card: recorded only while it is due, once a sitting (already_recorded), not_counted otherwise (an early answer never moves its schedule), retired for a card the learner retired. Pass reading_id and question_id as get_mnemonic_reading returns them, remembered (the learner's own say, or your judgment of what they answered, told to them), and sitting_id when you run several answers as one sitting; without it, a day's answers over MCP are one sitting. A question whose passage its source no longer prints cannot be kept and is refused. Returns the outcome, the card's item_id, its last grade and when it is next asked.

remembered.description: true when the learner remembered the answer, false when they forgot it.

sitting_id.description: Optional: one id for the answers of one sitting, at most 200 characters.

name: answer_mnemonic_question

description: Append markdown to a Notebook's synthesis notes without replacing existing notes.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: append_notebook_notes

description: Add Markdown to the end of the learner's daily note (today's unless date names another day), making the note when the day has none: the way to jot a thought, a finding or a task into the day, as in Roam Research's Daily Notes. The Markdown lands as its own block or blocks after everything already there (bullets that follow bullets join the list; anything else starts after a blank line). Nothing already in the note changes, and the write is checked against the note's revision, so a line the learner is typing at that moment is kept. Write in the notes grammar: [[Title]], #tag or #[[Two words]] name a page by its title, [Title](foreverlm://doc/<id>) links a Doc and [Title](foreverlm://idea/<id>) an Idea, a foreverlm://source/<id> link or a paper's web address cites a source, and ((id)) references a block, reading as its words, by the id get_block and get_linked_references give. Answers with the note's doc_id, title and new revision.

date.description: The day, as YYYY-MM-DD ("2026-10-06"), or today, yesterday or tomorrow. Defaults to today where the learner's Mac is.

markdown.description: The Markdown to add, e.g. "- Finished the methods of [[Mitophagy in neurons]]".

name: append_to_daily_note

description: Show a lens over the learner's Canvas: lay the cards you name out grouped under labels (layout groups), on two axes (layout axes), or beside the concepts of a topic in the order they connect (layout concepts), around where the learner is looking, and fade the rest. Any source, Doc or Idea in the library can be in a lens, placed on the canvas or not. The learner asked to see their material another way — "group these by species", "plot them by how direct the measurement is against how alive the subject is", "zoom in on the PINK1–Parkin axis in Parkinson's and place the papers in context" — and you decide each card's place by reading the sources (search tools, get_source_content) first. For a concepts lens, name the concepts or steps of the biology in your own words ("PINK1 builds up on depolarised mitochondria", "Parkin is recruited and activated", "Ubiquitin chains mark the outer membrane", "Mitophagy"), give each a one-sentence note and the papers that bear on it (a concept may have none), and link them in the direction the biology runs with a short label ("phosphorylates", "recruits"). A lens moves nothing the learner placed and is not saved: the banner over the canvas offers Keep, which places the cards where the lens put them and turns its groups or concepts into regions, and Back to My Canvas. Never call it to tidy the canvas on your own initiative. Opens the Canvas beside the chat if it is not showing. A new lens replaces the one showing.

concepts.description: For layout concepts: each concept or step of the topic, in the order to stack them, with a one-sentence note and the cards that bear on it. A card listed twice shows under its first concept.

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> (a Doc, site, animation, audio overview or reading), idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id> (a shortcut to another canvas), chat:<session_id> (a chat) or picture:<image_id> (an image from list_images). A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

note.description: One sentence on what it is or does, drawn under its name.

groups.description: For layout groups: each group's label and its cards, in the order to show them. A card listed twice shows in its first group.

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> (a Doc, site, animation, audio overview or reading), idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id> (a shortcut to another canvas), chat:<session_id> (a chat) or picture:<image_id> (an image from list_images). A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

hide_others.description: Fade the cards the lens does not name almost away (default true), or only dim them.

layout.description: groups: cards under labelled groups (pass groups). axes: cards placed on two axes (pass points, x_axis, y_axis). concepts: cards beside the concepts of a topic, laid out left to right in the order the links run (pass concepts and links).

links.description: For layout concepts: how one concept leads to another, by their labels, with a short label for the arrow. A concept nothing leads to is drawn on the left.

points.description: For layout axes: each card's place, x and y from 0 (the axis's low end) to 1 (its high end).

title.description: The lens's name in the banner, e.g. "By species".

label.description: What the axis measures, in the learner's words where they have them.
What the axis measures, in the learner's words where they have them.

name: apply_map_lens

description: Archive a source by ID, keeping the source record but removing cached content, embeddings, and Schedule assignments.
name: archive_source

description: Tidy or align cards already on the learner's Canvas, as Tidy Up and Align in its right-click menu do. arrangement lays the cards out as a row (left to right), a column (top to bottom) or a grid (about half again as wide as tall), taking them in reading order of where they sit now, each by its own width and height, 30 apart, with the selection's top left staying where it is. align then moves every card to the selection's left, center (the middle of its width), right, top, middle (the middle of its height) or bottom, by its own size; with both, the arrangement comes first. A region that held a card grows to hold it where it lands. Pass arrangement, align or both, and at least two cards that are on the Canvas; a card in a locked region is not moved: a call naming one is refused whole (unlock the region with update_canvas_region first). Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Returns how many cards moved and the cards as they now are, each with its rect.

align.description: Then align them on this edge or middle of the selection's bounds.

arrangement.description: Lay the cards out as a row, a column or a grid.

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id>, idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id>, chat:<session_id>, picture:<image_id>, clip:<id> or page:<source_id>:<n>. A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

name: arrange_on_canvas

description: Ask the learner's Canvas about cards on it, as the Ask in its inspector does. tool bridge finds sources in their library that connect the cards; connect proposes typed arrows between cards placed on the canvas (supports, contradicts, explains, causes, measures, extends, example or same_question, each with a short label); gaps names research questions the cards leave open. One call to the learner's chat model, grounded in passages from their library. The answer is drawn dotted on the Canvas beside the cards (the Canvas opens beside the chat if it is not showing) and returned here: each proposal with its why in ForeverLM's words and the passages it rests on. No tool keeps a proposal: keeping one places the source, draws the arrow or writes the question as an Idea, which is the learner's own act on their Canvas (the ✓ on a proposal, or Keep All); dismissing one tells the next ask of that tool not to offer it again. A new ask replaces the proposals showing. Refused while a lens shows (clear_map_lens first). Stop a running ask with cancel_ai_work. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

item_ids.description: The cards to ask about, 1 to 24, by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> or idea:<idea_id>. A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

tool.description: bridge: library sources that connect the cards. connect: arrows between the cards placed on the canvas (needs two). gaps: questions the cards leave open.

name: ask_canvas

description: Put sources on a specific day of the Schedule. A source already on the Schedule moves there; one that is not yet on it, whether it sits in a Goal's or Notebook's pool or only in the library, is placed on that day. With goal_id (a Goal or a Notebook), every source named that is not yet that goal's joins it — pool and tag — including one already on the Schedule for another goal. Without goal_id nothing is tagged, and the Notebook open in a ForeverLM window is never inherited. This is how sources get onto the Schedule, and it does not disturb any other day. Use get_schedule first to see valid source IDs and day dates.

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID to tag the sources to and add them to its pool. Omit to place them untagged.

source_ids.description: Library source IDs to place on the day

name: assign_sources_to_day

description: Assign something to learn to one member of a team — a parent assigning to a child, in a family team. Each source or Doc is copied into the team (the original stays in this library) and becomes a task on the team's Assignments board for that member, pointing at the team's copy. The task marks itself done when the member reads the source to the end or reviews it. Assigning the same item to the same member again updates their open task. Refused in a read-only team.

doc_id.description: A Doc to assign, from list_docs.

member.description: The member's user_record_name from list_teams, or their display name when it is unique in the team.

notes.description: Optional note for the member, such as what to look out for.

source_ids.description: Sources to assign, from list_sources or search_sources_semantic.

name: assign_to_member

description: Attach a local text file (transcript, notes, chat log, or other attachment) to a meeting session source as an additional artifact. The text becomes a section of the session's content (ordered transcript → notes → chat) and is listed with the session's artifacts, so one meeting can hold multiple sources. Re-attaching the same kind replaces that section. Use session source ids from get_meeting_group.

file_path.description: Absolute local path to a text, Markdown, VTT, or SRT file.

name: attach_meeting_artifact

description: Attach a local PDF file or download a remote PDF URL to a paper source, copying it into ForeverLM's synced Papers folder, extracting text, running AI paper metadata extraction, and clearing paywall/error state. A Slack file's download_url from read_slack_channel is accepted as pdf_url; ForeverLM fetches it as the learner.

file_path.description: Absolute local path to a PDF file. For backward compatibility, an http(s) PDF URL is also accepted.

pdf_url.description: HTTP(S) PDF URL to download and attach.

name: attach_pdf_to_paper

description: Attach a local text, Markdown, or HTML file to an article/manual source, copying it into ForeverLM's synced Articles folder and storing extracted text.

file_path.description: Absolute local path to a text, Markdown, or HTML file

name: attach_text_file_to_source

description: Lay a whole picture out on one of the learner's canvases in one call, on their word ("lay this paper out visually on a canvas", "mock up how these ideas connect"): write note cards, set them and cards from the library down in labelled groups, and draw arrows between them. Each note is an Idea of the learner's (a card with a title and a few lines of text; it is also linked to the canvas's notebook when the canvas belongs to one) that you author: a claim, a step, a question, a caveat. A note with source_id and quote is instead a passage card: the words are marked as a highlight in that source (the one the learner already has on them is reused), the card shows them, and clicking it opens the paper at those words, so quote the paper wherever a claim rests on it. Each group becomes a region of that name around its cards, set down in the order given, left to right; a card in no group is set down in free space. Cards from the library are named by item_id (source:<id>, doc:<id>, idea:<id>, canvas:<id> for a shortcut to another canvas, chat:<session_id>, picture:<image_id>), notes by the key you gave them. Arrows join two cards, each a note key or an item_id, with an optional short label. Keep what is observed apart from what is interpreted by putting them in different groups, and give each region a colour with the same meaning. A mind map is a tree: each trees entry names a region and a root note with nested children notes (all Ideas of the learner's, written the same way), set down left to right inside that region (the root at the left, each child to the right of its parent, a parent centred on its children), joined by tree branches, and the region's layout is a mind map so the Canvas keeps it one; a note in a tree may be named by its key in arrows. A paper can be laid out as its own pages too: each pdf_pages entry names a source with a PDF (a paper, or a book or hand-out kept as one), and its pages are set down as cards drawn from the PDF itself, one per page, left to right in a region named for the source, a row below the last, before the groups; name them page:<source_id>:<n> in groups and arrows, limit them to a range such as "1-8" (at most 60 at a time), and set collapsed to fold the region up to its name and count until the learner opens it. A talk can be laid out as its slides: each talks entry names a YouTube video or a meeting recording, and its slides are set down as a storyboard, the papers each slide cites that are in the library hung under it with an arrow from the slide. A paper whose PDF is on the Mac is set down as its first page, its title and authors under it, rather than as a card. Pass annotations (a note key or item_id to the words) to write the learner's reason for a card being on the canvas under it: any card but a note, whose own text holds its words; and give an arrow a stance (supports draws it green, contradicts red) to argue a claim. Nothing the learner already placed moves. Pass canvas_id (list_canvases) to build on a canvas other than the open one; it is opened. Returns the notes and passages made with their item_ids, the regions drawn, the mind maps laid out (trees: the region, the root and each note with its item_id), the pages laid out (pdf_pages: the region, the page count and each page's item_id), the talks laid out (talks: the region, the slides' and papers' item_ids and how many cited papers are not in the library) and the arrows drawn, and anything it could not resolve. One Undo step takes back everything it set down and drew, but the Ideas it made stay in the learner's Ideas. A card named in a group that is on the canvas already stays where it is (listed as already_on_canvas) and still takes its annotation and arrows.

annotations.description: The learner's words about why a card is on the canvas, drawn under it, by note key (a passage) or item_id: at most 600 characters each. Not for an Idea or a note, whose own text holds its words.

from.description: A note key or an item_id.

label.description: A short label on the arrow, e.g. "measured by".

stance.description: Which side of an argument it is on: supports (drawn green) or contradicts (red).

to.description: A note key or an item_id.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID from list_canvases. Defaults to the canvas open on the Mac.

groups.description: Labelled regions, at most 20, set down left to right in this order.

items.description: The cards in it, in reading order: note keys and item_ids.

notes.description: Note cards to write, at most 60.

key.description: A short name to refer to this note by in groups and arrows, unique among the notes.

quote.description: Makes this note a passage card: the words, copied verbatim from get_source_content, marked as a highlight in source_id. The card shows them, and a click on it opens the paper at them.

source_id.description: With quote: the source the passage is from (list_sources).

text.description: A few lines under the heading: the evidence, the caveat, the detail. For a passage, the learner's note on it.

title.description: The card's heading: a short claim or label. Not used for a passage.

pdf_pages.description: PDF sources to lay out as their pages, at most 10: each is set down as a row of cards, one per page, left to right in a region named for the source, before the groups.

collapsed.description: Fold the region up so only its name and count show until the learner opens it. Defaults to false.

pages.description: Which pages, one-based: a range such as "1-8" or "2,5,7-9". Defaults to all, at most 60 at a time; ask again with another range for the rest. Ignored when show is figures or figures_extended.

show.description: What the row holds: pages (default), figures (one clip card per main figure, cut from its page by the paper's printed captions and named by its label, as the Reader's Clip tool cuts one; the extended and supplementary figures left out), or figures_extended (the extended and supplementary figures too, after the main ones). Figures need a paper with printed figure captions; the cards are item_ids of the kind clip:<id>.

source_id.description: A source with a PDF on the Mac: a paper, or a book or hand-out kept as a PDF (list_sources).

talks.description: Videos or meeting recordings to lay out as their slides, at most 5: each is a storyboard of slide cards (clip:<id>, four to a row in the order shown, captured first if they never were), each slide with the papers it cites that are in the library hung under it and an arrow from the slide to each, in a region named for the talk, before the groups. Papers its slides cite that are not in the library are counted, not added (list_video_cited_papers, import_video_cited_paper); cited_papers_recorded 0 means the slides were never read for citations (scan_video_for_cited_papers) or cite nothing; a talk laid out before keeps its slides where they are and hangs the papers added since under theirs.

source_id.description: A YouTube video or a meeting with a recording (list_sources).

trees.description: Mind maps to lay out, at most 10, with at most 120 notes in all: each a region of the given name holding a tree of notes, the root at the left and each child to the right of its parent.

name.description: The region's name, e.g. the question the map explores.

root.description: The root note. children holds its child notes, each of the same shape, which may have children of their own.

children.description: Child notes, in the order to show them top to bottom, each with key, title, text and children as here.

key.description: Optional name to refer to this note by in arrows, unique among all the notes.

text.description: A few lines under the heading. Optional.

title.description: The note's heading: a short claim or label.

ungrouped.description: Cards (note keys or item_ids) to set down together in free space, in no region.

name: build_canvas

description: Stop work listed by list_running_ai_work: pass its work_ids, or all: true to stop everything it marks spends_money. The job_id generate_explainer_video returned is accepted as it is. A tool call aborts the model request in flight and starts nothing further; what it already saved stays, so generate_course_quizzes keeps the quizzes written so far and calling it again writes only the rest. An explainer video is discarded, though scenes already filmed were billed; a mnemonic reading keeps the questions of the sources already written, the rest waiting in it as pending; text-to-speech audio keeps its finished chunks; a scheduled task's chat keeps the reply so far and the run is recorded as stopped; a released bulk re-queue puts the sources the drain has not reached back on hold in get_background_ai_jobs, where skip drops them; a model step is stopped for every source, its requests aborted: one that runs on its own stays stopped on every Mac of the account until resume_ai_work or the learner's Resume, though what the learner asks for themselves still runs, while one the learner asked for runs again when asked; automatic audio stops mid-source and stays stopped the same way. Work running on another device is not reached. Returns what was stopped and what had already finished.

all.description: Stop everything list_running_ai_work marks spends_money. Defaults to false.

name: cancel_ai_work

description: Stop text-to-speech audio generation queued or running through generate_source_audio, for specific source_ids or everything with all: true. Chunks that already finished stay cached, so generating those sources again later does not pay for them twice.

all.description: Stop every queued and generating source. Defaults to false.

source_ids.description: Sources to stop.

name: cancel_source_audio_generation

description: Delete an article's reading view, so the Reader shows the original page and the list of hidden pieces is gone. Make a new one with make_article_reading_view.
name: clear_article_reading_view

description: Take the lens off the learner's Canvas, so their own arrangement shows again. Nothing the lens showed is kept; the learner's Keep is the only way a lens becomes their canvas.
name: clear_map_lens

description: Remove the sources assigned to a day of the Schedule. With goal_id only that Goal's or Notebook's sources on the day are untagged; without it every source on the day leaves the Schedule.

date.description: Day to clear in YYYY-MM-DD format from get_schedule days

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID: only its sources on the day. Omit for every source on the day.

include_completed.description: Whether completed items should also be removed. Defaults to false, matching the app clear-day behavior.

name: clear_schedule_day

description: Clear cached source text and embeddings without archiving or deleting the source.
name: clear_source_derived_data

description: Today's cohort review: everything the learner substantially read or listened to in the last ~10 days, plus older sources due again, plus one or two semantically adjacent sources deliberately drawn from a different stretch of time so you can ask a question that spans them. Each entry carries its role (spine / spacing / bridge), a compressed guide to what the source says, the learner's own highlights, and what they have previously made of it. YOU are the planner: choose 5-8 moves, ask one question at a time, compose fresh wording every time, and make at least one question span two sources from different times. Finish by calling record_understanding. When the app has already planned today's review by topic, `topics` lists them (topic_id, title, kind, idea_ids, source_ids): conduct those in order, one opening question per topic answerable from any of its sources, instead of planning your own moves.

goal_id.description: Optional Notebook/Goal ID to scope the cohort to that pool. Omit to draw from everything consumed.

start_session.description: Defaults to true: starts a linked review session. Pass false for a read-only briefing of what today would cover.

name: cohort_review

description: Comment on a Doc as its Comments panel does, signed Assistant (never as the learner). With doc_id and quote, start a thread on those words of the page: quote them exactly as they read, a phrase or a sentence or two (at most 1,000 characters); the page marks the first place they occur, and a thread whose words are not in the page says Original text unavailable. With reply_to (a comment_id from list_doc_comments), reply in that comment's thread instead; doc_id and quote are then not needed. A team's page is refused: the learner comments there in the app. Use it when the learner asks for comments on a page, or to answer a thread they started.

doc_id.description: Doc ID from list_docs, for a new thread.

quote.description: The exact words of the page the new thread is about.

reply_to.description: Optional comment_id from list_doc_comments: reply in that comment's thread instead of starting one.

name: comment_on_doc

description: Make an OpenRouter key for one member of a family team and hand it to their Mac. Opens OpenRouter's sign-in in the browser on this Mac; the learner finishes it there and this call waits for it (up to five minutes). The key is sealed to the member's device, so only their Mac can open it, and it bills this account's OpenRouter account. The member must have joined the family plan first (get_family_plan).

member.description: The member's user_record_name or unique display name.

name: connect_family_member_key

description: Add an event to the Mac's Calendar — how a day is planned: each block of work, reading, review, admin or a break is an event on the learner's clock, titled in the learner's words. It lands on the calendar new events go to (new_events_calendar in get_calendar_events; the learner chooses it in Plugins › Calendar) unless calendar_id names another that takes events, shows at once in the Calendar app and in ForeverLM's Now chip, and reaches the learner's phone through their calendar account. Pass date and start, and end or duration_minutes (an event past midnight takes duration_minutes); all_day true makes an all-day event on date. Blocks of work are best 90–120 minutes and never under 30. Put what the hour is for in notes — the next step, and the foreverlm:// link of a source or Doc it reads — so it opens from the event. A block on one topic may also carry its notebook's [Title](foreverlm://notebook/<id>) link in its notes, so ForeverLM's Now chip opens that notebook from the block and a bout started there is filed under it. Plan into the free stretches get_calendar_events gives, and never over a meeting with other people: the calendar itself allows overlapping events, so read the day first. Returns the event with its event_id.

all_day.description: true makes an all-day event on date.

calendar_id.description: Optional calendar id or title from get_calendar_settings; defaults to the calendar new events go to.

duration_minutes.description: Length in minutes, instead of end; the way to plan past midnight.

end.description: 24-hour clock time, HH:MM, after start on the same day.

notes.description: Optional detail: the next step, a foreverlm:// link to the source or Doc the hour is for.

start.description: 24-hour clock time, HH:MM. Required unless all_day.

title.description: What the hour is for, in the learner's words.

url.description: Optional link the event opens, e.g. a call link or a foreverlm:// source link.

name: create_calendar_event

description: Make a new canvas in the learner's Space, on their word ("start a canvas for the PINK1 work"): named as they say, filed in one of their spaces when they name one (space_id from list_spaces), and opened on the Mac unless open is false, so the Canvas tools then act on it. Pass notebook_id (list_notebooks) to make it a canvas of that notebook: it is listed in the notebook's menu, and any note written on it by build_canvas is linked to the notebook; with frame_notebook true the notebook's sources are drawn on it in a frame, ready to arrange. It starts empty otherwise: nothing is placed on it until the learner places it, or asks you to (build_canvas lays out a whole picture in one call). Returns the canvas.

frame_notebook.description: With notebook_id: draw the notebook's sources on the canvas in a frame. Defaults to false. Needs the canvas open.

name.description: The canvas's name. Defaults to Untitled canvas.

notebook_id.description: Optional notebook ID from list_notebooks: the canvas belongs to this notebook.

open.description: Open it on the Mac, where the Canvas tools act on it. Defaults to true.

space_id.description: Optional space ID from list_spaces to file the canvas in.

name: create_canvas

description: Draw a region on the learner's Canvas: around item_ids (cards all on the Canvas keep their places and the region is drawn around them; otherwise they are set down together inside it), or empty in free space in the middle of what the learner is looking at. With notebook_id it is that notebook's frame: named by the notebook, drawing the notebook's ticked sources and Docs that are not placed anywhere, and folding into the notebook and its takeaways when zoomed out; a notebook whose frame is on the Canvas already is not framed twice (the answer names that frame). Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Opens the Canvas beside the chat and flies to the region. Returns its region_id.

color.description: The region's tint as #RRGGBB. The Canvas's own: #7F77DD, #1D9E75, #D85A30, #D4537E, #BA7517, #378ADD, #639922, #888780. Omit for the next one.

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> (a Doc, site, animation, audio overview or reading), idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id> (a shortcut to another canvas), chat:<session_id> (a chat) or picture:<image_id> (an image from list_images). A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

locked.description: Lock the region: its cards cannot be dragged, nor it moved or resized by hand, until it is unlocked (update_canvas_region). Defaults to false.

name.description: The region's name. Required unless notebook_id is given; a notebook's frame takes the notebook's name.

notebook_id.description: Make the region this Notebook's frame (a Notebook id from list_notebooks).

name: create_canvas_region

description: Create a new empty course with a stable ID. Call list_courses first; this tool refuses a duplicate normalized display title. Pass notebook_id to make a Notebook follow it: the sources its lectures gain join that Notebook. The course itself lives in no Notebook.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks that follows the new course. Omit it and no Notebook follows it.

title.description: Course display title.

name: create_course

description: Create a numbered lecture inside an existing course. Call list_courses first and pass its stable course_id. A unique exact display title is accepted for backward compatibility; ambiguous titles fail instead of creating or choosing a duplicate. Exactly one of course_id or course_name is required. Number auto-assigns to the next available unless given.

course_id.description: Stable course ID from list_courses (preferred). Required unless course_name is given.

course_name.description: Backward-compatible unique exact course display title. Used only when course_id is omitted.

title.description: Lecture title (optional)

name: create_course_lecture

description: Create one globally addressable Markdown Doc. Only for a document the learner asked for or that has no existing home: material meant for a Doc that already exists — integrate this, fold that in, update the report — belongs in that Doc through edit_doc (or write_doc for a short one), never in a new companion Doc. A home Notebook is organizational only; notebook_ids controls every Notebook that uses the same canonical document. Markdown may link to another Doc as [Title](foreverlm://doc/<doc_id>) and to a notebook as [Title](foreverlm://notebook/<notebook_id>); ForeverLM opens those in place. Write each reference to the web — a paper, an article, a page — as its own line or list item holding one link, optionally followed by a short detail after a dash: `- [Title](https://doi.org/10.1038/…) — Nature, 2024`. ForeverLM draws such a line as a source card, marks it with a check when the source is already in the Doc's library (by URL, DOI or arXiv id — a team Doc's cards ask the team library, a Doc in My Library asks My Library) and offers Add to Sources when it is not. A link inside a sentence stays a plain link in the prose and gets the same card in the margin beside its paragraph, so citing a source where a claim is made is as good as listing it. So cite as a link, never as text: `([Sgarbi et al., 2006](https://doi.org/10.1042/BJ20051748))`, not `(Sgarbi et al., Biochem J, 2006, doi:10.1042/BJ20051748)` — a DOI or PMID typed into the sentence earns no card and leaves the journal, year and identifier in the prose, where the card would have carried them.

is_draft.description: Whether the new Doc starts as a draft. Defaults to false (Production).

markdown.description: Initial complete Markdown content. Defaults to empty.

notebook_ids.description: Notebooks to link. The home Notebook is added automatically.

title.description: Doc title.

name: create_doc

description: Jot an Idea down for the learner — a thought with no deadline and no commitment, which is the whole point of it. Keep the title in the learner's own words; do not polish it into a goal statement. Put anything longer than a sentence in notes. If the learner names a date or asks for a plan, they want a Goal instead: use create_learning_goal, then link_idea with kind "goal" so the Idea records what it became. Check list_ideas first so a thought already written is extended with update_idea rather than doubled.

links.description: Optional: what the Idea already draws on, linked as it is created.

kind.description: One of: source, artifact, chat, goal, notebook.

target_id.description: The id of the record to link. Refused when this library holds no such record.

notes.description: Optional: the rest of the thought, when there is more than the line.

title.description: The thought, in the learner's words. One line; it is collapsed to one and capped at 300 characters.

name: create_idea

description: Create a timebound Goal — a deadline-bound objective, either learning-shaped ('learn about GDF15 this week') or outcome-shaped ('write an article about mitochondrial transplantation'). For an outcome Goal, make the title the deliverable. A Goal stands on its own; notebook_id is optional and only tags it to an existing source pool, so never invent a Notebook to hold a Goal the learner just voiced. With discover=true ForeverLM finds related sources already in the library by topic similarity and adds them as pending suggestions for approval; approve them with review_suggested_sources, then pace them across the days with assign_sources_to_day. Multiple Goals can run at once. IMPORTANT — end_date is required, but do not invent one silently. If the user hasn't named a date, help them choose: consider how much material the topic implies and how much work the deliverable needs, propose a specific date with your reasoning ('that's maybe 10 papers at 3/day, plus a few days to draft — I'd suggest the 29th'), and confirm before calling this.

artifact_id.description: Optional id of the Doc, Site or animation this Goal is for — the deliverable itself, e.g. the site behind 'Make a site of the rare mitochondrial diseases' (from list_docs, list_animations or a save_site result). The Goals tab opens it from the row. Refused when no record has the id.

discover.description: Auto-discover related sources by topic each day. Defaults to true.

end_date.description: Required end date, YYYY-MM-DD. The plan paces the pool to finish by this date.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook to tag the Goal to, so it draws on that Notebook's sources. Omit it — the common case — for a Goal that stands on its own.

source_ids.description: Optional seed source IDs to anchor discovery and the plan.

start_date.description: Optional start date, YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out to start today.

title.description: Natural-language goal, e.g. 'Understand GDF15'.

topic.description: Topic used to discover related sources. Defaults to the title.

name: create_learning_goal

description: Create a new Notebook (an open-ended research effort over a source pool). Seed it with source_ids; set discover=true to auto-suggest related sources by topic. A deadline belongs on a timebound Goal created with create_learning_goal and optionally tagged to this Notebook. Check list_notebooks first and reuse an existing Notebook when one fits; creating with a title that matches an existing Notebook fails unless allow_duplicate=true. Omit title, as the app's New notebook does, and the Notebook is "New notebook" until ForeverLM names it, title and card description, from its sources and its first chat; a title or summary given here or with update_notebook is never renamed.

allow_duplicate.description: Pass true to create a second Notebook with an existing title. Defaults to false, which rejects collisions.

daily_target.description: Items per daily quiz. Defaults to 3.

discover.description: Auto-discover related sources by topic. Defaults to false.

instructions.description: The learner's standing instructions for this Notebook — guidance to follow in every chat that works in it (the app's Instructions field). Guidance for the model, not display copy.

repository.description: The GitHub repository this Notebook is about, as owner/repo (owner/repo.git and github.com URLs are accepted). Only the name is stored; chats read the repository live through the GitHub tools (read_github_file, search_github_code, list_github_issues, …) and nothing from it enters the library.

research_questions.description: The Notebook's defining research questions, in priority order — what the Notebook exists to answer (distinct from emergent open questions).

source_ids.description: Source IDs to seed the Notebook (added as approved).

summary.description: A short description shown under the title on the Notebook's card (the app's Description field): one line of display copy for the learner, not guidance for the model.

title.description: Notebook title. Omit it to let ForeverLM name the Notebook from its sources and chats.

topic.description: Natural-language topic for discovery. Defaults to the title.

name: create_notebook

description: Add a task to a Notebook's board. In a team Notebook the task is the team's and can be assigned to a member by user_record_name (or "me"); every member sees it. In a personal Notebook it is the learner's own and takes no assignee. Refused when the Notebook's team is read-only for this account.

assignee_record_name.description: Team Notebooks only: a member's user_record_name from list_teams or list_notebook_tasks, or "me" for this account.

doc_id.description: Optional Doc the task is about.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

source_id.description: Optional source the task is about.

title.description: What is to be done.

name: create_notebook_task

description: Create an open question on a Notebook: a research gap the learner is chasing, with no deadline. It is NOT a Goal and never appears in the Goals tab. When the learner says "goal" in any form ("set up a goal", "add this to my goals", "my goal is to understand X"), use create_learning_goal instead — and if they named no deadline, propose one and confirm it rather than filing the goal here as a question. Questions also accumulate automatically from end_review_session after reviews.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

source_id.description: Optional source ID from this Notebook's pool to link the question

summary.description: The question or thread the learner is pursuing

name: create_open_question

description: Create a recurring scheduled task. The instruction is ordinary chat text; when the task comes due, ForeverLM sends it in a new chat with the same tools you have, and the learner reads the result there. Times are wall-clock in the task's time zone.

cadence.description: How often it runs. Defaults to daily.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Required for the once cadence; otherwise the first eligible day.

day_of_month.description: Monthly cadence only: 1-31, clamped to each month's length.

enabled.description: Whether the task starts active. Defaults to true.

instruction.description: The message to send when the task runs, e.g. "Quiz me on what I read yesterday".

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook the produced chats are filed under.

source_ids.description: Optional sources attached to every run.

time_zone.description: IANA identifier the wall-clock time is anchored to, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam. Defaults to this Mac's zone.

title.description: Short name shown in the Tasks list.

weekday.description: Weekly cadence only: 1 = Sunday through 7 = Saturday.

name: create_scheduled_task

description: Highlight a passage or a picture in a source and optionally write a note on it, exactly as pressing Highlight in ForeverLM's reader would. Quote the passage verbatim from get_source_content: the passage is located in the stored text and the mark is anchored to the source's own wording, so it paints in the reader and syncs to the learner's other devices. A passage that is not found, or that is already marked, is refused rather than guessed at. To mark a figure or image of a web page instead, pass image_url (the picture's URL as the page serves it) with no quote; the reader outlines that picture. To attach research to the passage it updates — what has been published since a textbook or paper was written — save the research conversation with import_review_chat (mark_reviewed false), then mark the passage (a section heading works) in blue with the short version as publication_update (never as note, which is the learner's), each paper it names in references, and the chat's id as session_id: the reader shows the update under a Since publication heading, and opens that chat, and each paper, from the mark.

color.description: Marker color: yellow, green, blue, pink, or purple. Defaults to yellow.

image_alt.description: The picture's alt text, if the page gives one; it names the mark in the notes list.

image_url.description: The absolute http(s) URL of a picture in the page to mark, as the page serves it. Pass it without a quote to mark the picture alone, or with one to mark both.

note.description: Optional note about the passage or picture: the learner's own thinking, or what they ask you to note. Research goes in publication_update. Omit for a bare highlight.

publication_update.description: Optional: what has been learned since the source was written. First line a one-sentence headline of what changed; then, on the next line, two to four plain-text sentences naming each paper as (Author et al., Journal Year), the way its references entry's citation reads. No markdown or links.

quote.description: The passage to mark, copied verbatim from the source text returned by get_source_content. Omit when marking a picture by image_url.

references.description: Optional: the papers or pages the update (or note) cites, in the order it names them, at most 20. The reader lists them on the mark with Add to Library, or Open when the library holds one.

citation.description: How the note names it, such as "Vozza et al., PNAS 2014".

title.description: The paper's title, if known.

url.description: The paper's or page's address, for one without a DOI.

session_id.description: Optional: the chat this note came from, by the id import_review_chat or get_review_sessions gives (a foreverlm://chat/<id> link works too). The reader opens it from the mark. From a chat inside ForeverLM, leave it out: the mark links to that chat.

name: create_source_highlight

description: Make a list in the learner's Space on their word ("make a list of my goals for the thesis"): kind goals or ideas, named as they say, filed in one of their spaces when they name one (space_id from list_spaces), and holding item_ids when given, each moved out of any list it was in. To put a new goal or idea in it, make the goal (create_learning_goal) or the idea (create_idea) first, then pass its id here or to update_space_list. Returns the list.

item_ids.description: Goal IDs from list_goals for a goals list, or Idea IDs from list_ideas for an ideas list.

name.description: The list's name. Defaults to Goals or Ideas.

space_id.description: Optional space ID from list_spaces to file the list in.

name: create_space_list

description: Create a team this account owns: a shared library in this account's iCloud. Returns the team. Members are invited from ForeverLM through Apple's sharing sheet, not through MCP; content is put into the team with share_with_team. Check list_teams first and reuse a team that already fits.

name.description: The team's name, shown to every member and on the invitation.

name: create_team

description: Publish a post on X (Twitter) as the connected ForeverLM user, optionally as a reply to another post. This posts publicly and immediately — always show the user the exact text and get their explicit confirmation before calling. Requires the X plugin to be signed in with posting permission (Plugins → X); read-only sessions from before posting support must reconnect once. Returns the new post's id and URL.

reply_to_post_id.description: Optional id of an existing post to reply to (the numeric id from its URL).

text.description: The post text, exactly as it should appear. Standard accounts are limited to 280 characters; the X API rejects anything longer.

name: create_x_post

description: Get today's adaptive daily quiz for a Learning Companion goal and start a linked review session. Returns a blend of new and review sources (paced to the goal's end date, self-adjusting for missed days), source content, a summary of prior sessions, open gaps, and any pending source suggestions to approve. With no goal_id, returns a menu of active goals. Conduct the quiz one deep question at a time, then call end_review_session with the session_id, score, and any gaps you observed.

date.description: Optional date in YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out for today.

goal_id.description: Companion goal ID from list_learning_goals. Omit to get a menu of all active goals.

start_session.description: Defaults to true: starts a linked session and loads source content. Pass false for a read-only briefing — no session, no items marked served, no full content.

name: daily_quiz

description: Get today's chat-first daily review plan for a Learning Companion goal — merges open gaps, spaced-repetition due sources, deadline-paced new/review blend, and in-progress reading into one Review Chat session. Does not write to Schedule. With no goal_id, returns a menu of active goals. Pass start_session=false for a read-only briefing (plan + rationale, no session); default starts a linked review session with source content for a live chat review, then call end_review_session when done.

goal_id.description: Companion goal ID from list_learning_goals. Omit to get a menu of all active goals.

start_session.description: Defaults to true: starts a linked review session and loads source content. Pass false for a read-only morning briefing.

name: daily_review

description: Answer one held bulk re-queue from get_background_ai_jobs, exactly as the sidebar's buttons do. decision run_all releases every held source to the queue's drain; run_affected releases only the sources the change affects and takes the rest out of the queue (refused when the job's affected count is null); skip takes them all out, and each keeps the text it has. run_all and run_affected spend money — read the estimate and ask the learner first. Returns how many sources were released and how many were dropped, and for a run the work_id cancel_ai_work stops it by: the sources the drain has not reached then wait here for a decision again.
name: decide_background_ai_job

description: Adopt, dismiss or retire a study practice, on the learner's word. Adopting one that carries a setting_change applies it as that setting's own tool does (new cards a day through set_memory_review_settings) and records when (setting_applied). The decision follows the learner to their other devices, and a later proposal of the same practice never undoes it.
name: decide_practice

description: Close an open request without sharing anything; every member sees it closed. Any editor of the team may. Requires the learner's Mac to be open and connected.
name: decline_share_request

description: Remove an animation saved with save_animation from the library, with its files. Confirm with the learner first; this cannot be undone except by saving the files again. Refused for a Site — delete_doc removes those.

animation.description: The animation's animation_id from save_animation or list_animations.

name: delete_animation

description: Delete an Atlas for good. It is ForeverLM's own writing and can be made again with make_atlas; cards the learner drafted from it stay.
name: delete_atlas

description: Remove an event from the Mac's Calendar that the learner owns alone (editable in get_calendar_events). For one occurrence of a recurring event pass occurrence_date; span future removes it and every occurrence after it. Not undoable from here: delete only an event the learner asked you to remove or one you added for them in this conversation, and confirm first otherwise. An event with other people on it is refused; the learner declines or cancels it in the Calendar app.

occurrence_date.description: For one occurrence of a recurring event: its occurrence_date from get_calendar_events.

span.description: For a recurring event: this occurrence (the default) or this and every later one.

name: delete_calendar_event

description: Delete a canvas forever, on the learner's explicit word: what is placed on it, its regions and its arrows go, on every device, with its place in a space and its pin. Only a canvas already in Trash can be deleted (update_canvas with in_trash true first), as in the Space. The sources, Docs and Ideas that were on it are untouched. This cannot be undone.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID from list_canvases, of a canvas in Trash.

name: delete_canvas

description: Delete an arrow from the learner's Canvas, named by its edge_id (get_knowledge_map lists it under arrows) or by the cards at its ends (from and to). The cards stay. Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back.

from.description: Instead of edge_id: where the arrow starts, a card by item_id or a region as region:<region_id>.

to.description: Instead of edge_id: where the arrow points to, a card by item_id or a region as region:<region_id>.

name: delete_canvas_arrow

description: Delete a region from the learner's Canvas. Its cards stay where they are unless take_cards_off is true, which takes them off the Canvas too and deletes the regions inside it, in the same edit; a notebook's frame going takes nothing out of the notebook. Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back.

region.description: A region's name (as get_knowledge_map lists it; a notebook's frame by its notebook's name) or its region_id.

take_cards_off.description: Take the cards inside it off the Canvas and delete the regions inside it as well. Defaults to false.

name: delete_canvas_region

description: Delete a course collection while preserving its sources as ungrouped library items. This removes the course's metadata, lectures, and material relationships. Requires the exact stable course_id from list_courses and cannot be undone — confirm with the user first.

course_id.description: Exact stable course ID from list_courses.

name: delete_course

description: Remove one quiz from a course by its quiz_id. The learner's latest score for it is kept. generate_course_quizzes writes a ForeverLM quiz again when asked.
name: delete_course_quiz

description: Take one span off a day's log — the Activity pane's Delete on a sitting. The log is what ForeverLM saw the learner do (reading, a chat, a Doc); the span goes for good, and the sources stay. A sitting the Activity pane draws may be several spans; delete each. Not undoable; confirm with the learner first. activity_id comes from get_day_activity.
name: delete_day_activity

description: Permanently forget one research direction — the app's Delete on it. A later search may propose it again; to keep it from coming back, set it aside with update_direction instead. Confirm with the learner first.
name: delete_direction

description: Move a Doc to the Trash — the Docs pane's Move to Trash. The Doc's Markdown body and its Notebook links go with it and every linked Notebook stops seeing it; sources and chats are untouched. For a linked page (kind google_doc, claude_artifact or codex_site) this only removes the entry from Docs or Sites; the page itself is never touched. This cannot be undone through MCP, so call list_docs or read_doc first and confirm the title with the learner before deleting.
name: delete_doc

description: Delete a comment on a Doc, as the Comments panel's Delete comment does: its replies remain, and when it was the comment that opened its thread, the first reply opens the thread from then on with the same passage. whole_thread true deletes the thread the comment is in and every message in it (Delete thread). Cannot be undone. A team's page is refused. Confirm with the learner first unless the comment is the assistant's own.

whole_thread.description: Delete the comment's whole thread instead of the one comment. Defaults to false.

name: delete_doc_comment

description: Permanently forget one Idea — the app's Delete on a row of the Ideas tab. Its links go with it; every source, Doc, chat and Goal they pointed at stays in the library. Not undoable: to put an Idea away and keep it, use update_idea with status "archived" instead. Confirm with the learner first.
name: delete_idea

description: Move a kept image to the Trash: every version, or only the version named. Confirm with the learner first. A chat or Doc that showed it then says the picture is not on this Mac.

image.description: The image: its image_id from list_images, the id of any of its versions, or its foreverlm://image/generated/<id> address or Markdown line.

version.description: Optional. Only this version number; the image keeps its others. Omit to remove the whole image.

name: delete_image

description: Permanently delete one timebound Goal — the app's Delete on a row of the Goals tab. The Goal's record, its source pool and its Schedule tags go; the sources stay in the library, and a chat started from the Goal stays in Chats with the link cleared. Refused for a Notebook (delete_notebook takes those, with their Goals). Not undoable; to put a Goal away and keep it, use update_learning_goal with status archived instead. Confirm with the learner first.
name: delete_learning_goal

description: Delete a meeting series for good — the app's Delete Series. Every session in the folder, archived ones included, and their artifacts are deleted with it; the Drive folder and the recordings behind it are not touched. This cannot be undone: call get_meeting_group first and confirm the title and session count with the learner before deleting.
name: delete_meeting_group

description: Permanently delete a Notebook: its source pool membership, planning state, open questions, and notes. Any Goals nested in the Notebook are deleted with it, and the Notebook's workspace files are moved to the Trash. Sources stay in the library. Ask separately whether chats filed in the Notebook should also be deleted; delete_chats defaults to false, which keeps them as ungrouped chats. This cannot be undone — call get_notebook first and confirm the Notebook's name and its Goal count with the user before deleting. notebook_id is required; there is no active-Notebook default.

delete_chats.description: Delete chats filed in this Notebook too. Defaults to false, which keeps them in the ungrouped Chats list.

notebook_id.description: ID of the Notebook to delete. Use list_notebooks to find it.

name: delete_notebook

description: Delete a task from its Notebook's board. In a team Notebook every member loses it. Not undoable; confirm the title with the learner first.
name: delete_notebook_task

description: Delete a review session (or saved external session link) by ID.
name: delete_review_session

description: Delete a scheduled task. Chats it already produced are kept.
name: delete_scheduled_task

description: Permanently delete one of the learner's skills. Chats that already used it keep what they were told. Not undoable; confirm with the learner first.
name: delete_skill

description: Permanently delete a source from the knowledge base by ID. For the Studio row's normal Remove behavior, use remove_source instead.
name: delete_source

description: Remove a highlight and its note from a source. The learner made these marks by hand while reading, so only delete one when they ask for it by name.

highlight_id.description: Highlight ID from list_source_highlights or search_source_highlights.

name: delete_source_highlight

description: Delete a list from the learner's Space forever, on their explicit word: the list, its place in a space and its pin go, on every device. The goals and ideas it held are not deleted; they stay in Goals and Ideas, in no list. Only a list already in Trash can be deleted (update_space_list with in_trash true first), as in the Space. This cannot be undone.

list_id.description: List ID from list_space_lists, of a list in Trash.

name: delete_space_list

description: Delete a team this account owns — Settings › Data & Privacy › Teams › Delete Team. The team's iCloud zone is deleted, so the team and every copy in it disappear for every member at once; everyone's originals stay in their own My Library. This cannot be undone. Only the owner can delete; a member is refused and pointed at leave_team. Always ask the learner first, naming the team and saying that it goes for every member. If the team's library is open in ForeverLM, the Studio goes back to My Library.

team_id.description: The team's id from list_teams. Must be a team whose role is owner.

name: delete_team

description: Remove a paper's, a book chapter's, an article's, a video's or a saved animation's walkthrough; the subject is untouched. Pass source_id or animation. Confirm with the learner first — a walkthrough an assistant authored cannot be brought back except by saving it again.

animation.description: Instead of source_id: a saved animation (its animation_id from list_animations). The walkthrough is then of the animation, played by the chat beside it, each step pinning the animation to one of its own steps.

source_id.description: The paper, book chapter or article (from list_sources or a search), or a foreverlm://source/<id> link. Pass this or animation.

name: delete_walkthrough

description: Do exactly what a plugin pane's Disconnect / Turn Off / Remove Access button does. x: signs out of X (bookmark sync stops). youtube: forgets the YouTube grant (automatic import stops; followed channels and imported videos stay). google_drive: disconnects one Google account (account_id from get_plugin_connections; optional when only one is connected); its meeting folders stop importing, meetings already imported stay. apple_calendar: turns the Mac's Calendar off for ForeverLM (the macOS permission itself stays; the learner revokes that in System Settings) and forgets the calendar choice; the events stay in the calendar. slack: revokes one workspace's Slack tokens (account_id is its team_id; optional when only one). github: revokes ForeverLM's GitHub token (the GitHub App stays installed on the organisations). user_plugin: removes a Build Your Own plugin's access at once (account_id is its id or name); the sources it added stay — remove_connector_sources removes those. Google accounts, Slack, GitHub and user plugins follow the learner's account on every device; X, YouTube and Calendar are this Mac's. Reconnecting needs the provider's consent page again, so ALWAYS ask the learner before disconnecting anything.

account_id.description: google_drive: the account id (or email); slack: the workspace team_id (or name); user_plugin: the plugin id (or name). Optional when only one is connected.

name: disconnect_plugin

description: Find sources a Notebook is missing with one web search on the chat's model, using the Notebook's title, instructions, research questions and sources as context. Returns a one-sentence summary and up to count candidates, each with one line on why it fits. ForeverLM keeps an address only when the search engine cited it, Crossref knows its DOI, or the page opens (left_out counts the rest), sets aside addresses that are never sources, such as a home or search page, a Google Doc or a playlist (not_sources counts them), and reads each candidate's kind off its address. For papers, search_literature searches PubMed for free. Each candidate says whether the library already holds it (in_library, library_source_id) and whether the Notebook does (in_notebook). Nothing is imported: show the learner the list and import only the ones they pick, with import_paper_from_url for a paper (it needs its PDF; one behind a paywall lands as PDF needed) and add_sources for the rest, then add_notebook_sources with the returned ids; a candidate in_library needs only add_notebook_sources. Refused before anything is spent when the chat's model cannot search the web. An assistant that can search the web itself may do that instead and import the same way. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

query.description: What to look for. Omit to search for the Notebook's own subject, its title.

source_ids.description: Sources the search treats as the Notebook's, by ID. Defaults to the Notebook's own ticked sources.

name: discover_sources

description: Bulk-download missing PDFs for paper sources that need one — the MCP equivalent of Studio's 'Try Papers Needing Attention'.
