Selects papers with no local PDF, an http(s) landing URL, and no paywall marker, resolves the PDF (direct, then open-access fallback), extracts text and metadata, and marks the source ready. Paywall-shaped failures are marked paywalled so they stop being retried; transient failures are left unchanged and reported with source IDs, never faked. Call again to continue past `limit`. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

limit.description: Max papers to process this call (default 25, max 100).

source_ids.description: Optional: restrict to these paper source IDs. If omitted, all papers needing attention are eligible.

name: download_papers_needing_attention

description: Draft Memory cards from sources in ForeverLM, as Make Cards in the Reader or a Notebook's Studio does, for the learner to go through in Memory's To Check: the learner keeps, edits or skips each card there (or a source's at once with Keep All), and only a kept card is ever reviewed. Name the sources with source_ids, as list_sources or a search returns them (an id the library does not hold refuses the whole call), or pass notebook_id alone for the Notebook's own ticked sources (list_notebook_sources in_chat, without via_context_notebook_id); with both, notebook_id is the Notebook the cards are made in, whose decided cards guide the drafting and whose To Check lists them. count is auto (the default: about 4 a source, at most 40) or how many cards in all, from 1 to 40, shared across the sources; focus says what the cards should serve. Each source's whole text is read; one too long for the drafting model's context window is read as evenly spaced excerpts and named under sampled. Questions a walkthrough of the source already asks become cards with no model call; the learner's Card Drafting model drafts the rest, starting from the source's review-guide questions, the learner's highlights and notes, and its ideas, and never drafts again a seed or a question the source's cards already hold, kept or skipped. Every card stands on a passage its source prints, checked word for word: a card whose passage is not found is reported, never offered. The first call prices the drafting and starts nothing unless it is free: show the learner the estimate, and once they agree call again with the same arguments and confirm_cost true. Once started it answers with work_id while the cards are drafted in the background; list_running_ai_work shows its progress, cancel_ai_work stops it (the sources already drafted keep their cards), and list_cards lists the cards to check, with what each run drafted under drafting. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true only after the learner has seen this tool's estimate and explicitly agreed to the spend. Defaults to false, which prices the drafting and starts nothing unless it is free.

count.description: auto (the default: about 4 cards a source, at most 40), or how many cards in all, from 1 to 40, such as "10".

focus.description: Optional: what the cards should serve, in the learner's words.

notebook_id.description: The Notebook the cards are made in (list_notebooks): its ticked sources when source_ids is omitted, and its decided cards guide the drafting.

source_ids.description: The sources to draft cards from, at most 100, as list_sources or a search returns them. Omit with notebook_id for the Notebook's ticked sources.

name: draft_cards

description: Draw an arrow between two cards on the learner's Canvas, with a short label for how one leads to the other (supports, contradicts, explains, causes, measures, extends, example of, or the learner's own words). Both cards must be on the Canvas (place_on_canvas first); an arrow already drawn between them gets the label and what else is given. An end may be a region instead of a card (region:<region_id>, or region:<name>): an arrow to a region survives its cards leaving and goes with the region; a card is not joined to the region that holds it, nor a region to one around or inside it. Give the arrow a look: route (curve, the default; straight; or elbow), dashed, heads (end, the default; both; or none), color (#RRGGBB) and a stance (supports draws it green, contradicts red, unless it has a color of its own). With tree true it is a mind-map branch, parent to child, drawn as a branch and not an arrow: a branch joins two cards, a card has one parent, and a tree has no loop (update_canvas_region with layout tree lays a region of such cards out as a mind map). Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Returns the arrow's edge_id.

from.description: Where the arrow starts: a card by item_id, or a region as region:<region_id>.

heads.description: Where the arrowheads are: at the end (the default), at both ends or nowhere.

label.description: A few words on the arrow. Optional.

route.description: How the arrow runs: a gentle curve (the default), a straight line or an elbow.

stance.description: Which side of an argument the arrow is on: supports (drawn green) or contradicts (red).

to.description: Where the arrow points to: a card by item_id, or a region as region:<region_id>.

tree.description: Make it a mind-map branch from the parent (from) to the child (to).

name: draw_canvas_arrow

description: Change parts of a Doc in place without re-emitting it: each edit names the exact existing text to find and the text to put there, applied in order and all-or-nothing, and append adds Markdown at the end. This is the way to integrate, fold in, update, correct or extend an existing Doc of any length — a 200,000-character report is edited in one call that carries only the passages that change. Every find must occur exactly once (pass replace_all to change every occurrence; give more surrounding text to disambiguate); an edit that matches nowhere or in several places changes nothing and says which. Quote find text exactly as read_doc returned it, whitespace and Markdown markers included. Requires the revision from read_doc. The learner may be typing in the Doc meanwhile: when it changed after that read, the edits are applied to its newer text as long as every find still matches exactly once, and the result says doc_changed_meanwhile; an edit whose own passage changed is refused and nothing is saved. Refused for a linked page (the refusal says how to refresh ForeverLM's copy with link_page, make it an editable Doc with unlink_page, or make it ForeverLM's own published page with adopt_page). Every linked Notebook sees the same edit. A published Doc's page is not re-rendered unless publish is true: without it the result says the page is stale and publish_doc updates it; with it a Doc that already has a page gets the page updated in the same call.

append.description: Optional Markdown appended at the end of the Doc, after the edits, on a new line.

edits.description: Targeted replacements, applied in order. May be empty when only append is used.

find.description: Exact existing text to replace. Must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true.

replace.description: Text to put in its place. An empty string deletes the found text.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of find instead of requiring a single match. Defaults to false.

expected_revision.description: Exact revision returned by read_doc. A newer revision does not refuse the edit by itself; the find texts are checked against the newer body.

publish.description: When the Doc has a published page, update it with the edited body in the same call (same address, same readers). Ignored for a Doc that is not published. Defaults to false.

name: edit_doc

description: Stop the clock on a running bout without writing it up yet. The write-up is still owed and no break is earned until it is filed. Use this when the learner says they have stopped but is not ready to reflect; otherwise go straight to write_up_learning_bout, which stops the clock itself.
name: end_learning_bout

description: End a review session only after the learner explicitly asks to stop or confirms they want to finish; covering the planned concepts or reaching a question count is not permission to end. Records the score and summary and saves the review with its transcript. Pass the session_id from start_review_session or daily_quiz (the "Session ID:" line). If that id is lost, call this anyway with transcript and source_ids — the review is then saved as a completed imported review, never discarded. For daily_quiz sessions, pass any gaps you observed so they carry into future quizzes; source study state updates automatically.

gaps.description: Optional gaps in understanding observed during the quiz. Each carries forward until resolved.

source_id.description: Optional source most related to the gap.

summary.description: Short description of the gap, e.g. 'Confuses TRPV4 gating with Ca2+ influx mechanism'.

memory_attempts.description: Structured evidence from memory_review. For an existing memory_item pass item_id and omit first-review fields. For a new_item omit item_id and pass source_id, semantic_target, rubric, and an exact evidence_excerpt from that source. Omit this array for ordinary reviews and host-bound in-app chats, which record attempts turn by turn.

evidence_excerpt.description: First-review mode only: a non-empty exact excerpt (20 to 2000 characters) from the canonical source text grounding this target.

item_id.description: Existing-review mode only: exact item_id returned in memory_review.memory_items. Omit for a first review.

missing_rubric_elements.description: Rubric elements still missing; use an empty array when none are missing.

prompt.description: The question actually asked: a card's `ask` wording as written, otherwise the fresh question you composed.

retrieval_quality.description: How much retrieval support the learner used; ForeverLM maps this to scheduling deterministically.

rubric.description: First-review mode only: 1 to 12 compact criteria that distinguish a strong answer. Do not include a fixed question or answer script.

semantic_target.description: First-review mode only: one stable, source-grounded idea the learner should be able to explain or apply. Keep this target across future varied questions.

source_id.description: First-review mode only: exact source_id returned in memory_review.new_items. It must belong to this review session.

session_id.description: Session ID from start_review_session or daily_quiz. May be empty if lost.

source_ids.description: Source IDs reviewed. Links and marks them reviewed; required when session_id is empty.

summary.description: Short summary of what was covered and how the learner did.

topic.description: Optional saved title; used only when session_id is empty.

transcript.description: Full Markdown transcript of the review chat. Always send it; required when session_id is empty.

name: end_review_session

description: Run AI title/author extraction for an article source. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

name: extract_article_metadata

description: Run AI metadata extraction (author, journal, year, DOI) for an existing paper source. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

name: extract_paper_metadata

description: Capture a library video's slide frames so they can be shown and read, without reading them for cited papers. This is the opt-in first step: slides are no longer captured at ingest (it downloads storyboards and streams the video for frames, so it takes noticeably longer on a long talk), so a YouTube video with a transcript has none until this runs. Idempotent — a video that already has frames just reports how many. Makes no model calls. Follow with scan_video_for_cited_papers to read the captured slides for the papers they cite.
name: extract_video_slides

description: Fetch article text from archive.ph for a paywalled or errored web source and store it as source content.
name: fetch_source_from_archive

description: Fetch and store the transcript for a YouTube video source, a one-off Zoom cloud-recording link (zoom.us/rec/play or /rec/share), or a Teachable lecture. YouTube: also extracts representative slide screenshots from storyboards when available. Zoom: prefers the recording's own transcript/captions and falls back to managed OpenAI transcription; passcode-protected recordings fail with a passcode request — ask the user for the passcode and retry with the passcode argument. An accepted Zoom passcode is saved securely in Keychain and reused for that source. Teachable: the lecture's audio is downloaded and transcribed in the background, a few minutes per lecture; the call returns at once and a later call (or get_source_content) returns the transcript — the learner must be signed in to the school inside ForeverLM. Errors are surfaced directly when a transcript is unavailable. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

passcode.description: Passcode for a protected Zoom recording (only needed when a previous call reported one is required)

name: fetch_video_transcript

description: List EVERY source whose metadata matches — the exhaustive answer to "all Huberman Lab episodes", "every paper by Martin Picard", or "everything with Picard in the title, byline or show". Filters are case-insensitive substrings over metadata (title, author, show or channel, journal), combined with AND; nothing is ranked or cut off by similarity. Returns each source's id, type, show or author, year, word count and the local date and time it was added, newest first. It is also the answer to "the latest", "the newest" or "the last" source of a kind: "look at my latest YouTube video" is source_type video with a small limit, and the first line is the one most recently added (add show for "the last Huberman episode"). A ranked search orders by similarity, never by recency, so it cannot answer that. Use this whenever the learner names a show, channel, author or person and wants the complete set; then read the titles, or pass the show to search_sources_semantic or search_sources_keyword to find what those episodes say about a topic. It reads metadata only, not a source's text.

author.description: Text the author or byline contains: a paper's authors, an article's author, a meeting's presenter.

limit.description: Maximum sources to return (default 200, maximum 1000). The answer says when more matched.

show.description: Podcast show or YouTube channel name, from list_shows; part of the name also works ("Huberman").

text.description: Text any of title, author, show or channel, journal, or book/course/playlist contains — use it for a person who may be a guest in an episode title or an author of a paper ("Martin Picard").

name: filter_sources

description: Find the other sources of the learner's library that also state what a card asks, so the card can stand on every source that prints it. A card is about an idea, and an idea is often printed in several sources (a talk and the paper behind it, two lectures on one mechanism); a card that stands on several sources shows each in To Check and in review. Pass card_id (a card to check or a kept card, from list_cards), or a question and an answer you are about to save with save_card_drafts. Returns the passages of other sources nearest the card, up to 4, each with source_id, source_title and passage: they are retrieved, not judged, so read each and keep only those that state the card's answer in substance, not merely its topic, then name them in also_from (source_id and a quote copied word for word from its passage) in save_card_drafts, or in triage_cards when the learner keeps the card. source_ids or notebook_id narrow the search to those sources or to one Notebook's; sources the card already stands on, and sources kept from AI, are never listed. Reads only; free apart from the embedding of the card's words.

card_id.description: A card_id from list_cards (status to_check or kept).

notebook_id.description: Look only among this Notebook's sources (list_notebooks).

question.description: With answer, instead of card_id: the question of a card you are about to save.

source_ids.description: Look only among these sources, as list_sources or a search returns them.

name: find_card_sources

description: Start a search for research directions toward one of the learner's Goals, Notebooks or Ideas — what they could pursue next, not a summary of the field ("find interesting methods to target rare mitochondrial diseases", "what could I do with this idea?"). Returns the brief: the home and its standing instructions, the sources it holds and related ones in the library, the learner's Ideas and chats, every direction already proposed toward it with the learner's answer and reason, their recent answers elsewhere, and the steps to follow. Makes no model call and spends nothing: you do the searching (search_literature, web search, the library tools) and save what survives with propose_directions. If the learner's aim is not yet a Goal, Notebook or Idea, create it first — create_idea when it has no date, create_learning_goal when it has one — and pass its id.

focus.description: Optional: what kind of directions the learner asked for, in their words ("methods to target", "companies to talk to", "cheap experiments").

home_id.description: The Goal (list_goals), Notebook (list_notebooks) or Idea (list_ideas) the directions are toward.

name: find_directions

description: Detect duplicate papers across the library with AI. Reports duplicate groups; if archive_duplicates is true, archives the lower-quality copy in each group and keeps the best.

archive_duplicates.description: If true, archive the lower-quality duplicates (default false = report only).

name: find_duplicate_papers

description: Find the papers cited by every active video, notes file, syllabus, slide deck, and other readable material attached to one course lecture, and record each as a candidate without importing or attaching anything. The tool scans complete video decks, lecture transcripts, and all bounded chunks of stored text; verifies model-returned URLs and DOIs against the literal material; resolves citations against the scholarly catalogs; and returns one candidate per paper with its cited_paper_id, status (pending: can be imported; imported: already in the library; unresolved: no record matched; dismissed), the materials it was found in, and whether it is already attached to the lecture. Show the learner the candidates and pass the ones they choose to ingest_lecture_papers. Existing video scan decisions are reused by default; pass force true to re-extract and rescan each video's slides and transcript while merging without overwriting prior decisions. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

force.description: Re-extract and rescan lecture videos, merging new citations while preserving existing imported/dismissed decisions. Text materials are read on every invocation. Defaults to false.

name: find_lecture_papers

description: Search Apple Podcasts for an episode matching a source (by YouTube URL or title) and stage the match for confirmation.
name: find_podcast_match

description: Find the YouTube upload of a podcast episode whose transcript Apple Podcasts does not give: the Reader's Find on YouTube. ForeverLM reads the episode's own web page for the video it links, the show's YouTube channel (known from earlier episodes whose transcript came from YouTube) for uploads near the episode's release, and YouTube search, then ranks what it found with the learner's model, best match first; each candidate says where it was found (found_by). Nothing is attached. An upload is often titled differently from the episode, so show the learner the best match and, once they confirm it is this episode, call import_podcast_youtube_transcript with its url. always_for_show ticks the Reader's "Always find <show> on YouTube" for the episode's show, so its later episodes with no Apple transcript go straight to YouTube; false unticks it. Needs YouTube connected in Plugins › YouTube. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

always_for_show.description: Optional. true ticks "Always find <show> on YouTube" for the episode's show, false unticks it; omit to leave it as it is.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

name: find_podcast_on_youtube

description: Fly the learner's Canvas to cards or a region and ring them for a moment, or select them, so what you are talking about is on screen. Moves the view only, never a card. Opens the Canvas beside the chat if it is not showing.

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> (a Doc, site, animation, audio overview or reading), idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id> (a shortcut to another canvas), chat:<session_id> (a chat) or picture:<image_id> (an image from list_images). A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

region.description: A region's name (as get_knowledge_map lists it) or its region_id.

select.description: Select the cards, showing them in the Canvas side panel, instead of only ringing them. Defaults to false.

name: focus_map

description: Plugins › YouTube › Followed channels › Follow: resolve a channel from its address or @handle, import its newest 50 uploads into a Videos group named after it, and keep importing every new upload in the background (this turns YouTube's automatic import on). Needs YouTube connected. The group follows the learner's library on every device. For a channel's older back catalog, add its playlist as a course instead. Returns the group_id (unfollow_youtube_channel takes it) and how many videos the group now holds.

channel.description: The channel's address (youtube.com/@handle, youtube.com/channel/UC…) or its @handle.

name: follow_youtube_channel

description: Follow the signed-in user's YouTube playlist named "ForeverLM" and import all of its videos. The playlist may be public, unlisted, or private. Metadata only; transcripts fetch on demand. Requires connecting YouTube in Plugins → YouTube.
name: follow_youtube_foreverlm_playlist

description: Follow the signed-in user's YouTube "Liked videos" and keep them fresh in the background. Choose whether to import existing likes or only likes added from now on. Automatic AI transcript formatting is off unless explicitly enabled because a large history can run up a substantial bill on the learner's OpenRouter key. Requires connecting YouTube in Plugins → YouTube.

format_transcripts_automatically.description: true to opt into paid AI formatting for automatically fetched liked-video transcripts. Defaults to false; raw transcripts remain available.

import_existing.description: true to import existing and future likes; false for future likes only. Defaults to true.

name: follow_youtube_liked_videos

description: Take back activity ForeverLM recorded on sources that did not happen — a review marked by a chat that reviewed nothing, say. For each source it removes the automatic Schedule entry (the one ForeverLM made to hold activity no one planned) with every activity day under it and the read stamp when that day set it, and reopens any assignment the entry's completion closed; every device follows. Refused, with nothing changed, for a source placed on the Schedule by plan (unschedule_sources or set_source_completion are for those) and for one whose entry also holds activity on another day, which this would erase too. Not undoable; confirm with the learner first. get_today_sources with date_basis activity lists what a day recorded.

date.description: The day the activity was recorded, YYYY-MM-DD. Every activity day of each source must be this one.

source_ids.description: Sources whose recorded activity did not happen.

name: forget_source_activity

description: Forget one working note: ForeverLM stops handing it to its chats, on every Mac signed in to the account. Not undoable; do it when the learner asks to forget it. Pass the whole note_id from list_working_notes, or the first eight characters or more of it.
name: forget_working_note

description: Answer an open request with this Mac's own copy: the source in My Library is shared into the team, file included, and the request records the team copy that answered it. Refused when My Library does not hold the source, when the request is already closed, or when the learner can only read the team. Answering gives the team's members a copy of the source, so the learner affirms once, in ForeverLM or through share_notebook, share_with_team or here, that they may share their sources; until they have, this is refused with the question to ask: "Do you have the rights to share these sources with the people you invite, in line with copyright and each source's terms?" Pass rights_affirmed_by_learner: true only after asking the learner exactly that and hearing yes; their answer is recorded and not asked again. Requires the learner's Mac to be open and connected.

rights_affirmed_by_learner.description: true only after the learner, asked whether they have the rights to share these sources with the people they invite, in line with copyright and each source's terms, said yes. Needed while the learner has not yet affirmed; ignored once they have.

name: fulfil_share_request

description: Make a Notebook's audio overview in ForeverLM, as its Studio does: one spoken script written over the Notebook's sources by the learner's Audio Overview Writing model and, by default, narrated by their text-to-speech voice. Formats: deep_dive (a thorough tour of what the sources say together, where they agree and conflict, and what stays open; shorter about 7, default about 12, longer about 19 minutes), brief (the core ideas in about 2 minutes; length does not apply) and critique (a constructive expert review of the sources' strengths, weaknesses, methods and gaps; about 5, 8 or 13 minutes). focus leads the script. The sources are the Notebook's own ticked sources (list_notebook_sources in_chat, without a context notebook's rows, via_context_notebook_id; set_notebook_source_selection) unless source_ids names some of its own sources; sources with no text yet are left out and listed. Every source is read whole when the model's context window takes them together; otherwise the longest are read from the ideas stored for them, or from a condensed account of their whole text written for this overview, and the answer says which — nothing is cut. The overview is saved as an Artifact in the Notebook (list_docs kind audio_overview) with its spoken script as a source (audio_source_id), which plays on every device. The first call prices the writing and the audio and starts nothing when the voice costs money: show the learner the estimate, and once they agree call again with confirm_cost true. With automatic audio switched on for explainers (get_automatic_audio_settings, kind explainer), that standing opt-in covers the audio and the overview starts at once. Once started it answers with work_id, overview_id and audio_source_id while the writing runs in the background; list_running_ai_work shows its stage, cancel_ai_work stops it and nothing is saved, get_source_audio_status with the audio_source_id follows the writing and then the audio, cancel_source_audio_generation stops the audio, read_doc returns the recipe and get_source_content the script. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key for the writing and the narration. A team's Notebook cannot hold one yet. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true only after the learner has seen this tool's estimate and explicitly agreed to the spend. Defaults to false, which prices a paid voice and starts nothing, unless automatic audio is switched on for explainers.

focus.description: Optional: what the overview should be about, in the learner's words. It leads the script.

generate_audio.description: Narrate the script once it is written. Defaults to true.

length.description: shorter, default or longer. Ignored for brief.

notebook_id.description: The Notebook the overview is written from and filed in (list_notebooks).

source_ids.description: Write from these of the Notebook's own sources, in this order. Omit for its own ticked sources (in_chat, not via_context_notebook_id).

name: generate_audio_overview

description: Plan and write a course on a topic from the learner's own library, optionally researching the live web and importing what it cites. Searches the library for the topic, plans a curriculum of modules over the sources found, writes a lesson and an exercise sheet per module as course sources, and saves it all as one course. Pass notebook_id to make that Notebook follow the course: it gains its sources and the modules it gains. The course itself lives in no Notebook. With schedule_start, a Goal in that Notebook, due the day after the last module, places one module every days_per_module days; with schedule_start and no notebook_id, an open-ended Notebook named after the course is created first, to follow the course and hold the Goal. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key on every run and takes minutes; tell the learner what it will do before calling it, and never call it twice for the same request. When the course was planned with the learner first, pass the sources they settled on as source_ids and the agreed outline as plan, and leave use_web off unless they want more research. Returns the course_id, lecture ids, and the lesson and exercise source ids; an explainer video for a module is made afterwards with generate_explainer_video and that module's lecture_id. While it runs, list_running_ai_work shows it and cancel_ai_work stops it. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

days_per_module.description: Days between module study days when scheduling (default 2).

learner_notes.description: Optional: what the learner already knows or wants from the course.

module_count.description: Optional preferred number of modules, 2–12. Omit to size the course to the material.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks (of My Library) that follows the course. Checked before anything is paid for; an archived Notebook, or a team's, is refused.

plan.description: Optional: the plan agreed with the learner, in plain words — the modules in order, what each covers and which chosen sources it reads, what to stress or leave out. The planner keeps it and fills in only what it leaves open.

quizzes.description: Also write the course's quizzes once its lessons are written, as generate_course_quizzes does: a practice quiz after each module, checkpoints, and a course test (default false; one more model call per quiz).

schedule_start.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD. When set, a Goal in the course's Notebook is created and modules are placed on days from this date toward it; without notebook_id, a Notebook named after the course is created first. The answer carries notebook_id and goal_id.

source_ids.description: Optional: library source ids the learner settled on for this course — found by search or imported while planning it. The planner places every one of them; the library search still adds what they miss. Import a web paper or video first (import_paper_from_url, add_source) and pass the id it returns.

topic.description: The subject of the course, e.g. "mitochondrial transplantation".

use_web.description: Research the topic on the live web and import cited pages as sources (default false).

name: generate_course

description: Write a course's quizzes ahead of time, the way a Khan Academy unit alternates lessons and practice: a practice quiz after every lecture (about that lecture), a checkpoint quiz where a topic ends, about every few lectures (across them, some questions connecting lectures; the parts of a lecture series such as "Ion Transport 1" to "4" stay under one checkpoint), and a course test at the end. For each quiz the writer first lists every key point and fact worth remembering in the lecture videos, from the whole transcript, then asks at least one question about each, so a long lecture gets many questions; a point the list names that no question tests gets one more call for exactly those points. A lecture's readings are quizzed too: the textbook pages add_textbook_to_course planned for it, and any source filed under it with role reading. A practice quiz writes each reading's questions in a call of its own after the lecture's, and a checkpoint or the test reads the readings beside their lectures. Questions are open recall, never multiple choice, each tied to the lecture source or reading and the stretch it rests on (with its page, for a reading). Written from each lecture's stored transcript or text; lectures without one are listed so you can fetch_video_transcript them first. Every quiz is saved as it is written and shows in the course's Lectures list; by default only missing quizzes are written, so calling again resumes. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key: one model call per quiz, one more per reading of a practice quiz's lecture, and one more wherever the first call left a learning point without a question; takes a few minutes for a long course; tell the learner before calling. Image generation is off by default for an assistant's bulk run. With draw_pictures true, each newly written quiz also gets its picture and its writer may ask for up to 12 separately billed drawings for questions no slide or figure shows. That paid route is refused until the learner has seen the returned maximum image-request count, selected model and published maximum cost and explicitly agrees; then repeat it with confirm_drawings true and approved_spend_usd. Captured lecture slides and reading figures remain available without generated drawings. Returns the ladder with each quiz's quiz_id and status. While it runs, list_running_ai_work shows it and cancel_ai_work stops it; the quizzes already written stay. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

checkpoint_every.description: About how many lectures a checkpoint quiz covers, 2–12 (default 4). Checkpoints fall where a lecture series ends, so one can cover a few more or fewer. A course this short or shorter gets no checkpoints.

confirm_drawings.description: With draw_pictures true, pass true only after the learner has seen this tool's refusal with the maximum image-request count, selected model and published maximum cost and explicitly agreed. Pass that approval as approved_spend_usd too. Defaults false.

draw_pictures.description: Draw a picture for each newly written quiz that has none, and the separately billed pictures its writer asks for questions no slide or figure shows (default false for assistant bulk runs).

final_test.description: Write the course test at the end (default true).

quiz_ids.description: Optional: only these quizzes of the ladder, by the quiz_id get_course shows; with rewrite, rewrites just those.

rewrite.description: Rewrite quizzes that already exist instead of keeping them (default false). A rewrite of the whole ladder also moves the checkpoints to where the ladder puts them now: a checkpoint written before its groups moved is removed once the new checkpoints cover its lectures. Without it, no checkpoint is written over lectures such an old one already covers.

name: generate_course_quizzes

description: Write a spoken explainer of a paper or article in ForeverLM and, by default, narrate it. Reads the source's full text and writes a plain-language script for the ear with the learner's Explainer Writing model — brief (about four minutes), standard (about seven) or extended (about twelve) — and saves it as a text source titled 'Explainer: <title>' that is listed under the original rather than on its own; the explainer is an ordinary source, so it can be opened, searched, reviewed and listened to on every device, and it is deleted with the source it explains. Then, unless generate_audio is false, starts text-to-speech audio for it exactly as generate_source_audio does: a free voice starts at once; when the voice costs money the audio part of the result is awaiting_confirmation with an estimate and nothing has been narrated yet — the script is already saved — so show the learner the estimate and, once they agree, call generate_source_audio with the explainer's source id and confirm_cost: true (or call this tool again with confirm_cost: true, which rewrites the script). With automatic audio switched on for explainers (get_automatic_audio_settings / set_automatic_audio_settings, kind explainer), that standing opt-in is the consent: the audio starts with the selected voice and no quote, and the audio result says cost_confirmed_by automatic_explainer_audio. A second call for the same source replaces its explainer. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key for the writing call. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true only after the learner has seen the audio estimate and explicitly agreed to the spend. Defaults to false, which quotes a paid voice and starts nothing — unless automatic audio is switched on for explainers (get_automatic_audio_settings), in which case that standing opt-in is the consent and the audio starts without a quote.

generate_audio.description: Start text-to-speech audio for the explainer once it is written. Defaults to true.

length.description: How long the spoken explainer runs: brief is about four minutes, standard (the default) about seven, extended about twelve.

source_id.description: The paper or article to explain (from list_sources or a search).

name: generate_explainer

description: Make a short explainer video of one concept on this Mac: the Explainer Writing model storyboards it in eight-second scenes, the learner's video model (Settings › AI Models › Videos) films each scene with its narration, and the film is kept under Videos as a video source. Pass lecture_id to add the finished video to that course module as its video — the way a generated course gets a film for a module (lecture ids come from generate_course or get_course). A video costs dollars, so ForeverLM itself asks the learner the exact price in a dialog on the Mac before anything is filmed, every time; still tell the learner in chat which video you are starting and why before calling, and call it once per video they agreed to. The call returns as soon as the learner answers: started with a job_id while the film is made in the background (a few minutes; it appears in the module, or under Videos, when done), or declined, in which case nothing was made or billed. Mac only. cancel_ai_work with the returned work_id stops a film under way. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

concept.description: The one idea the film explains, in plain words — "why the electron transport chain pumps protons", not a module title.

lecture_id.description: Optional course module (lecture) to add the finished video to, as its video material.

length.description: brief (3 scenes, 24 s), standard (5 scenes, 40 s, the default) or extended (8 scenes, 64 s). The price scales with the scenes.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks: the finished video joins that Notebook's sources. A video of a source or a module already shows wherever that source or course does; use it above all for a video of a concept alone. Checked before the price is asked.

source_id.description: Optional paper or article whose text grounds the storyboard.

name: generate_explainer_video

description: Draw a picture with ForeverLM's image model (the learner's image model, images.model in get_app_settings) and keep it with its prompt, in the Notebook notebook_id names, whose Studio lists it; returns the picture and its ids. Each call is billed to the learner's own OpenRouter key, so call it only when the learner asks ForeverLM to draw it — a picture you or another tool can make yourself is kept with save_image instead, at no charge. Write prompt as a complete description of the picture: subject, composition, style, mood, and whether it contains any text, and give a new picture a short title. Pass revises to change a picture already kept: that version (the latest, when revises names the image) is sent to the model to edit, and the result becomes the image's next version — write prompt as the edit, what to change and what must stay. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

notebook_id.description: Optional. The Notebook (from list_notebooks) a new image lives in. The app lists a picture only in its Notebook's Studio, so pass the Notebook the learner is working in; an image kept in no Notebook is found only by list_images and wherever it is shown. A revision keeps its image's Notebook. Refused, before anything is made, for an archived Notebook or a team's the learner can only read.

prompt.description: Full description of the picture to draw; with revises, the edit — what to change and what must stay the same.

quality.description: medium (default); low for a quick draft, high only when asked for the best possible picture.

revises.description: Optional. When this picture is a change to one already kept — "make it bluer", a second attempt at the same idea — the image_id (or any version's id) of that image. The picture is then stored as its next version, and the image is listed once, at this version. Omit for a new image.

title.description: Required for a new image: two to six words naming it, as a file is named — "Forward vs reverse electron transport", not the prompt's opening. Its Notebook's Studio lists the image under it. With revises, omit it to keep the image's title.

name: generate_image

description: Make a mnemonic reading in ForeverLM, as the Mnemonic reading tile in a Notebook's Studio and Make Mnemonic Reading in the Reader do: the sources' own stored text read with recall questions set right after the passages they test, the way quantum.country's essays set them. A book's chapters in reading order, or any chapter, paper or article. The learner reads it in ForeverLM, answers each question in their head, shows the answer and grades it, and every answered question is kept as a Memory card that comes back in the card review. Name the sources with source_ids in reading order, as list_sources or a search returns them (an id the library does not hold refuses the whole call); or book, a book's book_id or title as list_sources shows it, for all its chapters in order; or notebook_id alone for the Notebook's ticked sources. With notebook_id the reading is filed in that Notebook. density is auto (the default: about one question for every 350 words of text, at most 24 a source), fewer or more. The learner's Mnemonic Reading Writing model writes one request a source; a source too long for its context window is read in consecutive parts, never sampled. Every question stands on a passage its source prints, checked word for word, and one that does not is dropped. The first call prices the writing and starts nothing unless it is free: show the learner the estimate, and once they agree call again with the same arguments and confirm_cost true. Once started it answers with reading_id and work_id while the questions are written in the background, a source at a time: the reading exists once its first source is written, and fills in. list_running_ai_work shows its progress and cancel_ai_work stops it; the sources already written keep their questions. Pass reading_id alone to write a reading's pending sources (a run that failed or was stopped before them). get_mnemonic_reading reads it. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

book.description: A book's book_id or title, as list_sources shows it: all its chapters, in order.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true only after the learner has seen this tool's estimate and explicitly agreed to the spend. Defaults to false, which prices the writing and starts nothing unless it is free.

density.description: How many questions: auto (the default, about one for every 350 words), fewer or more.

notebook_id.description: The Notebook the reading is made in (list_notebooks); its ticked sources when no sources are named.

reading_id.description: A reading whose pending sources are written; pass it without sources or notebook_id.

source_ids.description: The sources to read, in reading order, at most 200, as list_sources or a search returns them.

name: generate_mnemonic_reading

description: Write a Notebook's report in ForeverLM, as its Studio's Report does, and save it as a Doc in the Notebook. Formats: briefing (an executive summary, the key themes with their evidence, the important quotations, where the sources agree and conflict, and the open questions), study_guide (an overview, a ten-question short-answer quiz with its answer key, five essay questions and a glossary of key terms), meeting_questions (questions to bring to a meeting about the sources, grouped by theme, each with why it matters, and the three to ask first), document_feedback (constructive, specific feedback on one document, subject_id, judged against the Notebook's other sources) and custom (the report the learner's instruction describes). focus leads any format but custom. It is written by the learner's Report Writing model over the Notebook's own ticked sources (list_notebook_sources in_chat, without a context notebook's rows, via_context_notebook_id; set_notebook_source_selection) unless source_ids names some of its own sources; sources with no text yet are left out and listed. Every source is read whole when the model's context window takes them together; otherwise the longest are read from the ideas stored for them, or from a condensed account of their whole text written for this report, and the answer says which — nothing is cut. Each passage stands on the sources it cites, as the Doc's own citations, and the Doc closes with a card for each source and the recipe it was made from (read_doc returns it as report). The first call prices the writing and starts nothing unless the model is free: show the learner the estimate, and once they agree call again with the same arguments and confirm_cost true. Once started it answers with work_id and doc_id while the report is written in the background; list_running_ai_work shows its stage, cancel_ai_work stops it and nothing is saved, and read_doc with the doc_id returns the report once saved, or says why it was not. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true only after the learner has seen this tool's estimate and explicitly agreed to the spend. Defaults to false, which prices the writing and starts nothing unless the model is free.

focus.description: Optional: what the report should focus on, in the learner's words. It leads the report. Not used with custom, whose instruction says it all.

format.description: briefing (the default), study_guide, meeting_questions, document_feedback or custom.

instruction.description: Required for custom, and used only there: what the report should be, in the learner's words: its purpose, sections, tone or length.

notebook_id.description: The Notebook the report is written from and filed in (list_notebooks).

source_ids.description: Write from these of the Notebook's own sources, in this order. Omit for its own ticked sources (in_chat, not via_context_notebook_id).

subject_id.description: Required for document_feedback, and used only there: the document the feedback is about, one of the Notebook's sources (list_notebook_sources) or one of its Docs (list_docs with notebook_id). A source of the Notebook that is not ticked is read as well.

take.description: Optional (Think first): what the learner thinks matters most, in their own words, written before seeing the report. The report opens with it under "Your take", as written, and ends with "Where this differs from your take": what their take saw that the report does not, and the other way round, never a grade. Pass only the learner's words, never your own.

name: generate_report

description: Generate text-to-speech audio files for sources in ForeverLM — the sidebar's Generate Audio, for many sources at once. Select by source_ids, by book_ids (every chapter of a book, in reading order; ids from list_sources), and/or by source_types (e.g. ["book"] for every book in the library). Uses the voice the learner chose in ForeverLM Settings and the same metered route the app uses; sources that already have audio are skipped, never re-billed. Two-step when it costs money: the first call returns status awaiting_confirmation with an estimate (characters, listening time, price, model) and starts nothing — show the learner the estimate, and only after they explicitly agree call again with the same selection and confirm_cost: true. Free voices start immediately. Generation runs in the app a couple of sources at a time and continues while ForeverLM is open; follow it with get_source_audio_status and stop it with cancel_source_audio_generation. Podcasts, videos, and meetings have their own audio and are refused. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

allow_unsupported_languages.description: Generate a source even when no available voice speaks its language (it will be mispronounced). Defaults to false, which skips such sources and says why.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

book_ids.description: Books to narrate whole: the book_id values list_sources shows (a book's exact title is also accepted). Chapters are queued in reading order.

confirm_cost.description: Pass true only after the learner has seen the estimate from a previous call with the same selection and explicitly agreed to the spend. Defaults to false, which quotes and starts nothing when the run would cost money.

source_ids.description: Individual source ids to narrate, in the order to generate them.

source_types.description: Every ready source of these types that has no audio yet. ["book"] means every book in the library.

name: generate_source_audio

description: Write a guided walkthrough of a paper, a book chapter or an article with ForeverLM's Walkthrough Writing model and open it beside the source in the Reader, as a deck of cards the learner also flips through on the phone. Two writing passes: the argument first — three to seven claims in teaching order — then chapters that teach those claims, one chapter a claim, each ending on its claim as a recap card. Ten to thirty steps, one point each, dealt one beat a card — a figure step is about one panel, which the Reader scrolls to and outlines while the cards read it (axes, traces, what the data do, what it means); an explain step is the guide talking, anchored to a passage the Reader marks only when the point is in the source's own words. A panel is shown when it carries a claim, not because it is printed. Questions along the way, about one step in three, in four kinds — recall, think_first (before the evidence), predict (the panel's data are hidden until the learner guesses) and find (the learner picks the panel that answers) — all open and answered in the learner's own words or on the figure, graded against the writer's reference answer, never multiple choice; Say more chips for context a newcomer may want; and small code-drawn animations for the steps whose mechanism a still figure cannot show. The first step situates the source in its field — what was known before it, the problem or debate it enters, why the question matters beyond its own system — as a journal's editorial summary would, and the last says what changes for the field if the authors are right. It explains the way a good textbook does, simply and step by step, for a newcomer to the field unless the learner's About you (Settings › General › About you, account.about_you) says otherwise: the terms and parts the argument needs are taught in plain words before the steps that use them, an abstract claim starts from a concrete case, each card says how it follows from the one before, and the questions ask about the argument rather than its vocabulary. The writer reads the source's text and, for a paper or a chapter split from a PDF, its figure index; an article or an EPUB chapter is shown as text, so its steps are anchored to passages alone, which the Reader scrolls to and flashes. Every figure label and quoted passage is checked against the source before saving, and a step whose anchor fails keeps its words and loses only the scroll target (the result's warnings say which). Every point card carries a picture: a figure step's panel, a figure the writer names for an explain step, or a picture drawn with the account's image model from the writer's brief (each kept with its prompt, as a drawn picture is); a step without one shows the picture before it in its chapter. The steps are saved and shown before anything is drawn, then the pictures and the animations are drawn one call each, so the walk is usable at once. A second call replaces the source's walkthrough. Bills the learner's OpenRouter key for the two writing calls, each picture and each animation; pass animations: false to write the steps alone. A paper can be walked through once its PDF has been read, a chapter or an article once its text has. A book is walked through one chapter at a time: call this per chapter (list_sources with the book's group lists them). To author the steps yourself instead — when you have already read the source and, for a paper, its figures with inspect_paper_figure — call save_walkthrough. The result's subject says what was walked (paper, chapter, article) and figure_anchors whether its steps may point at figures. A YouTube video is not walked through here: write its steps with save_walkthrough, each at its moment of the talk. While it runs, cancel_ai_work stops it. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

animations.description: Draw the pictures and animations the writer briefed (at most ten pictures, four animations) through ForeverLM's separately billed media route. False saves the briefs undrawn so the connected assistant can make and save them with its own allowance. Defaults to false.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

source_id.description: The paper, book chapter or article (from list_sources or a search), or a foreverlm://source/<id> link.

name: generate_walkthrough

description: Read Settings › AI Models: the Default Model that chat and its companions follow, docs (the model Edit with AI in a Doc runs on; follows_default_model while Docs have none of their own), the text-only and multimodal Background models, every background task with the model it runs on and which it follows (background_text, background_multimodal, or task_model when the learner gave it a model of its own; a meeting task says kept_off_free_model while it runs on a paid model because its Background model is free, and waiting_for_paid_model when it has none to run on), meetings_may_use_free (Setup's Meetings answer), the catalogue every picker offers, grouped by maker with each model's price per million input, output, cached-input and cache-write tokens from the app's one pricing table, whether it can read images, its effort options, whether it is selectable, and qualification: for chat, background and background_images, whether the model passed a test run of that work (passed, failed with OpenRouter's words, or untested; a model is tested the first time it is picked for a role and applied only if it passes; one that failed stays in the catalogue and is tested again when picked, and set_ai_task_settings tests an untested or previously failed pick first and refuses one that fails), and free_models: OpenRouter's free models that can run text work and work that reads images and have not failed a test run of it, best first, with free_model_blocker saying why none can run when that is so. accepts lists exactly what set_ai_task_settings takes.
name: get_ai_task_settings

description: Read the AI usage ledger behind Settings › AI Usage › Activity for a period (days back, default 30, or from/to as local YYYY-MM-DD): total spend, spend by task with the models each task ran and per-call averages (tokens in and out, cache read share, cost per call), spend by model with its catalogue price, spend by day, and beside every configurable task the route it would run on now (provider, model, effort, speed, which default it follows or that it is overridden) with that model's price per million tokens. cost_usd is what the provider billed when it reported an amount, else the list-price estimate stamped at record time; calls that could not be priced are counted in unpriced_calls and never folded into a total, and a model whose price is unknown says price_known false rather than a guess. Reads no source content.

days.description: How many days back from now to report. Default 30. Not with from/to.

from.description: First local calendar day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD.

to.description: Last local calendar day of the period, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today when from is given.

name: get_ai_usage_report

description: Get what is open in the ForeverLM app: the Notebook each open window holds, frontmost window first and marked, with its title, notebook_id and source count (a window outside any Notebook says so), then the sources the frontmost window's Notebook reads. What a window holds is discoverable context, never an implicit MCP default. Call this only when the learner explicitly asks about the Notebook or sources open in ForeverLM; otherwise use list_sources or resolve an explicitly named Notebook with list_notebooks.
name: get_app_context

description: Read the ForeverLM Settings window as chat can change it: every switch, picker and slider in Appearance, Voice (speech-to-text models, text-to-speech voice and speed), Images, Videos, Sources › Reading Lists and Zoom Transcripts, and the Plugins place (Google Drive, YouTube), each with its id, current value, type, whether it follows the learner's account or stays on this Mac, and the options its picker offers. Also lists the panes that have tools of their own (dedicated_tools), the one-shot buttons run_settings_action performs (actions), and the few controls that stay in the window because they need the learner's own hand (only_in_the_settings_window). Pass pane to narrow by pane name, or setting for one entry.

pane.description: Optional: only settings whose pane contains this text, e.g. voice, images, youtube.

setting.description: Optional: one setting id, e.g. read_aloud.speed.

name: get_app_settings

description: Read an article's reading view: whether the learner has one, the instruction it was made from, whether the Reader currently shows it or the original, how many pieces of text it hides, and the first pieces as examples.
name: get_article_reading_view

description: Read an Atlas: with no concept_id, every concept (id, name, kind, gist, line, paragraph and steps when written, parent, terms, relations, status, open questions, and evidence by passage id) and the passages they cite with their source ids, titles and exact text from the learner's library; with concept_id, that concept in full with its passages, broader and narrower concepts. deepen true (with concept_id) first writes the concept in depth (a textbook paragraph, 3 to 7 steps, more terms and evidence from a fresh search of the library), which spends one model call and is saved with the Atlas; a concept already deepened is not written again. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

atlas_id.description: The Atlas, as make_atlas or list_atlases gives it.

deepen.description: Write the concept in depth before answering. Needs concept_id. Defaults to false.

name: get_atlas

description: Read the learner's automatic audio settings — set only from chat through set_automatic_audio_settings; the Settings window has no pane for them: for every kind automation covers — articles, papers, books, courses and explainers — whether text-to-speech audio is generated as soon as a source of that kind is ready (enabled), its optional natural-language rule (filter), and how many of that kind have no audio yet with the estimated characters and price; the selected voice with its rate; whether automation may run on that voice at all (a free OpenRouter voice always, a priced one only after allow_paid_voices, an unpriced voice or another provider never), the paid-voice consent and, for a priced voice, the quote consenting would start. Explainers are article-typed sources with a switch of their own: with it on, generate_explainer and the Mac's Explain button start an explainer's audio with the selected voice without asking about cost. The switches, rules and consent follow the learner's account to their other devices.
name: get_automatic_audio_settings

description: List the bulk re-queues waiting for the learner before they spend: when an update or a bulk change puts more than 50 sources into a paid background queue (source clean-up, Listen preparation, podcast ad clean-up), nothing in it runs until the learner decides, and the sources sidebar shows the same question. Each job has its id, the queue, the reason (what changed), how many sources it holds, how many of them the change affects (null when the change cannot say), and an estimate from the learner's own AI usage ledger — the average cost per source of that queue's task over the last 30 days times the count, or null with cost_known false when the ledger has no priced history. Also reports today's background AI spend against the daily cap (billing.background_daily_cap_usd in get_app_settings). Put the count and estimate to the learner before calling decide_background_ai_job.
name: get_background_ai_jobs

description: Read the ForeverLM account behind Settings › Billing (paying for ForeverLM) and Settings › AI Usage (the key and the monthly spending limit), freshly fetched from the account server as those panes do when they open. ForeverLM is a paid app after 7 free days: they begin at the first sign-in, and then the app is paid once (the Early user deal), with no subscription; an account that has not paid by then is locked until it does, and nothing in it is deleted. No monthly plan is sold; one bought before still counts as paid while it is active. AI is never part of the price: the learner's own OpenRouter API key pays for every model, billed by OpenRouter at cost, and ForeverLM adds nothing. OpenRouter is the only supported provider. Returns whether the learner is signed in; the plan (state free_days, paid_once, monthly, comped, family or locked; whether the account is unlocked, when the free days end, how many are left and how many an account gets; a monthly plan's renewal and price; whether the own key may run AI) and the plans on sale with the account server's prices (once, the Early user deal, recommended); a summary of the learner's own router key (details in get_own_router_key); any balance left over from before prepaid balance was retired, which still pays for requests sent without the key until it runs out and cannot be added to; and the monthly spending limit (current value, what has been spent this month, whether it is reached, when it resets, and the options the pane's picker offers, including no_limit). This is account state, the same on every device.
name: get_billing_settings

description: Read one block of the learner's Docs by its id: the nine lowercase letters and digits a block ends with as ` ^id` (hidden in the editor), which ((id)) references and {{embed: ((id))}} embeds from other Docs. Answers with the Doc that holds it (doc_id, doc_title, and day for a daily note), the block's own Markdown without its id, its plain text and kind (paragraph, heading, listItem or quote), its breadcrumbs (the bullets and heading it sits under, outermost first), the Markdown nested under it, and how many times it is referenced or embedded. Use it to read what a ((id)) says; read_doc with resolve_references reads a whole Doc with every reference replaced by its words, and get_linked_references with block_id lists where the block is referenced. Read-only.

block_id.description: A block's id: the nine lowercase letters and digits it ends with as ` ^id`, the id ((id)) names. ((id)) and ^id are read too.

team_id.description: Team ID from list_teams, for a source or a block in a team's library. Omit for My Library.

name: get_block

description: Read the learner's day from the Mac's Calendar — the day is the calendar, and there is no separate plan: every event on the calendars ForeverLM shows (Plugins › Calendar; get_calendar_settings), for one day or up to 14 from date. Each event has event_id (with occurrence_date for one occurrence of a recurring event — pass both to change it), title, calendar and calendar_id, start and end on the learner's clock (HH:MM) and start_at and end_at in ISO 8601 with the offset, all_day, when (ended, now with minutes_left, or ahead), location, join_link (the Teams, Zoom or Meet link, when there is one), notes, attendees, has_other_people (a meeting: it stays at its time and only the Calendar app may change it), and editable (whether update_calendar_event and delete_calendar_event may touch it). Each day also says its weekday, where it sits against today (relative_day), the hours the learner's day runs (day_starts, day_ends; get_day_settings), and the free stretches inside those hours — free_from_now on today, free on a day ahead — which is where a plan goes. new_events_calendar is where create_calendar_event puts an event unless told otherwise. Needs the Mac's Calendar on; the error says how to turn it on. To plan a day: read it (and get_day_activity for how recent days actually went), ask the learner the one thing only they can say — what is fixed and what the day is for — then add each block of the day as an event with create_calendar_event.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, "today" or "tomorrow". Defaults to today on the learner's Mac.

days.description: How many days from date to read, 1 to 14. Defaults to 1.

name: get_calendar_events

description: Read Plugins › Calendar — the Mac's Calendar app, which is the learner's day: whether it is on for ForeverLM, whether macOS granted access or refused it, every calendar the Mac holds (iCloud, Google, Exchange, subscriptions) with its id, title, account, whether it takes new events (writable) and whether it is shown (on_day: its events are what get_calendar_events reads and the Now chip shows), and new_events_calendar — the calendar create_calendar_event writes into unless told otherwise (the learner's choice, or the Calendar app's own default). selection_is_default true means the learner never narrowed the shown list, so every calendar but Birthdays is shown. The choice is this Mac's. Change with set_calendar_settings.
name: get_calendar_settings

description: Read how the learner's Memory cards stand behind the cards on their Canvas: for each card drawn on the Canvas (or the item_ids given), the kept cards anchored to its sources (a source its own, an Idea its evidence's, a Doc its citations') with cards, due (cards whose answer counts now: due, or kept and never answered), fading (overdue by more than two days), solid (scheduled ahead), dusty (mostly fading, or untouched for a month) and last_reviewed_at; the same for each region; the arrows the learner drew, by edge_id, for make_cards_from_canvas; and whether the Canvas's Memory layer shows and a review in place runs. Reads only.

item_ids.description: Cards on the Canvas by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: idea:<idea_id>, source:<source_id> or doc:<doc_id>. A bare id is tried as a source, then a Doc, then an Idea.

name: get_canvas_memory

description: Read Settings › Chat › Models as it stands: the models the chat picker offers (the ticked cards), each with its provider, model id, name, whether it is the Default Model, and whether the learner added it from the OpenRouter directory (user_added). This is the account's list and syncs across the learner's devices. The full catalogue, with prices, is in get_ai_task_settings (catalogue, enabled_for_chat); set_chat_model_offered changes the list.
name: get_chat_models_offered

description: Return this ingest plugin's private local staging directory for paper PDFs. Write a downloaded PDF there, then call import_connector_paper with its absolute file path. The directory is plugin-specific and is the only local path import_connector_paper will accept from an ingest-only client.
name: get_connector_inbox

description: Inspect one course's metadata, the Notebooks that follow it (followed_by; a course lives in no Notebook), lecture IDs, lecture-item IDs, attached sources, and unassigned course sources. Pass the stable course_id from list_courses; a unique exact display title is also accepted.

course_id.description: Stable course ID from list_courses (preferred), or a unique exact course display title.

name: get_course

description: Read one of a course's quizzes: its kind, the lectures it covers, where it sits in the course, the learner's latest score, and its questions with their ids, the lecture source each rests on, and the picture each is shown with, above the question or with its answer: a lecture's frame or a reading's page (show it with show_source_image as listed), an image in ForeverLM's store drawn for it or kept from another app (look at it with get_image), or a picture briefed and not drawn yet. Answers are left out unless include_answers is true, so you can quiz the learner one question at a time without showing them. Record each answer with record_course_quiz_result as it is graded.

include_answers.description: Include each question's reference answer and key points, for grading (default false).

quiz_id.description: Quiz ID from get_course or generate_course_quizzes.

name: get_course_quiz

description: Read the learner's daily note: Roam Research's page a day, kept in Docs. A daily note is an ordinary Markdown Doc in My Library whose id is daily-YYYY-MM-DD and whose title is the day written out ("October 6th, 2026"), so [[October 6th, 2026]] in any Doc links it, and read_doc, edit_doc and get_linked_references take its doc_id. Answers with its doc_id, title, Markdown and revision, or says the day has no note. Writes nothing unless create is true, which makes the day's empty note when there is none, as opening the day in ForeverLM does. To write in a day, use append_to_daily_note.

create.description: Make the day's empty note when there is none. Defaults to false: the call only reads.

date.description: The day, as YYYY-MM-DD ("2026-10-06"), or today, yesterday or tomorrow. Defaults to today where the learner's Mac is.

name: get_daily_note
