description: Read one day's log — what ForeverLM saw the learner actually do, span by span: a paper read in the Reader (reading, listening, watching, with source_id), a chat had (chat, with chat_id) or a Doc written (doc, with doc_id), each with activity_id, start, end, duration_minutes and a foreverlm:// link that opens it; on today a span still going is marked ongoing and runs to now. Also logged_minutes by kind, the day's learning bouts with their write-ups, and minutes_learned, with the day's weekday and relative_day. The log is observation, the Activity pane's; nothing here changes it but delete_day_activity. Read it beside get_calendar_events to see what a day planned for actually went to.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, "today" or "tomorrow". Defaults to today on the learner's Mac.

name: get_day_activity

description: Read Settings › General › Day: the hours the learner's day runs (day_start_hour, day_end_hour; 6 and 24 unless the learner set them) — what get_calendar_events counts free time inside and the hours the Activity pane's clock draws; this pair follows the account to the learner's other Macs — and whether this Mac asks "Plan your day?" (suggest_planning_the_day, device-local, on unless switched off: each morning today's calendar holds nothing the learner planned — meetings with other people and recurring events do not count — from the start of their day until the afternoon hour /plan turns to tomorrow, with suggest_planning_scope giving this Mac's hours, a card in the bottom-left of the Studio window asks and waits until answered, and a notification says it once if the learner sits down with ForeverLM not in front). notifications_status is whether macOS lets ForeverLM notify on this Mac at all (allowed, refused or not_asked), which a bout's alarms, the memory review reminder and "Plan your day?" as a notification need; refused means none of them reaches the learner while the switches still read as on, and only the learner can undo it, in System Settings › Notifications. notifications_note says what the status means.
name: get_day_settings

description: Today's card review in ForeverLM, for you to run here: the learner's kept cards to ask today, in the order the app's own card review asks them (the cards of a notebook with a block on today's calendar or a Goal ending within 36 hours first, then due cards most overdue first, then up to the day's new cards, new_cards_per_day), cut to the learner's daily minutes, across every Notebook or narrowed to one with notebook_id. Each card has item_id, card_id, ask (the wording to ask exactly as written: the card's question, the learner's own rewording, or, once it has been remembered twice, a rewording ForeverLM checked asks for the same answer), back, why, optional front_images/back_images, source_id, source_title, quote, sources (every source the card stands on, each with its quote), is_new, and say_first when it is asked in other words for the first time. Show front_images with the question; ask one card at a time and show nothing of its back, back_images, why or quote before the learner has answered it in their own words, typed or said: never a bare “show me”, never an answer you supply for them (an “I don't know” is an answer, and counts as forgot). Then show back_images beside the answer and record each answer with record_card_result and the sitting_id returned here. due_left_over and new_left_over count what the day's minutes leave for another day. Reads only: a card listed is not marked asked.

limit.description: Most cards listed (default and max 200).

notebook_id.description: Only this Notebook's cards (those on its sources), from list_notebooks.

name: get_due_cards

description: Family plans: for each team, whether this account's plan covers its members (family_plan), and for each member whether their Mac has joined and whether they have an OpenRouter key; and membership, when another account's plan covers this one. A covered member's AI runs on an OpenRouter key the owner connected for them, billed to the owner's OpenRouter account.
name: get_family_plan

description: Read one GitHub issue live and in full: title, body, state, author, assignees, labels, milestone, dates, URL, and every comment. Takes the issue number (the 42 in #42 or at the end of its URL). Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to GitHub; point the learner at the issue's url to act.

number.description: The issue number, from list_github_issues or the issue's URL.

name: get_github_issue

description: Read one GitHub pull request live and in full: title, body, state, author, reviewers, head and base branches, commit and change statistics, the files changed with their per-file additions and deletions, its comments and its review comments. Takes the pull request number. Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to GitHub; point the learner at the pull request's url to act.

number.description: The pull request number, from list_github_pull_requests or its URL.

name: get_github_pull_request

description: Read one GitHub repository live: description, default branch, language, visibility, topics, stars, open issue count, dates and URL, its README, and the entries at the top level. Start here before listing files or reading code. Read-only: ForeverLM reads GitHub as the learner through a read-only grant and never writes to it.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit to read at. Defaults to the default branch.

repository.description: owner/repo, or a github.com URL such as https://github.com/owner/repo.

name: get_github_repository

description: Return one timebound Goal in full: deadline, days remaining, whether it is overdue, lifecycle status, the Notebook it is tagged to if any, the Doc, Site or animation it is for (`artifact`, null when none), its approved and pending sources, and open questions. Use get_schedule with its goal_id alongside it to see which days the Goal's sources are scheduled on.
name: get_goal

description: Show one kept image: the picture itself, its title, the prompt it was made from, its model and date, and its versions (newest first, each with its id and prompt). Returns the latest version unless version names another. Use it to look at a picture before changing it, or to hand its prompt to another image model.

image.description: The image: its image_id from list_images, the id of any of its versions, or its foreverlm://image/generated/<id> address or Markdown line.

version.description: Optional. The version number to show (1 is the first); the latest by default. A later version's own id passed as image shows that version.

name: get_image

description: Read the learner's Canvas: a zoomable plane for what they think, holding the Ideas (questions, claims, hunches) and other cards they placed, the regions they drew around them and the arrows between them; a source not placed is not on the plane unless it is an Idea's evidence. Returns the regions they drew (by name, with region_id and rect, and collapsed when folded up, its cards then placed but not drawn) with the cards placed in each, the cards placed outside any region, each placed Idea's evidence (the sources and Docs linked to it), the arrows they drew between cards with their labels and edge_id, what is in view right now (the zoom level, the regions and up to 60 cards on screen), the cards they selected or circled, the lens showing if any, and how many cards are not placed yet, by notebook. Every card has an item_id (source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> for a Doc or anything else a notebook made, idea:<idea_id>, page:<source_id>:<n> for one page of a PDF source laid out on the Canvas, drawn from the PDF, canvas:<canvas_id> for a shortcut to another canvas, chat:<session_id> for a chat, or picture:<image_id> for an image of the Images library) to pass to apply_map_lens, focus_map and the tools that edit the Canvas on the learner's word (place_on_canvas and the rest); a source's id works with every source tool and a Doc's with read_doc. A placed card also gives its rect (x, y and the width and height it is drawn at) and what the learner gave it (w, h, folded, color); a source drawn as a page of its PDF says which (page) and how many the PDF has (pages), and a card says the learner's words about why it is on this canvas (annotation), an Idea drawn as plain words (plain), an Idea whose title is a question (question) and a question marked answered (answered); a region says when it is locked and when its layout is a tree (a mind map); an arrow says its route (curve, straight or elbow), dashed, heads (end, both or none), color, its stance (supports or contradicts) and whether it is a tree branch, and an arrow's end may be a region (region:<region_id>); what is left out is the default. Call it when the learner talks about the canvas, the area they are looking at, a region, or what they circled, before answering about it. The learner may have several canvases in their Space; this reads the one open on the Mac, named in canvas (list_canvases lists them, open_canvas opens another).

include_unplaced.description: Also list the cards not placed yet, by notebook, up to limit. Defaults to false: only their counts.

limit.description: Most cards listed in any one list (default 200, at most 1000).

name: get_knowledge_map

description: Read the learner's timer: the bout running now — a stretch of learning with a clock on it — and the day's finished ones with their write-ups. A bout is in one of five phases: learning (the clock is running, and it keeps running past its end until the learner stops it), writing (stopped, the write-up is owed), earned (written up, a break is waiting), resting (on that break), complete. Call this before any other bout tool.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD or "today". Defaults to today. The live bout is returned whatever day it started on.

name: get_learning_bout

description: Get every paper source associated with one course lecture, including source IDs, lecture-item IDs, bibliographic metadata, and availability state. Use get_source_content with a returned source_id to read a paper.
name: get_lecture_papers

description: Read one Linear issue live and in full: title, description, state, priority, assignee, labels, project, team, URL, dates, sub-issues, and every comment. Takes an identifier such as ENG-123 or an issue id. Linear tools are the only way into Linear: nothing from it is stored in the library. ForeverLM reads Linear as the learner through a read-only grant and cannot comment, assign, or change anything; point the learner at the issue's url to act.

issue.description: Issue identifier such as ENG-123, or the issue id, from a search hit or a list.

name: get_linear_issue

description: Read one Linear project live and in full: description and content, status, health, lead, teams, progress and dates, its issues summarised by state type and listed, its recent project updates, and its comments. Takes the project's id or slug_id (the token at the end of its URL). Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to Linear.

project.description: Project id or slug_id, from list_linear_projects or the project's URL.

name: get_linear_project

description: Read the Linked References of a page, an Idea, a source or one block in the learner's Docs: what points at it, as Roam Research lists it under a page. Pass exactly one of doc_id, idea_id, source_id or block_id. Answers with the pages that point there, newest edit first: each page's kind (doc, dailyNote or idea), id and title, and the blocks in it that point, each with its Markdown, plain text, block_id (null until something references the block), breadcrumbs (the bullets and heading it sits under, outermost first) and the Markdown nested under it. The Ideas linked to a Doc or a source come as idea pages without blocks. include_unlinked (doc_id only) adds the Unlinked References: blocks of other Docs that write the page's title without linking it. A team Doc's references are its team's Docs. The grammar a block points with: [Title](foreverlm://doc/<id>), [[Title]], #tag and #[[Two words]] name a page (a daily note's title is its day written out, "October 6th, 2026"); [Title](foreverlm://idea/<id>) an Idea; a foreverlm://source/<id> link or the source's web address cites a source; ((id)) references a block and {{embed: ((id))}} on a line of its own embeds it, where id is the nine lowercase letters and digits the block ends with as ` ^id`. Read-only.

block_id.description: A block's id: the nine lowercase letters and digits it ends with as ` ^id`, the id ((id)) names. ((id)) and ^id are read too.

doc_id.description: Doc ID from list_docs, or a daily note's doc_id from get_daily_note.

include_unlinked.description: With doc_id: also list the Unlinked References, each block with start and end, the UTF-16 offsets of the title's words in its markdown. Defaults to false.

limit.description: Most pages listed, and most unlinked references (default 50, at most 200).

source_id.description: Source ID from list_sources or a search.

team_id.description: Team ID from list_teams, for a source or a block in a team's library. Omit for My Library.

name: get_linked_references

description: Check whether the ForeverLM MCP server is active and ready to receive tool calls. Call this before other ForeverLM tools. From the Mac, icloud_account says which iCloud account its library syncs with (syncs_with_icloud, environment, and user_record_name, the account's container-scoped CloudKit user record name, the same kind of id list_teams gives for members, once CloudKit has answered); ForeverLM on the web uses it to ask only a Mac on the learner's own account. answered_by says which Mac answered, since another Mac signed in to the same account can hold the connection: app and build, device_id (that Mac's ForeverLM sync id), model, and computer_name, which is left out while its answers are narrowed. narrowed, when present, says that Mac lists only part of the library for now: when what the learner names is not listed, say you cannot see it from that Mac rather than choosing the closest match.
name: get_mcp_status

description: Get one recurring meeting group as JSON with session source IDs, artifact metadata, and its sidebar image. Pass group_id from list_meeting_groups.
name: get_meeting_group

description: Settings › General › Memory review as JSON: budget_minutes (the daily review's length, your account), new_cards_per_day (how many new cards a day's review introduces, which also sets how many sources ForeverLM drafts cards from in the background each day, your account), auto_draft_cards (whether ForeverLM drafts cards into To Check as the learner finishes sources, within the daily background AI limit, your account), draft_nudges (whether the Cards to check corner card and the next morning's banner say drafted cards wait, your account), prepare_review_questions (whether ForeverLM writes review questions ahead of time for the few sources a review is likely to be about today, your account), prepare_daily ("Have today's review ready": the reminder on mornings that hold cards, your account), ready_by_hour (when this Mac selects the morning's cards and the reminder fires), automatic_drafting (sources_a_day, this Mac's last_run with what it left waiting, and the sources that failed today), and what this Mac last did about the morning (last_preparation).
name: get_memory_review_settings

description: Read a mnemonic reading: its title, its Notebook, its sources in reading order (written, or pending while their questions are not written), and every question with its question_id, source_id, quote (the passage it is asked after), question, answer, why and difficulty, and where it stands for this learner: unanswered, kept as a Memory card (with its last grade, and due when the card review asks it now, else next_due_at), or retired. counts says how many questions there are, how many are answered and how many are due. While ForeverLM is writing it, writing says how far it has come; last_run says how the last run this session ended. To go through it in a chat, quote the passage and ask one question at a time, show nothing of its answer before the learner answers, and record each answer with answer_mnemonic_question. Reads only. list_docs lists readings as kind mnemonic_reading.

reading_id.description: The reading, from list_docs (kind mnemonic_reading) or generate_mnemonic_reading.

name: get_mnemonic_reading

description: Get an explicitly identified Notebook with its standing instructions, key research questions, linked GitHub repository (repository, null when none), linked source metadata, its context notebooks (related_notebooks), each with in_chat: whether the learner put it into the Notebook's chats, and Think first: think_first, the Notebook's own level (null when it follows the library's), and think_first_level, the level that applies.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: get_notebook

description: Read an explicitly identified Notebook's full research context for an external assistant, as its chats read it: Notebook-native workspace files, the library sources its chats read (its own ticked sources and those of the context notebooks the learner put into its chats, with those notebooks' instructions, notes and materials), synthesis notes, open questions, per-source understanding state, recent review summaries, and source content excerpts. It says what it leaves out (unticked sources, context notebooks out of its chats); list_notebook_sources lists them. When the Notebook is linked to a GitHub repository the context names it; read the repository itself live with the GitHub tools.

include_emergent_state.description: Include synthesis notes, open questions, understanding state, and recent reviews before source content. Defaults to true.

include_source_content.description: Include hydrated source text excerpts. Defaults to true. Set false for a lightweight state-only snapshot.

max_source_chars.description: Maximum characters per source content excerpt. Defaults to 8000.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: get_notebook_context

description: Read one Notion database's schema live: title, description, url, and every property with its type and, for selections and statuses, the options it offers — the names a filter for query_notion_database uses. Takes the database's id or its Notion URL; a database with several data sources lists them so one can be chosen. Read-only: ForeverLM reads Notion as the learner through a read-only connection and cannot create, edit, move or comment.

database.description: The database's id (dashed or not), or its Notion URL, from list_notion_databases or search_notion.

name: get_notion_database

description: Read one Notion page live and in full: title, url, icon, parent, dates, every property flattened to plain values, and its content rendered as text (headings, lists, to-dos, quotes, callouts, code, tables, and the addresses of images and files) with nested blocks indented. Sub-pages appear as [Page: title] (id) lines to read with another call. Content is cut at 400 blocks or 60,000 characters (content_truncated). Takes the page's id or its Notion URL. Read-only: ForeverLM reads Notion as the learner through a read-only connection and cannot create, edit, move or comment; point the learner at the url to act.

include_content.description: Render the page's blocks as text. Defaults to true; false returns the properties alone.

page.description: The page's id (dashed or not), or its Notion URL, from search_notion or query_notion_database.

name: get_notion_page

description: Read Settings › AI Usage › Your own key: whether the learner has stored their own OpenRouter key, which router it is for, and the key's last four characters. Never the key itself. ForeverLM's AI features are bring your own key: with a key stored, OpenRouter bills the learner directly, at cost, for everything ForeverLM sends through it, and ForeverLM adds nothing. OpenRouter is the only supported provider. The key runs while the account is unlocked (its free days, or ForeverLM paid for; own_key_allowed); a locked account's key runs no model, free ones included. The response names the scope: an OpenRouter key covers chat, reviews and background tasks plus every voice, speech-to-text, image and video model OpenRouter serves, first-party ones such as Gemini and Grok speech, GPT-4o mini transcription and Veo included, so the key pays for every model ForeverLM uses.
name: get_own_router_key

description: Read the Plugins place as the learner sees it: for each plugin whether it is connected, which account(s), and what connecting would take. X (connected, @username, needs reconnect, last sync); YouTube (connected, automatic import on/off, which import source is followed — liked videos or the ForeverLM playlist — the channels followed with their group_id, hidden channels); Google Drive (connected accounts with id and email, the meeting folders each reads); Calendar, the Mac's own (on/off, macOS permission) — the learner's day; Slack (workspaces with team_id, and each workspace's channels with id, name and whether ForeverLM may read it); GitHub (the account and the organisations the App is installed on); Linear and Notion (connected workspace); and the learner's own Build Your Own plugins (id, name, health, sources added). Every entry names its open_settings pane and the tool that disconnects it. Connecting any plugin needs the provider's consent page, so it cannot be done from a chat: offer open_settings with the pane named here. The Slack channel lists cost one Slack call per workspace; pass include_slack_channels false to skip them.

include_slack_channels.description: Optional, default true: list every connected Slack workspace's channels with their on/off state.

name: get_plugin_connections

description: Get the exported chat transcript or recorded exchanges for a review session or chat. The one tool to call when the learner hands you a chat link — foreverlm://chat/<id>, what the app's Copy Link on a chat copies: pass the link as session_id. A chat still in progress in the app returns its turns so far, so call again later for what has been said since.

session_id.description: Review session ID from get_review_sessions, or a chat link of the form foreverlm://chat/<id> exactly as the learner pasted it

name: get_review_session_transcript

description: List past review sessions and chats, optionally filtered by topic or source_id. Each line carries the session's id; the app's Copy Link on a chat gives that same id as foreverlm://chat/<id>, and every tool that takes a session_id accepts the link as given.

source_id.description: Filter by source ID (exact match, returns all sessions that reference this source)

name: get_review_sessions

description: Get the user's Schedule plan and automatic daily activity history, including source metadata, planned dates, reading/listening/watching/chat/review activity, completion timestamps, review status, and the Goals and Notebooks each placement serves. Use get_today_sources with date_basis=activity to load what the learner used on a particular day.

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID: only the placements tagged with it. Omit for the whole Schedule.

include_completed.description: Whether completed items should be included. Defaults to true.

name: get_schedule

description: Get one scheduled task with its recent runs, including the chat session each successful run produced.
name: get_scheduled_task

description: Read one of the learner's skills in full: its instructions, and the same skill as a SKILL.md file. Call it when a request matches a skill's description, before starting the work, then do the work the way the skill says. Pass the name (with or without the leading /) or the skill_id from list_skills.

skill_id.description: Skill ID from list_skills. Takes precedence over name.

name: get_skill

description: Report on text-to-speech audio generation started with generate_source_audio: what is generating now, what is queued, and what finished, failed, was skipped, or was cancelled, with reasons. Pass source_ids to also learn, for specific sources, whether audio already exists and where they stand in the queue. Also lists sources the learner is generating from the app itself.

source_ids.description: Optional source ids to report on individually.

name: get_source_audio_status

description: Get the full text content of a specific source by ID. When canonical stored text is available, the response includes its SHA-256 revision so a pre-generated review guide can be saved safely with save_source_review_guide.
name: get_source_content

description: Read a source zoomed out, as the Levels panel beside ForeverLM's Reader shows it: its gist (its point in one sentence), why it matters, up to 4 key findings with the section that establishes each, every section's title and one line on what it establishes, every paragraph's line (paragraphs numbered 1..N over the source's stored text), and 5 to 12 key terms with plain definitions — names first, the vocabulary a newcomer needs before the rest. Each section, paragraph and term carries opens_with, the source's own first words there, verbatim from its stored text (never written by a model), so you can quote it or find the passage with get_source_content. stale is true when the source's text has changed since the levels were written. level narrows the answer: gist (gist, why, findings, key terms), sections (those and every section's line), or paragraphs and all (the default: those and every paragraph's line). With write_if_missing true and no levels written for the text as it is now (none, or stale ones), ForeverLM writes them first on the learner's Reading Levels model — one request, a few more for a long source, billed to the learner's OpenRouter key — and answers with them; a run already writing the same source's levels is joined, not repeated. Without it nothing is written or spent. cancel_ai_work stops a write; nothing of it is saved. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

level.description: How far to zoom out: gist (gist, why, findings, key terms), sections (those and every section's line), or paragraphs and all (the default: those and every paragraph's line).

source_id.description: The source, as list_sources or a search returns it.

write_if_missing.description: Write the levels first when none are written for the source's text as it is now. Defaults to false, which reads only and spends nothing.

name: get_source_levels

description: Read Settings › Sources: for every source family (articles, papers, books, courses, meetings, podcasts, youtube, x) whether it takes part in search and AI — chat, semantic and keyword search, reviews and the MCP library tools — and whether its tab is pinned to the Studio tab bar, in the learner's tab order. This is the per-family knowledge boundary; hiding a single source is visual only and is not part of it.
name: get_source_settings

description: Check iCloud sync health for this Mac: how many local changes are still waiting to upload, how many records CloudKit has never acknowledged, quarantined conflicts, the container environment, whether iCloud is full, and how much of the learner's iCloud ForeverLM's PDFs, text and iCloud Drive files take up. Under the new iCloud store it also reports the library's move in `migration`: whether the library has moved and how this Mac joined, the seed's progress and the Mac moving it, why uploads pause, whether this Mac is offered This Mac holds my library, the rollback copy and the rollback build, the old iCloud library (when an older ForeverLM last wrote to it, what was kept from it or not applied, a question waiting for Apply or Keep), the byte parity report, the bytes each owned space holds, and whether Remove old iCloud data is available. Use this when the learner reports missing or stale items across devices, before concluding anything is lost. answered_by names the Mac that answered, as in get_mcp_status, and narrowed, when present, says its listings show only part of the library for now.
name: get_sync_status

description: Get a team's invitation link — Settings › Data & Privacy › Teams › Copy Invitation Link — and put it on this Mac's clipboard as the button does. For a team this account owns, this opens the team's iCloud share to anyone with the link, at read and write, exactly as the owner's Copy Link does: whoever gets the link can join the team and edit its library. Ask the owner before calling it unless they just asked for the link. For a member, the link is returned as it stands (only people the owner admitted can open it). Adding or removing named members is Apple's sharing sheet, which stays in the window (open_settings team_members).
name: get_team_invitation_link

description: Get the full content of Schedule or automatically recorded activity sources for a day in one call. Use date_basis=planned for assigned work, activity for reading/listening/source-chat/review activity, and completed only for explicitly finished work. Defaults to today's pending planned sources. For what the learner watched, read or listened to today, pass date_basis=activity with the matching activity_kind and send no date at all: the word "today" is not a date here. Long sources are truncated per source; use get_source_content for one source's full text.

activity_kind.description: Optional activity-only filter. Use when the learner asks specifically what they read, listened to, watched, chatted about, or reviewed.

date.description: Leave it out for today; never send the word "today". Only for another day, give that day as YYYY-MM-DD; past days work too.

date_basis.description: planned filters by assigned day; activity filters by automatic reading, listening, watching, chat, or review activity; completed filters by the actual completion timestamp. Defaults to planned.

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID: only the placements tagged with it. Omit for the whole Schedule.

include_completed.description: Also include sources already marked completed. Defaults to false.

max_chars_per_source.description: Content characters per source. Defaults to 50000, capped at 200000.

name: get_today_sources

description: Read a paper's, a book chapter's, an article's, a video's or a saved animation's walkthrough as the deck deals it: the title, who wrote it (the app or an assistant), its chapters (id, title, claim — the sentence the learner can say by the chapter's end — and step_ids), and every step with its kind (explain, figure, quiz), title, text, beats (one a card), more (Say more chips: label, text, from_paper), cites (the works the step cites, shown under its cards: title, authors, year, venue, kind, doi, url, and in_library with the library's source_id when it holds the work), anchor (figure_label, panel_label, passage, page_number, and at — a video step's moment, as m:ss), the figure's printed title (figure_title), the panel's own caption (panel_caption) and the sentence of the text that cites the panel (source_mention) for a figure step, its question (quiz: kind — recall, think_first, predict or find — question, answer, key_points, and target_panel for find; an open question graded against the reference answer) its picture (picture: figure_label and panel_label, or brief and image_id — the drawn picture's id on this Mac, readable with get_image) and whether it has an animation — inline, or by reference (animation: animation_id, title, step, conditions, url, the animation's page pinned to that step). status is ok, none (no walkthrough yet) or stale (the source's text, or the animation's address, changed since it was written, so it is not shown); subject says what the walk is of (paper, chapter, article, video, animation) and figure_anchors whether its steps may point at figures — false for a source shown as text, a video and an animation; moment_anchors is true for a video, whose steps point at moments of the talk. Pass source_id for a source or animation for a saved animation. Use it before rewriting one, and to walk a learner through the subject in conversation step by step.

animation.description: Instead of source_id: a saved animation (its animation_id from list_animations). The walkthrough is then of the animation, played by the chat beside it, each step pinning the animation to one of its own steps.

source_id.description: The paper, book chapter or article (from list_sources or a search), or a foreverlm://source/<id> link. Pass this or animation.

name: get_walkthrough

description: Import one paper for an ingest-only plugin through ForeverLM's complete paper pipeline. Supply either a public academic URL/DOI or a local PDF staged inside the directory returned by get_connector_inbox. The import is deduplicated by canonical URL and DOI, runs the required Paper Metadata and Source Content Cleanup model steps, and stamps the authenticated plugin name as provenance. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a PDF inside this plugin's private staging directory. Supply this or url.

source_url.description: Stable public provenance URL for a staged PDF, such as the Slack file permalink. Used as the paper's canonical URL and dedup key.

title.description: Optional title hint. The required Paper Metadata model remains authoritative.

url.description: Public paper URL, DOI URL, arXiv/OpenReview page, publisher page, or direct PDF URL. Supply this or file_path.

name: import_connector_paper

description: Import a Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM until July 2026) from its address, notebook.google.com/notebook/<id>, into ForeverLM as a Notebook, the way pasting the link into the source bar does. ForeverLM reads the notebook as the learner signed in to Google inside ForeverLM and files: each source (a web page or YouTube video through the ordinary link route, so the app reads it and a paper gets its PDF; a Google Doc linked in Docs; pasted text, an uploaded file or a PDF as an article holding the notebook's text word for word), each chat as a chat under the Notebook linked to those sources and drawn on the day's log (the Activity pane) at the hours it ran (a chat, not a review: its sources are not marked reviewed), and each note and written report as a Doc in the Notebook. Audio and video overviews, flashcards, quizzes, mind maps and apps stay in the notebook and are listed in left_in_notebook. The Notebook is the one named by notebook_id, else the Notebook already titled like the notebook, else a new one. Importing again adds only what is new: sources are matched by address, a chat by its conversation (and brought level with it), a Doc by its title in the Notebook, and no Doc is overwritten. The learner must be signed in to Google in ForeverLM's browser (Library profile) — a sign-in made in their own web browser does not count; the error says so when it is missing. Returns notebook_id, the source, chat and Doc ids, and anything that could not be filed.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook (from list_notebooks) to file the notebook under. Omit to reuse the Notebook titled like the notebook, or to create one.

url.description: The notebook's address, e.g. https://notebook.google.com/notebook/0a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d (a notebooklm.google.com address works too).

name: import_gemini_notebook

description: Import a file on this Mac into the library the way the app's own import of it does, whatever it is: a PDF as a paper (as import_local_pdf_as_paper does) or as a book, an EPUB or DRM-free Kindle file (azw, azw3, mobi, prc) as a book, a plain text or Markdown file (txt, md, markdown) as a text source. A paper is saved at once with its PDF and read by the models in the background, as import_local_pdf_as_paper does. A book goes through Add Book's importer: its title and author are read, it is split into chapters by the book chapter splitting model, and each chapter is filed under the book, with its cover. A paper or a book runs in the background, a few minutes for a long book, so the answer comes at once with a work_id (list_running_ai_work shows it, cancel_ai_work stops it); afterwards a paper carries its metadata, and for a book list_sources with source_type book, or search_sources_keyword for its title, lists the chapters. kind auto (the default) takes a PDF of 100 pages or more for a book and a shorter one for a paper; pass kind paper or book to choose. The file must be in the ForeverLM library or the Desktop, Documents or Downloads folder. A scanned PDF needs a text layer for its chapters to be found. title applies to a paper only: a book takes its title from the file, and a text source from its text. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

description: Import a full external review chat (Claude, ChatGPT, another assistant) into ForeverLM as a completed review. ForeverLM parses the transcript into individual question/answer exchanges that are stored, displayed per-turn, and searchable — no share link needed. Prefix each message with a role label, on its own line or inline ('Assistant:' / 'You:', or '**Claude**' / '**User**'), so turns are detected correctly. Links the review to the given sources, marks them reviewed (unless mark_reviewed is false, which the chat keeps for every later call), and optionally files the chat directly under a Notebook. A chat too long for one call arrives in chunks: import the first chunk without session_id, then pass the id that call returns as session_id with each further chunk, in order, and its turns are appended after the stored ones. A retried chunk identical to the stored tail is not stored twice. The same two calls keep an ordinary conversation about the learner's sources as it happens: save the first question and answer without session_id, keep the id, and append each later exchange with it as soon as you have answered — every chat about a source lives in ForeverLM, and it is saved as you go, not when it ends. The stored chat must be the chat the learner saw: in Claude Code, pass transcript_file (the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable) instead of transcript, after your answer is written, and ForeverLM reads the turns, their times and their source links from Claude Code's own session file; anywhere else, transcript carries the question and the answer word for word — the markdown and every foreverlm://source link as written, never a summary or a shortened version.

ended_at.description: When the conversation finished, ISO 8601. Must be after started_at. A Claude Code session file supplies the time of every message itself, and the chat is drawn in sittings, split wherever more than 10 minutes passed between two messages.

mark_reviewed.description: Whether the chat counts its sources as reviewed and marks their Schedule items done. On a first import it defaults to true; pass false for a chat that researched or discussed the sources without reviewing the learner on them — research into what has changed since a textbook was written, for one. The choice is the chat's: with session_id it defaults to what the first import chose, so the sources a later call adds to a chat saved with false stay unreviewed unless that call passes true.

model_provider.description: Optional assistant that ran the review, e.g. 'Claude' or 'ChatGPT'.

notebook_id.description: Optional: the Notebook (from list_notebooks) or the Goal (from list_goals) to file a first import under; a chat about a Goal's papers belongs on that Goal, where its row and editor list it. Ignored when session_id is given; appended chunks keep the chat's existing home.

overall_score.description: Optional overall understanding score from 0.0 to 1.0.

session_id.description: Append mode: the id returned by an earlier import_review_chat call for this same chat. The chunk's turns are appended to that session; any source_ids are added to its sources; summary, overall_score, model_provider and model_id replace the stored values when given. Omit for the first chunk.

source_ids.description: Source IDs this review covers. Omitted, the chat is saved with no sources; an appended chunk adds only the ids given here.

started_at.description: When the conversation actually ran, ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-09-18T14:00:00Z). Given with ended_at, the chat is drawn on the day's log (the Activity pane, get_day_activity) at the hours it happened rather than at the minute it was imported, so an hour spent in ChatGPT shows where it was spent. With session_id, the hours of the exchanges this call adds: they are drawn as a span of their own, or joined to the chat's span they continue within 10 minutes, so time away between two exchanges is not drawn. Omit when you do not know them: the app never invents an hour it did not see.

summary.description: Optional short summary of what was covered and how it went.

title.description: Short title for the saved review, e.g. the topic covered. Ignored when session_id is given: the session keeps its title.

transcript.description: The full chat with role-labeled turns (Assistant/Claude/ChatGPT vs User/You), exactly as the learner saw it — markdown, source links and all. With session_id, only the turns not yet imported. Omit when transcript_file is given.

transcript_file.description: The assistant's own record of this conversation on the learner's Mac, read in place of transcript so the stored chat is the chat word for word: a Claude Code session id (the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable, which names ~/.claude/projects/*/<id>.jsonl) or the path of that file, or the path of a role-labeled text export. A Claude Code session file yields what the learner typed, including messages sent while a turn ran, and every text the assistant showed, each at the time it happened; tool calls, tool results and thinking are left out. Call after your answer is written, so it is in the file. With session_id, the stored chat is made to match the file: turns already stored stay, turns the file has gained are appended, and a stored turn that disagrees with the file is rewritten from it.

name: import_review_chat

Each canvas that belongs to a notebook also has its notebook_id; pass notebook_id to list only that notebook's canvases. Pass include_trash to list the canvases in Trash too. Call it before open_canvas or update_canvas when the learner names a canvas.

include_trash.description: Also list the canvases in Trash. Defaults to false.

notebook_id.description: List only the canvases of this notebook (list_notebooks).

name: list_canvases

description: List the learner's Memory cards in ForeverLM. status to_check (the default) lists the cards waiting in Memory's To Check: drafts not yet kept or skipped (kind draft, offered until expires_at, 14 days after drafting) and the Memory items from before cards, offered once (kind from_before, kept already), each with card_id, source_id, source_title, front, back, why, optional front_images/back_images, quote, origin and kept_by_default; sources lists every source the card stands on, its own first, each with source_id, source_title and the quote it stands on there (a card often stands on several). status kept lists the kept cards, each with card_id, item_id, ask (the wording to ask: the learner's own rewording when there is one), back, why, optional images, source_ids, sources (each with its quote) and where its schedule stands (new, due, or scheduled with next_due_at). status all lists both. notebook_id narrows to one Notebook's cards (those on its sources) and source_id to the cards that stand on that source, whichever it is of theirs. With to_check or all, drafting says what Make Cards and draft_cards drafted lately for those sources: each run's state and, once done, the card ids it added, the cards it did not find in their source (not_grounded) and the sources it read as excerpts (sampled). Reads only: keep or skip cards with triage_cards.

limit.description: Most cards listed of each status (default 100, max 500).

notebook_id.description: Only this Notebook's cards, from list_notebooks.

source_id.description: Only the cards on this source.

status.description: Which cards: to_check (the default), kept, or all.

name: list_cards

description: List every course with its stable course_id, display title, metadata, lecture count, grouped-source count, lecture-item count, and the Notebooks that follow it (followed_by_notebook_ids; a course lives in no Notebook). Pass notebook_id to list only the courses that Notebook follows. Always call this before creating a course or adding course materials so an existing course is reused instead of duplicated.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks: only the courses that Notebook follows.

name: list_courses

description: List research directions with their evidence and the learner's answers: pursued first, then proposals waiting for an answer, then what was set aside with the learner's reason. Pass home_id for one Goal, Notebook or Idea; omit it for every home. Each piece of evidence says whether the library holds it now.

home_id.description: Optional: the Goal, Notebook or Idea.

name: list_directions

description: List the chats a Doc's passages started, with the exact quote each conversation was opened on. Use this to find the conversation that already covered a passage instead of starting a second one about it.
name: list_doc_chats

description: List the comment threads on a Doc — the page's Comments panel in ForeverLM — in the order of their passages: each thread's comment_id, the quote (the words of the page it is about), whether it is resolved, and its messages oldest first (comment_id, author, by_assistant, body, created_at, updated_at). The page marks each open thread's words; a resolved thread is listed under Resolved and no longer marked. Pass include_resolved false to list only open threads.

include_resolved.description: Include resolved threads. Defaults to true.

name: list_doc_comments

description: List the earlier versions of a Doc that this Mac keeps — the page's Page activity in ForeverLM — newest first: each one's version_id, saved_at, reason (what replaced that body: learner_edit, assistant_edit, another_device or restore), the app's summary of it and its size in bytes, with the current body's revision and size. A version is kept when an assistant or a restore replaces the body, after every ten minutes of the learner's typing, and when the page loses more than half its text at once; a page keeps at most 100 versions and 50 MB. Versions are this Mac's alone: another Mac, the iPhone and the web keep none of these. Pass version_id to read that version's Markdown, whole or by character range with start and length as read_doc pages a body. restore_doc_version makes one the page again.

length.description: Optional number of characters of the version_id's Markdown to return (maximum 50,000).

start.description: Optional zero-based character offset into the version_id's Markdown.

version_id.description: Optional version_id from this list: return that version's Markdown as well.

name: list_doc_versions

description: List canonical Markdown Docs. Omit notebook_id for the global collection, or pass an explicit Notebook ID to list only Docs linked to that Notebook. A Doc whose kind is google_doc, claude_artifact or codex_site is a linked page — a Google Doc, a Claude artifact or a Codex site: read-only here, with its URL in linked_url. space_id and space_name name the learner's space of pages the Doc is in (list_spaces), null when it is in none.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: list_docs

description: List a GitHub repository's commits live, newest first, on a branch, tag or commit, optionally only those touching one path or made within the last days. Each entry carries sha, message, author, date and URL. Read-only: ForeverLM reads GitHub as the learner through a read-only grant and never pushes.

limit.description: Most commits to return. Defaults to 30, maximum 100.

path.description: Only commits that touch this file or directory.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit to list from. Defaults to the default branch.

since_days.description: Only commits made within this many days.

name: list_github_commits

description: List the files and directories at a path in a GitHub repository live, with each entry's type, size and path for read_github_file. Set recursive to walk the whole tree below the path in one call (capped, so a large tree is truncated with a note). Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to GitHub.

path.description: Directory path within the repository. Omit for the root.

recursive.description: Walk every directory below path instead of listing one level.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit. Defaults to the default branch.

name: list_github_files

description: List a GitHub repository's issues live, most recently updated first, filtered by state, labels, or how recently they changed. Pull requests are excluded; call list_github_pull_requests for those. Each entry carries its number for get_github_issue. Read-only: ForeverLM reads GitHub as the learner through a read-only grant and cannot comment, label, assign or close.

labels.description: Only issues carrying every one of these labels, comma-separated.

limit.description: Most issues to return. Defaults to 30, maximum 100.

since_days.description: Only issues updated within this many days.

name: list_github_issues

description: List a GitHub repository's pull requests live, most recently updated first, filtered by state. Each entry carries its number for get_github_pull_request, with title, author, branches, draft and merged state, and dates. Read-only: ForeverLM reads GitHub as the learner through a read-only grant and cannot review, approve or merge.

limit.description: Most pull requests to return. Defaults to 30, maximum 100.

state.description: Pull request state. Defaults to open; closed includes merged.

name: list_github_pull_requests

description: List the GitHub repositories ForeverLM can read live, across every organisation and account where the ForeverLM GitHub App is installed, most recently pushed first, optionally filtered by words in the name or description. Each entry carries the owner/repo name the other GitHub tools take. GitHub tools are the only way into GitHub: nothing from it is stored in the library. ForeverLM reads GitHub as the learner through a read-only grant and cannot write, comment, push or merge.

limit.description: Most repositories to return. Defaults to 50, maximum 100.

query.description: Words from the repository's name or description. Omit to list everything.

name: list_github_repositories

description: List the learner's timebound Goals (deadline, days remaining, approved/completed source counts, review status, and the Doc, Site or animation each is for, as `artifact`). Omit notebook_id to list every Goal, tagged to a Notebook or standing alone; pass it to scope to one Notebook. Notebooks themselves are listed with list_notebooks.

include_completed.description: Include Goals explicitly marked done or archived. Overdue active Goals are always included.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID to scope to. Omit to list every Goal, including untagged ones.

name: list_goals

description: List the learner's Ideas — their own jotted-down thoughts, newest first, each with the research and explorations linked to it. An Idea is NOT a Goal: it has no deadline and nothing is scheduled from it (Goals are list_goals). Use this before create_idea so an existing thought is extended rather than duplicated, and when the learner asks what they have been thinking about.

include_archived.description: Include Ideas the learner put away. Defaults to true.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks: only the Ideas linked to it or to one of its Goals.

name: list_ideas

description: List the images ForeverLM keeps on this Mac — drawn by its chat or generate_image, or made in ChatGPT, Claude or another tool and saved with save_image — most recently changed first, each once at its latest version: its title, image_id, the prompt it was made from, the model, how many versions it has and their ids, its file path, and its foreverlm://image/generated/<id> line for a ForeverLM chat or Doc. Browser screenshots are not listed. Use it before making a picture the learner may already have, and to find the image_id that get_image, revises and delete_image take.

limit.description: Optional. How many images to list; 20 by default, at most 100.

notebook_id.description: Optional. Only the images that live in this Notebook (from list_notebooks): those drawn or kept there. A picture inside a course quiz or a walkthrough belongs to that, not to a Notebook of its own.

query.description: Optional. Words every listed image's title or prompt (any version's) must contain.

name: list_images

description: Legacy combined listing of Notebooks and Goals. Prefer list_notebooks for Notebooks and list_goals for timebound Goals.

include_completed.description: Include records explicitly marked done or archived. Defaults to false.

name: list_learning_goals

description: List Linear issues live, most recently updated first, filtered by team, workflow state type, assignment to the learner, project, or how recently they changed. Use it for what is in progress for a team or what is assigned to the learner; to find an issue by words, call search_linear_issues. Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to Linear.

assigned_to_me.description: Only issues assigned to the learner.

limit.description: Most issues to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

project.description: Only issues in this project, by id or slug_id from list_linear_projects.

state_type.description: Workflow state type. started is in progress; unstarted is todo.

team_key.description: Team key such as ENG, from list_linear_teams.

updated_since_days.description: Only issues changed within this many days.

name: list_linear_issues

description: List Linear projects live, most recently updated first, with status, health, lead, teams, progress, start and target dates. Optionally filter by team key or status type. Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to Linear.

limit.description: Most projects to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

team_key.description: Only projects a team with this key can see, from list_linear_teams.

name: list_linear_projects

description: List the teams in the learner's Linear workspace with their keys, names, descriptions and issue counts. A team's key is the prefix of its issue identifiers (ENG in ENG-123) and the team_key the other Linear tools take. Read-only.
name: list_linear_teams

description: The action items ForeverLM read out of a meeting series' session transcripts: what each session asked someone to do, with owner and due hint when the transcript named them, and whether the learner ticked it off. Pass group_id from list_meeting_groups, or source_id for one session. latest_only true returns just the most recent session's items, open first.

latest_only.description: Only the most recent session's items, open first.

source_id.description: One session's source ID instead of the whole series.

name: list_meeting_action_items

description: List recurring meeting groups as JSON with stable group_id values, session counts, and the sidebar image each folder has been given.
name: list_meeting_groups

description: List the learner's collections of Notebooks: the Collections ForeverLM groups its Notebooks by (the Space's Group by Collection, the iPhone's Home). Each collection has an id, a name (a leading emoji is its icon) and the notebook_ids of the Notebooks in it, by title. A Notebook can be in any number of collections, or none. Collections are the learner's own grouping: they change nothing about a Notebook, follow the learner's account to their other devices, and a team's Notebook is in the collections of each member who put it there. update_notebook_collection changes them.
name: list_notebook_collections

description: List an explicitly identified Notebook's workspace files. Returns stable relative paths and identifies Markdown files that can be read or edited with the Notebook Markdown tools.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: list_notebook_files

description: List an explicitly identified Notebook's persistent source context, including source IDs, metadata, and per-source understanding state (to-read/reading/understood, quiz scores, review-due): its own sources, then those of its context notebooks (via_context_notebook_id), with in_chat for each source a new chat in the Notebook reads, and context_notebooks saying which of them the learner put into its chats.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: list_notebook_sources

description: List a Notebook's tasks with every field: status (todo, doing, done), notes, due date, assignee, and the source or Doc a task is about. When the Notebook is a team's, the response also carries the team and its roster so a member's name can be resolved to the user_record_name an assignee carries. A personal Notebook's tasks have no assignee.

assignee.description: Only tasks assigned to this member: a user_record_name from the team roster, or "me" for this account. Team Notebooks only.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: list_notebook_tasks

description: List ForeverLM Notebooks. A Notebook is an open-ended source pool and MCP context; timebound outcomes inside it are listed separately with list_goals.

include_completed.description: Include Notebooks explicitly marked done or archived. Defaults to false.

name: list_notebooks

description: List the Notion databases the learner shared with ForeverLM live, most recently edited first, optionally filtered by words in their titles. Each carries id, title, description, url, parent, database_type and its property names; the id is what get_notion_database and query_notion_database take. Read-only: ForeverLM reads Notion as the learner through a read-only connection and cannot create, edit, move or comment.

limit.description: Most databases to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

query.description: Words from database titles. Omit to list them all.

name: list_notion_databases

description: List an explicitly identified Notebook's open questions (research gaps) — the emergent spine of what the learner is chasing.

include_resolved.description: Include resolved questions. Defaults to false.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: list_open_questions

description: The learner's study practices: each with practice_id, title (the practice in one sentence), why, status (proposed, adopted, dismissed or retired), origin (rule: found in the learner's history by ForeverLM; user: set by the learner; ai: suggested by an assistant), rule (what the card queue, drafting and the tutor follow once it is adopted: {kind, params}), setting_change when adopting it changes a Setting, the evidence and minimum sample behind a rule's proposal, and when it was decided. status narrows the list. ForeverLM's own rules are off until they are signed off (engine.proposes), so practices come from set_practice for now. Needs the Mac on ForeverLM's new iCloud sync. Reads only.

status.description: Only the practices with this status.

name: list_practices

description: List saved Claude and ChatGPT review session share links.
name: list_review_session_links

description: List the ForeverLM work running right now, above all what is spending money, so the learner can stop what they no longer want: tool calls still running on this Mac (a course's quizzes being written, a course, a walkthrough, a transcription — including a call whose assistant timed out waiting for it), explainer videos being filmed, mnemonic readings whose questions are being written, the text-to-speech audio queue, Teachable transcripts made in the background, scheduled task runs generating on this Mac, bulk re-queues released with decide_background_ai_job that the background drains are still working through, the app's own paid requests (Text-to-Speech Preparation, Paper Metadata, a transcript's formatting, a Zoom recording's transcription, a notebook's cover, a PDF found by browsing: kind model_step, one entry a step with its requests and the sources it is on), and automatic source audio (kind automatic_audio). A chat the learner is typing in is not listed. stopped_steps lists the steps stopped until resume_ai_work or the learner's Resume. Each registered entry has its work_id for cancel_ai_work, its kind, the tool that started it, what it is about, when it started, spends_money, current recorded spend and approved ceiling, and progress when the tool reports a current stage or count. Answers at once, even while a long call is still writing to the library.
name: list_running_ai_work

description: List the learner's recurring scheduled tasks: instructions ForeverLM sends to itself on a cadence, each producing a new chat. Distinct from the Schedule, which places sources on study days.

include_runs.description: Include each task's recent run receipts. Defaults to false.

name: list_scheduled_tasks

description: List a team's requests for sources — open ones by default — with who asked, from which Doc, and for the open ones whether this Mac can answer (can_fulfil: the team is editable here and My Library holds the source). Omit team_id for every team on this Mac. Requires the learner's Mac to be open and connected.

team_id.description: Team ID from list_teams; omit for every team.

name: list_share_requests

description: List every podcast show and YouTube channel in the library with its episode count, most episodes first. Use it to find a show's exact name before filter_sources or a search's show argument, or when the learner asks which podcasts or channels they have.
name: list_shows

description: List the learner's skills. A skill is instructions the learner wrote for one kind of work, in the shape of a SKILL.md: a name (typed as /name in ForeverLM's chat), a description saying when it applies, and markdown instructions. Returns each skill's id, name and description, not its instructions; read those with get_skill.
name: list_skills

description: List the Slack channels the learner has enabled for ForeverLM, with their names and the workspace each belongs to (the learner may have connected several workspaces; workspaces lists them). Call this before read_slack_channel to find a channel_id. Only enabled channels are listed; ForeverLM cannot see the rest of any workspace.
name: list_slack_channels

description: List durable actions available for a source, matching the source row context menu where possible. UI-only actions such as opening Finder, Safari, or file pickers are reported as unavailable to MCP.
name: list_source_actions

description: The artifacts a source is linked to — the app's Linked in menu on a source. For a paper, an article, a chapter, a video or a meeting, lists every Doc, site and animation linked to it and how: grounded (the record's own source links name it — an animation's sources, a site's cards, a Doc's grounding, a book standing for its chapters) or cited (a Doc's body holds a reference to it — its DOI or page address, or a foreverlm://source link), both when both. Each entry carries the record fields list_docs reports plus artifact_id, linked_by and url. Nothing is inferred from wording: a Doc that discusses a paper without linking it is not listed. Use it to answer "where have I used this paper?" before writing about it again.

source_id.description: The source: its id from list_sources or search_sources_semantic (or a unique prefix), a foreverlm://source/<id> link, or a web address the library holds.

name: list_source_artifacts

description: List the passages the learner highlighted in one source, with the note they wrote on each. These are the learner's own marks, made while reading in ForeverLM — the clearest record of what they found important in a source. Read them before reviewing or summarizing a source the learner has already read. A mark's publication_update is what has been learned since the source was written, as research put it (not the learner's words), and a mark with a session_id carries the chat that research came from.
name: list_source_highlights

description: Inventory the ENTIRE knowledge base (articles, papers, podcasts, books, videos). Use only when the learner explicitly asks to browse or list the whole library. Never use this for a targeted title, author, paper, keyword, or topic lookup, and never use it as a fallback after search_sources_semantic; for a complete list of one show's episodes, one author's papers, or every title containing a name, use filter_sources; refine that search or inspect a promising candidate with get_source_content instead. This result can be very large. Book chapters are grouped under their book. Returns metadata only, not full content. To list one explicitly requested Notebook's sources, resolve its ID with list_notebooks and pass it to list_notebook_sources.
name: list_sources

description: List the learner's lists in their Space: lists of goals and lists of ideas, items beside their pages and canvases as a to-do list is in ChatGPT's Space, each filed in at most one of their spaces. Returns each list's list_id, kind (goals or ideas), name, created_at, the space it is in (space_id and name) if any, whether it is pinned, whether it is in Trash, and what it holds: for a goals list each goal's goal_id, title, deadline and status; for an ideas list each idea's idea_id, title and whether it is open. A goal or an idea is in one list at most and stays listed by list_goals or list_ideas whatever list it is in. Pass include_trash to list the lists in Trash too.

include_trash.description: Also list the lists in Trash. Defaults to false.

name: list_space_lists

description: List the learner's spaces of pages: the Spaces in the sidebar of ForeverLM's Space, which group pages around a topic or a project as ChatGPT's spaces do. Each space has an id, a name (a leading emoji is its icon) and the docs in it by title, each with its id, title, kind, is_hidden and updated_at; pages in the Trash are left out, and the spaces in the Space's Trash are listed under in_trash (id, name, trashed_at), their pages in no space until restored. A page, linked Google Doc, site or reading is in one space at most, or in none. Spaces are the learner's own grouping: they change nothing about a Doc and follow the learner's account to their other devices. The teams are the shared spaces and are listed by list_teams, not here. update_space changes spaces; list_docs names each Doc's space.
name: list_spaces

description: List every team this account owns or has joined: id, name, this account's role (owner or member) and permission (readWrite or readOnly), the roster with each member's user_record_name and display name (is_current_user marks this account), and the invitation share_url when iCloud has minted one. A team is a library of its own in the owner's iCloud; call this before share_with_team or before assigning a task so names resolve to ids.
name: list_teams

description: The Zoom recordings on the learner's Mac that only Zoom can convert — what the Meetings tab and Settings › Sources › Zoom Transcripts list. Zoom records a local meeting as raw double_click_to_convert_*.zoom files and converts them when the meeting ends; a meeting ended before that, or with Zoom quit, leaves the raw files, and ForeverLM cannot read them. Each entry carries folder_path (the key for resolve_unconverted_zoom_recording), title (the series' title when one matches the folder, else Zoom's file-safe spelling), started_at, last_written_at, raw_bytes and ignored. A recording written in the last fifteen minutes is left out: Zoom may still be converting it. converts_automatically says whether ForeverLM may use Accessibility on this Mac; when it may, ForeverLM hands waiting recordings to Zoom by itself, one at a time and at most twice each, and answers Zoom's unknown-source dialog, so a recording still listed is one Zoom could not convert. Device-local: the answer is this Mac's folder.
name: list_unconverted_zoom_recordings

description: List the source candidates recorded for a source: papers found on a video's slides, papers explicitly mentioned in a meeting's transcript and notes, papers a paper's reference list cites, or — for a web article — the sources its links point at (other articles, papers, videos, podcasts; see scan_article_for_linked_sources). Each candidate carries a kind (paper, article, video, podcast, xPost), a url, and a status: 'pending' can be imported, 'unresolved' was observed but no matching record was found (dismiss only), 'imported' is already in the library (see imported_source_id), 'dismissed' was waved off and can be restored. A linked source also carries context: one line on what the article says about it. Use scan_video_for_cited_papers for videos, scan_meeting_for_mentioned_papers for meetings, scan_article_for_linked_sources for articles.

source_id.description: Video, meeting, paper or article source ID

name: list_video_cited_papers

description: List every walkthrough in the library, newest first — a walkthrough rides its source, so each notebook's Studio lists those of the sources it holds: for each, its source (source_id, source_title, subject: paper, chapter, article or video), title, author (app or assistant), generated_at, step_count, card_count (one card a point, one a question — how many the deck deals), quiz_count, figure_step_count, animation_count, and status: ok while the walk matches the source's current text, stale once that text changed (generate_walkthrough or save_walkthrough replaces it). Pass notebook_id for only the walkthroughs of sources that Notebook holds. Read-only; get_walkthrough reads a walk's steps.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks: only the walkthroughs of sources it holds. A walkthrough rides its source, so it belongs to every Notebook holding that source (a team Notebook's copy of it included).

name: list_walkthroughs

description: Read the working notes ForeverLM keeps about how the learner is working: short sentences, each a thread (work in progress), an interest, a preference, a fact or an outcome, kept by the learner or at their word and handed to every ForeverLM chat. Use it to see what they have been working on, or to answer what ForeverLM knows about them. With a query, the notes nearest those words come first (by the same on-device embedding the chat recalls with); without one, newest first. Answers with each note's id, kind, text and dates, whether notes are switched on, and running_log: ForeverLM's running summary of what they are working on (Right now, then the newest log lines). Both are kept in the background, never as Docs. Notes can be out of date; trust what the learner says now.

limit.description: How many to return. Defaults to 50, at most 200.

query.description: Words to rank by, e.g. "Berlin conference". Omit for newest first.

name: list_working_notes

description: Change how the learner reads one web article, in their own words, without changing the article: "remove the inline citations", "hide the subscribe bar", "leave out the footnote numbers". A model reads the article and names the exact pieces of its text to hide; the Reader then hides them on the page and the learner can switch back to the original any time. The article's saved page, its text, highlights, chat and search are untouched — only the Reader changes, and only on this Mac. Replaces the article's earlier reading view. Pass the learner's wish as the instruction, in plain words. If the model finds nothing matching the instruction, nothing is saved and the existing reading view stays. Answers with how many pieces are hidden and a few examples; tell the learner to open the article in the Reader, and show them what was hidden if they ask. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

instruction.description: How the learner wants to read it, in their own words, for example 'Remove all inline citations like (Lewontin 1970)'

name: make_article_reading_view

description: Lay a topic out as an Atlas in ForeverLM, for a learner who wants to understand it quickly at several levels of abstraction: a small hierarchy of 8 to 24 concepts (the field, its subtopics, concepts, mechanisms, methods, measures, claims and debates), each with a gist of a few words, a one-sentence line, terms a newcomer must know, how it relates to the others (prerequisite, part of, causes, measures, contrasts), whether it is established, debated or speculative, and the passages from the learner's own library that bear on it, cited by id (get_atlas gives their text). A concept no passage covers is kept and marked as not in the library. Scope it with item_ids (Canvas cards from get_knowledge_map) or a notebook_id, or leave both out for the whole library; with no topic, it is read from the cards or the notebook. The Atlas opens in the Studio's Atlas pane, where the learner can focus concepts, read them deeper, draft cards and lay them out on the Canvas. If an Atlas of the same topic and scope exists it is opened as it is and no model is called; pass rebuild true to write it again. Spends one model call on the learner's Atlas model when it builds. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

item_ids.description: Canvas cards to make the Atlas over, as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, idea:<idea_id> (its evidence sources count) or doc:<doc_id> (its cited sources count). A bare source id is accepted too.

notebook_id.description: A notebook whose ticked sources the Atlas reads first.

rebuild.description: Write the Atlas again even when one of this topic and scope exists. Defaults to false.

topic.description: What to lay out, in the learner's words: a field, a mechanism, a question ("the PINK1–Parkin axis in Parkinson's"). Optional when item_ids or notebook_id are given.

name: make_atlas

description: Draft Memory cards from what the learner made sense of on their Canvas, as the Canvas's Make Cards does: one or two cards from each of their Ideas (item_ids idea:<id>) and each arrow they drew (edge_ids, as get_canvas_memory lists them), in the learner's own wording where possible, an arrow's cards asking how or why one end leads to the other. Each card stands on a passage of the sources behind it (an Idea's evidence, the sources of an arrow's two ends), quoted word for word: a card whose quote its source does not print is reported under not_grounded and never offered. The cards wait in Memory's To Check, where the learner keeps, edits or skips them; nothing is kept without the learner. An Idea with no evidence gives no card (ideas_without_evidence). Sources named with no Idea or arrow are not drafted here: they come back under source_ids_for_draft_cards, for draft_cards. One model call for every eight Ideas and arrows, on the learner's Card Drafting model. Returns drafted, not_grounded, already_drafted (the same Idea drafted before), the sources whose decks gained cards, and why anything was left out. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

edge_ids.description: Arrows the learner drew, by the edge_id get_canvas_memory lists under arrows.

item_ids.description: Cards on the Canvas by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: idea:<idea_id>, source:<source_id> or doc:<doc_id>. A bare id is tried as a source, then a Doc, then an Idea.

name: make_cards_from_canvas

description: Mark all pending, non-missing Schedule sources assigned to a day done. This records each source as reviewed on the completion date.

date.description: Day to mark done in YYYY-MM-DD format from get_schedule days

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID: only its sources on the day. Omit for every source on the day.

name: mark_schedule_day_done

description: The assistant's memory review: what is due for retrieval now, and by default a linked session to conduct it in this chat. It is not ForeverLM's own daily review, which is the card review the learner starts from Memory in the app; both move the same schedules; to run that card review here instead (today's cards in the app's order, each answered remembered or forgotten), use get_due_cards and record_card_result. `memory_items` are the memory items due now by their schedule, struggles first, never a new card (the app's card review introduces those, a day's allowance at a time); each includes a stable item_id, private rubric, learner context, and source anchors. An item with `ask` is a card the learner kept: ask that wording exactly as written and record it as the attempt's prompt.
