For any other item, generate a fresh question instead of reciting a flashcard. `new_items` are consumed sources awaiting their first retrieval attempt: load their content before asking, choose one source-grounded semantic target, and preserve its compact rubric plus an exact evidence excerpt for end_review_session. `items` are legacy source-level refreshes. Ask one question at a time. Only when the learner explicitly finishes, call end_review_session with structured memory_attempts; existing item IDs are rescheduled and validated first reviews become durable memory items.

goal_id.description: Optional Learning Companion goal ID to scope the refresh to that goal's sources. Omit to review across everything studied.

limit.description: Maximum sources to surface (default 5, max 25).

operation_id.description: Optional caller-generated idempotency key (max 200 characters) for start_session=true. Retry a lost response with the exact same request and operation_id to receive the same session instead of creating a duplicate.

start_session.description: Defaults to true: starts a linked review session and loads source content. Pass false for a read-only briefing of what's due (no session started).

name: memory_review

description: Merge one meeting series into another — what dropping a meeting folder onto another does in Sources. Every session and artifact of source_group_id moves to target_group_id, the source folder disappears, and its id is kept as an alias so links to it keep resolving. Both ids come from list_meeting_groups; a folder's id is not its title.

source_group_id.description: The meeting group to fold in. It ceases to exist as a folder.

target_group_id.description: The meeting group that receives the sessions.

name: merge_meeting_groups

description: Fold the sessions of one meeting series that are really one sitting into one session — the series' Merge Same-Day Sessions in the sidebar. A free Zoom account ends a call after forty minutes and the host starts a new meeting, so one standup arrives as two recordings and two sessions; ForeverLM already folds such a pair as the second transcript lands (same local day, started within four hours). This is the hand-driven form for sessions split before that rule existed or filed by hand. Pass group_id (from list_meeting_groups) to fold every day of the series that holds more than one finished session, with date (YYYY-MM-DD, the learner's local day) to do one day only; or pass source_ids (two or more session ids of one series, from get_meeting_group) to fold exactly those. The session that started first survives with its id, URL, title and date; the others' transcript, notes, chat and recording sections are appended in start order under a “Reconnected at HH:MM” line, their files, Notebook membership, chats and highlights move to it, and their rows are archived so the same recording is never filed again. The survivor's action items are read afresh. Idempotent: a series already at one session a day answers nothing_to_merge.

date.description: With group_id: fold only the sessions of this local day, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit to fold every day that holds more than one.

group_id.description: Meeting group id from list_meeting_groups (a title is accepted too). Required unless source_ids is given.

source_ids.description: Two or more session source ids of one series to fold into the one that started first. Overrides group_id and date.

name: merge_meeting_sessions

description: Merge multiple Notebooks into one. The first notebook_id is the survivor; the others are folded in and deleted. Everything follows: source pools are unioned (deduped), and the merged Notebooks' chats, nested Goals, tasks, Docs, courses, scheduled tasks, Schedule placements, memory items, related-Notebook links, Ideas' links, Directions and workspace files move to the survivor. Open questions are deduped by summary, research questions unioned, and synthesis notes concatenated by default. All Notebooks must be in the same library (My Library or one team).

merge_notes.description: Concatenate synthesis notes from merged notebooks. Defaults to true.

notebook_ids.description: At least two notebook IDs. The first is the survivor.

title.description: Optional new title for the merged notebook.

name: merge_notebooks

description: Change a source's type (e.g. reclassify an article as a paper).
name: move_source_type

description: Open one of the learner's canvases on the Mac, by canvas_id from list_canvases: it becomes the canvas get_knowledge_map reads and apply_map_lens, focus_map and the Canvas edit tools act on, and it shows beside the chat. A lens showing on the canvas open before is put away with it. A canvas in Trash opens too, marked as in Trash.
name: open_canvas

description: Show one of the learner's things in the ForeverLM window on this Mac, as a click on it would: a notebook opens in its workspace, a doc comes forward in Docs, a chat resumes in the chat panel, a source opens in the Reader, a course quiz is taken, an idea opens, space shows the Space's All list, where every notebook and course is listed, and plugins shows the Plugins place, at one plugin's page when id names it (x, youtube, google_drive, apple_calendar, slack, linear, github, notion, build_your_own_plugin). Use it whenever the learner asks to open, show, go to or switch to something ("open this notebook") — listing or loading it for yourself (list_notebooks, get_notebook) changes nothing on screen. id is the thing's own id from the list tools or the call that created it; space takes none, and plugins none for every plugin. Opens in the window the learner last used and brings ForeverLM to the front. Writes nothing synced. Needs a Studio window open.

id.description: The notebook, doc, chat (review session), source, quiz or idea id, or a plugin's id for plugins. Omit for space, and for plugins to show every plugin.

name: open_in_app

description: Open ForeverLM's Settings window on the learner's Mac at one pane, for what a chat must leave to the learner — signing in, paying for ForeverLM, managing team members in Apple's sharing sheet. team_general and team_members open the open team's own Settings, a separate window from the learner's, and need a team library open. Plugins are not in Settings: plugins, and a plugin's id (x, youtube, google_drive, apple_calendar, slack, linear, github, notion, build_your_own_plugin), open the Plugins place on the icon strip at every plugin or at that plugin's page, where the learner connects it through the provider's consent page. Brings ForeverLM to the front.

pane.description: The pane to show. Omit for Billing, paying for ForeverLM; ai_usage is the key, spending and activity; plugins and a plugin's id open the Plugins place.

name: open_settings

description: Switch the ForeverLM Studio on this Mac to a team's library, or back to My Library — Settings › Data & Privacy › Teams › Open Library, and the library switcher in the account menu. Everything on screen (sources, Notebooks, Docs, chats) is then the chosen library's; selections pointing into the previous library are dropped. Changes only this Mac's window, not the account. Omit team_id for My Library. Needs a Studio window open.

team_id.description: The team's id from list_teams. Omit (or pass an empty string) for My Library.

name: open_team_library

description: Set cards down on the learner's Canvas, or move ones already on it: into a region or a notebook's frame (region), beside a card already placed (beside), as a block with a new region drawn around it (new_region), or, with none of these, in free space in the middle of what the learner is looking at. Any source, Doc or Idea in the library can be placed; a card already on the Canvas moves. Cards in a region fill the free cells of its grid and the region grows to hold them; a notebook's frame lays its cards out in rows. Pass at most one of region, beside and new_region. Pass color, folded, w and h to give the cards set down a look of their own at once (update_canvas_card changes it later). A paper whose PDF is on the Mac is set down as page 1 of it, its title and authors under, rather than as a card (face card sets it down as the usual card; face page shows any source as its page); pass annotations to write the learner's reason for each card being there under it (update_canvas_card changes it later). Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Opens the Canvas beside the chat and flies to the cards. Returns the cards placed, the region they went into, and any item_ids the library does not hold.

annotations.description: The learner's words about why a card is on this canvas, drawn under it, by item_id: at most 600 characters each. For any card set down in this call but an Idea, whose own note holds its words.

beside.description: Set the cards down as a block beside this card, which must be on the Canvas: by item_id (source:<id>, doc:<id> or idea:<id>; a bare id is tried as a source, then a Doc, then an Idea).

color.description: Tint the cards as #RRGGBB (the Canvas's own eight: #7F77DD, #1D9E75, #D85A30, #D4537E, #BA7517, #378ADD, #639922, #888780).

face.description: page: show sources as page 1 of their PDF; card: the usual card. Without it a paper whose PDF is on the Mac is set down as its page and every other card as itself.

folded.description: Set the cards down folded to their title line.

h.description: Give the cards this height, 56 to 2000 (a card is as tall as its kind is unless asked).

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> (a Doc, site, animation, audio overview or reading), idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id> (a shortcut to another canvas), chat:<session_id> (a chat) or picture:<image_id> (an image from list_images). A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

new_region.description: Draw a new region of this name around the cards, set down together in free space.

region.description: Put the cards in this region: its name (as get_knowledge_map lists it; a notebook's frame by its notebook's name) or its region_id.

w.description: Give the cards this width, 160 to 720 (a card is 240 wide unless asked).

name: place_on_canvas

description: Open ForeverLM's own card review on the learner's Mac over kept cards you chose: the way to review some of the cards — a topic (“show me my cards on mitochondria”), a source, a set — rather than today's review. Read list_cards status kept and choose the cards by what each one asks, not by a word in it; pass their card_ids and a title saying what they are about. The review takes the window the learner last used and brings ForeverLM to the front, as practice they asked for: the due and new cards among them first, whose answers count, then the ones not due yet, whose answers never move their schedule. The learner answers each card there, typed or said, and the app checks it; nothing is asked in this chat. Returns how many cards were dealt (due_or_new, not_due_yet) and not_found for any card_id no kept card answers to. Refused while a card review already has that window. Needs a Studio window open.

card_ids.description: The card_id of each kept card to practise, from list_cards status kept (at most 500).

title.description: What the cards are about, in a few words (Mitochondria).

name: practice_cards

description: Save the directions a search kept for one Goal, Notebook or Idea, as proposals waiting for the learner's answer — they appear on its Directions list in the app. Call it once per search with the three to seven that survived, after find_directions. Every direction needs its sentence, why it is worth a look now, its angle, and at least one piece of evidence with a DOI or address; a direction missing any of them refuses the whole call and nothing is saved. One the home already has, reworded or not, is skipped and named. Never add papers to the library from here.

angle.description: gap, transfer, revival, enabling, connection, contrarian or other — the way of looking that produced it.

evidence.description: One to five papers or pages you actually opened. Never invent one.

citation.description: How the learner would cite it: "Jain et al., Science 2016".

doi.description: The DOI (10.xxxx/…), when it has one. Preferred: it is what the library matches on.

finding.description: The one thing it shows for this direction, in a sentence.

title.description: The paper's or page's title.

url.description: The page's address, when there is no DOI or the page itself is the evidence.

next_step.description: The cheapest experiment, analysis or reading that would tell whether it holds.

objection.description: The strongest case against it, or the prior art that cuts against it.

rationale.description: Why it is worth a look now, in two to four sentences.

title.description: The direction in one sentence: the specific mechanism or approach, and the specific population, system or problem it is aimed at.

home_id.description: The Goal, Notebook or Idea from find_directions.

session_id.description: Optional: the chat the search ran in, when it is not this ForeverLM chat.

name: propose_directions

description: Publish a Doc as a page on foreverlm.com, or update the page it already has — the app's Publish to foreverlm.com…. By default anyone with the returned link can read the page; pass readers to share it with specific people instead, who enter their email address on the page and follow the link that is sent to them. The page is unlisted, and only the learner's ForeverLM account can update or take it down. It is rendered from the Doc's Markdown: cited sources stay as links and reference lines become cards; foreverlm:// links are unwrapped to their text and attached pictures are not published. Republishing keeps the same address (unless slug is passed) and, unless readers is passed, the same readers. Refused for a linked page and when the Mac is not signed in with Apple.

doc_id.description: Doc ID from list_docs or create_doc.

readers.description: Optional. The email addresses the page is shared with (at most 200). Only these people can open it: each enters their address on the page and follows the link emailed to them, and the page remembers them for thirty days. Pass an empty list to open the page to anyone with the link. Omit to leave the current readers as they are. Removing an address shuts that reader out at once. list_docs reports the current list as published_readers.

slug.description: Optional. A custom address for the page, the part after foreverlm.com/share/: 3–64 lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens (for example obesity-landscape-2026). Omit to keep the current address, which is a random twelve-character one on a first publish. Passing a new slug moves the page there and its old address forwards; an address another page holds is refused.

name: publish_doc

description: Read a Notion database's rows live, each a page with its properties flattened to plain values, with Notion's own filter and sorts passed through unchanged (filter: {property, <type>: {…}} with and/or compounds; sorts: [{property or timestamp, direction}]). Pages of 25 by default, 100 at most; pass next_cursor back as cursor for the next page. Call get_notion_database first for the property names and options a filter needs. Read-only: ForeverLM reads Notion as the learner through a read-only connection and cannot create, edit, move or comment.

database.description: The database's id (dashed or not), or its Notion URL.

filter.description: A Notion database filter object, such as {"property": "Status", "status": {"equals": "Done"}} or an and/or compound of them.

limit.description: Most rows to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

name: query_notion_database

description: Read a canonical Markdown Doc and its SHA-256 revision. Omit start/length for the complete body, or page through a large Doc by character range without copying it into chat context. Pass the revision to write_doc before replacing it. For a linked page (kind google_doc, claude_artifact or codex_site) the body is ForeverLM's read-only text copy and the result carries linked_url.

length.description: Optional number of characters to return (maximum 50,000).

resolve_references.description: Return the Markdown with the notes grammar resolved, as a reader outside ForeverLM sees it: each ((id)) block reference as that block's words, each {{embed: ((id))}} as the block and what is nested under it, [[Title]] and #tag links as their words, and the ` ^id` block markers removed. For reading only: edit_doc and write_doc work on the stored Markdown, which read_doc returns without it; start and length then count in the resolved text. Defaults to false.

name: read_doc

description: Read one text file from a GitHub repository live, with its path, size, ref and content. Binary files are described, not returned; a very large file is truncated with a note. Read-only: ForeverLM reads GitHub as the learner through a read-only grant and cannot change a file.

path.description: The file's path within the repository, from list_github_files or search_github_code.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit. Defaults to the default branch.

name: read_github_file

description: Read one complete .md or .markdown file from a Notebook workspace. Returns its Markdown and SHA-256 revision; pass that revision to write_notebook_markdown_file before replacing the file.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

path.description: Relative path from list_notebook_files, for example Article draft.md or Drafts/Article.md.

name: read_notebook_markdown_file

description: Read a site or animation kept in the library. With path, one file — the current index.html before changing it, a stylesheet, a script; text comes back as content, an image as content_base64. Without path, the list of its files. Read only the files you are about to change: save_site and save_animation keep the rest.

path.description: Optional. The file's path inside the site, such as index.html or css/site.css. Omit to list the site's files.

site.description: The site's site_id from save_site or the Sites list (or an animation_id); its foreverlm-site:// address also resolves.

name: read_site_file

description: Read recent discussion from one enabled Slack channel live, with thread replies, posted links, posted files, and exact URL/DOI matches to sources already in ForeverLM. Slack tools are the only way into Slack: nothing from it is stored in the library, so a library search never answers a question about a channel. Use this read for what a channel has been discussing; to find a specific article, paper, PDF or message, call search_slack_messages instead of reading channels one by one. The read pages back through the window and says when it filled up (truncated, oldest_read); older threads may be listed with replies_omitted, and read_slack_thread reads any thread in full. Every posted file is listed under files with a download_url that ForeverLM fetches as the learner: pass a PDF's download_url to attach_pdf_to_paper (pdf_url) to complete a paper already in the library, or to import_paper_from_url (url, with source_url set to the file's permalink) to add a new one; never ask the learner to download it. IMPORTANT: every item in library_matches is already in the ForeverLM library—not merely an external link or Slack attachment. When the learner asks to read or discuss a match, you must call get_source_content with its source_id before answering. For a named reading without an exact link match, call search_sources_semantic with its DOI or title before concluding it is absent from the library. ForeverLM reads as the learner and never posts, replies, or reacts.

since_days.description: How many days back to read. Defaults to 7; any window up to ten years is accepted, and the result says if it was cut short.

name: read_slack_channel

description: Read one Slack thread in full — the root message and every reply — from an enabled channel, however old it is. Use it on a search_slack_messages hit or a channel read's replies_omitted thread. Returns the messages with their links and files (each file with a download_url for attach_pdf_to_paper or import_paper_from_url), and exact URL/DOI matches to sources already in ForeverLM under library_matches, which are already in the library: call get_source_content before discussing one.

channel_id.description: The channel the thread is in, from a search hit or channel read.

thread_ts.description: The thread's root timestamp, e.g. 1788740520.000100 — the thread_ts on a search hit or channel-read thread.

name: read_slack_thread

description: Recheck papers already marked paywalled to see whether a legitimate free PDF is now available. Tries the publisher URL plus DOI-aware PubMed Central, Unpaywall, Crossref, OpenAlex, and preprint fallbacks; validates and attaches any recovered PDF through the normal paper pipeline, then clears paywall state. Papers remain marked paywalled when no readable PDF is recovered. Call again to continue past `limit`. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

limit.description: Max papers to process this call (default 25, max 100).

source_ids.description: Optional: restrict to these paywalled paper source IDs. If omitted, every active paywalled paper without a PDF is eligible.

name: recheck_paywalled_papers

description: Record the learner's answer to one kept card, as ForeverLM's card review does when they press Forgot or Remembered: a self-graded attempt with the wording asked as its question, which moves the card's schedule. Pass card_id (or item_id) as get_due_cards or list_cards returns it, remembered (your judgment of the answer the learner gave in their own words, against the card's back, told to them in a line saying what was missing — as ForeverLM's Check does — or the learner's own say when they overrule you; false when they did not know), asked (the wording you asked; the card's ask by default) and the sitting_id get_due_cards returned. Storage decides what counts: one answer per card per sitting (another is already_recorded), only for a card that is due, or new and eligible (any other answer is not_counted: an early answer never stretches an interval), and never for a retired card. practice true is for practice the learner asked for outside today's review: a new card then counts even on the day it was kept, and a card seen before still counts only when due. A card still to check is refused: it is kept with triage_cards first, on the learner's word. Returns outcome (recorded, already_recorded, not_counted or retired) and when the card is next asked.

asked.description: The question exactly as you asked it. Defaults to the card's ask.

card_id.description: A card_id from get_due_cards or list_cards.

item_id.description: The card's item_id, instead of card_id.

practice.description: true when the learner asked to practise cards outside today's review. Defaults to false.

remembered.description: true when the learner remembered the card, false when they forgot it.

sitting_id.description: The sitting_id get_due_cards returned. Without it, the day's answers over MCP are one sitting.

name: record_card_result

description: Record answers to a course quiz taken in this chat as the quiz goes: call it after each graded answer, or a few at a time, with one result per question answered since the last call, graded by you against the reference answer (get_course_quiz with include_answers). Each call adds to the quiz's sitting under way, the same sitting the app's Continue Quiz picks up whether it was begun here, in another chat or in the app, or starts one when none is; the reply gives its sitting_id and the next question to ask. The sitting keeps each question, answer and your feedback as a ForeverLM chat, the quiz's row in the course shows it under way, and every miss becomes a Memory item that comes back in spaced review as soon as it is recorded. It completes once every question has an outcome, or when you pass finish true because the learner stops, and questions without an outcome then count as skipped; the quiz's row then shows the score, exactly as a sitting in the app does. Recording a question again corrects its grade.

finish.description: Optional: true ends the sitting now, when the learner stops before the last question; the questions without an outcome count as skipped and the score is recorded (default false: the sitting completes once every question has an outcome).

new_sitting.description: Optional: true starts a new sitting from question 1 even though one is under way, when the learner wants to start over (default false).

answer.description: The learner's answer, in their words.

outcome.description: correct, partial or incorrect for a graded answer; remembered or forgot when the learner graded themselves; skipped.

question_id.description: The question's id, as get_course_quiz lists it in brackets before the question.

sitting_id.description: Optional: the sitting to add to, as an earlier call's reply or get_course_quiz names it. Leave it out to go on with the quiz's sitting under way, or to start one when none is; pass it to correct an answer in a sitting already completed.

name: record_course_quiz_result

description: Close a cohort review. Rewrite what the learner now understands about each source actually discussed — the complete replacement document, compacted, not a patch — and record a short session summary. Only sources the session covered may be written; anything else is rejected.

session_summary.description: At most three lines: what was covered, what moved, what to pick up next time.

open_thread_count.description: How many genuinely unresolved threads you left. 0 is normal.

understanding_markdown.description: The complete rewritten document about what THIS learner understands. Not a summary of the source.

name: record_understanding

description: Re-fetch a source's content from its URL and store it, clearing an error state. A web article is refreshed exactly as the app's Refresh from Website does it: read through ForeverLM's signed-in browser, cleaned, and stored with its re-archived page only when the site showed no bot check and returned at least as much text as the saved article, so a paywall preview never replaces it. A podcast episode's transcript is fetched again from Apple Podcasts the way the app fetches one, never its page's text, in the background: the answer names the work, cancel_ai_work stops it, and the stored transcript stays until the new one is saved.
name: refetch_source_content

description: Re-check the selected YouTube import source and import any new videos (metadata only).
name: refresh_youtube_sources

description: Remove every episode of a podcast show (matched by show name) — dismiss + archive each, like Studio's 'Remove All from <show>'.

show_name.description: Podcast show name as shown in Studio

name: remove_all_from_podcast

description: Remove every active source a user-made plugin added, identified by its plugin label (shown on the source rows and in the OAuth consent). Same semantics as remove_source per source: the URL is dismissed so discovery will not re-add it, then the source is archived (undownloaded papers are deleted). Full-scope connections only.

connector_label.description: The plugin label whose sources should be removed.

name: remove_connector_sources

description: Remove a material from a course lecture by its lecture-item ID.
name: remove_course_lecture_item

description: Remove a source the same way the Studio context menu does: dismiss its URL so discovery will not re-add it, then archive it (or permanently delete an undownloaded paper).
name: remove_source

description: Rename a course lecture by ID.

title.description: New lecture title

name: rename_course_lecture

description: Rename one of a course's quizzes, and optionally change its symbol, without touching its questions, picture or scores. The title names the topics its questions cover, two to six words in title case, without the word "Quiz" (for example "Cristae and Supercomplexes"); the course's list shows it in place of the plain "Quiz".

symbol.description: Optional SF Symbol name for the quiz's tile.

title.description: The quiz's new title.

name: rename_course_quiz

description: Rename a course, video playlist, or meeting group (sets its display title). group_key is the course name, video-playlist id, or meeting group name.

group_key.description: Course name, video-playlist id, or meeting group name.

name: rename_group

description: Give a kept image a new title — the name its Notebook's Studio lists it under, as the learner renames it there. Every version takes the title; the pictures, prompts and dates are left as they are.

image.description: The image: its image_id from list_images, the id of any of its versions, or its foreverlm://image/generated/<id> address or Markdown line.

title.description: The new title: a few words naming the picture.

name: rename_image

description: Rename a team this account owns — Settings › Data & Privacy › Teams › the team's ⋯ menu › Rename…, or Team General's name field. The new name is what every member sees and what an invitee sees on the invitation before accepting; it syncs to every member through iCloud. Only the owner can rename (a member's pane says so), and this refuses a member's team the same way. team_id comes from list_teams. Returns the team.

name.description: The new name; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed and it cannot be empty.

name: rename_team

description: Put the learner's Goals in an order — the drag of a row in the Goals tab. goal_ids may be a subset: the listed Goals are placed first in the given order, and every other open Goal follows in the order it already reads (placed Goals, then the rest by deadline), so reordering three never scrambles the rest. Pass an empty list to forget every placement and read by deadline again. The order drives the Goals tab and list_goals. Each id must name an open timebound Goal (from list_goals); a Notebook, a finished Goal or an unknown id is refused and nothing changes. Confirm the order with the learner before calling this.

goal_ids.description: Timebound Goal IDs in the desired order (first = top of the list). May be a subset; unlisted Goals follow in their current order. An empty list clears every placement.

name: reorder_goals

description: Set the study order of an explicitly identified Notebook's approved sources — which ones the learner wants to do first. source_ids may be a subset: listed sources are placed first in the given order; all remaining approved sources keep their current relative order after them. The new order drives list_notebook_sources, get_notebook_context, the in-app pool, and daily quiz pacing.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

source_ids.description: Approved source IDs in the desired study order (first = study first). May be a subset; unlisted sources follow in their current order.

name: reorder_notebook_sources

description: Change one passage of a site kept in the library without rewriting the page — the app's Change action on a selection in an open Site. Pass find, the text as it reads on the page (one line, or several consecutive lines such as a kicker and the heading under it; entities decoded, whitespace as rendered), and replace, the new text. ForeverLM reads the stored page, finds the passage in its HTML source — the text between tags, joined across inline markup; scripts, styles, comments and attributes never match — replaces exactly that text with the new one encoded, and saves the site with every other file kept. The passage must occur exactly once: the call is refused with the count when it appears more often (pass a longer passage) and when it is not in the source (text a script drew, or text changed since it was read). With as many lines in replace as in find, each line changes in place; otherwise the first matched element takes the whole new text and the others are emptied, tags kept. Returns the address, the path and what changed. For anything more than a passage — new markup, a new page, a stylesheet — use save_site.

find.description: The passage as it reads on the page. Several consecutive lines may be passed, one per line.

path.description: Optional. The page's path inside the site, such as about.html, or the page's foreverlm-site:// address. Defaults to index.html.

replace.description: The new text. Empty removes the passage and keeps its tags.

site.description: The site's site_id from save_site or the Sites list (or an animation_id); its foreverlm-site:// address also resolves.

name: replace_site_text

description: Report this ingest plugin's current upstream sync health. Call at the start and end of every scheduled run, including runs with no new sources, and report needs_reconnect when upstream authorization is invalid.

detail.description: Optional concise user-actionable detail. Do not include credentials or source content.

state.description: Current operational state of this plugin's upstream sync.

name: report_connector_status

description: Ask a team for a source its library lacks — the route for a paper or a book a card on a team Doc cannot add because it is not open on the web while a teammate holds it. The request lives in the team zone, so every member sees it; any editor whose own library holds the source answers it with fulfil_share_request, and their copy (file included) becomes the team's. Idempotent: a second request for the same address while one stands returns the standing request. Refused when the team already holds the source, or when the learner can only read the team. Requires the learner's Mac to be open and connected.

doc_id.description: Optional Doc ID from list_docs the request was made from.

title.description: Optional title, so the request reads well before the source arrives.

url.description: The source's web address as the Doc cites it: a DOI link, an arXiv page, a publisher page.

name: request_share

description: Confirm or reject a podcast match staged by find_podcast_match. Confirm converts the source to a podcast episode; reject reverts it to queued.

confirm.description: true to confirm, false to reject

source_id.description: Source ID with a pending podcast match

name: resolve_podcast_match

description: Say what to do with one Zoom recording from list_unconverted_zoom_recordings, exactly as the row's buttons do. action convert opens the raw file in Zoom on the learner's Mac — the double-click Zoom names the file after; Zoom asks "Files from unknown sources" there, ForeverLM presses Convert Anyway itself when it may use Accessibility (answers_zoom) and the learner answers otherwise, and ForeverLM then files the recording as a session of its series and transcribes it. action ignore leaves the recording in the folder, takes it off the Meetings tab and never files it — for a meeting that did not happen; unignore takes that back. Ask the learner before converting a recording they did not mention: conversion is visible on their screen and the transcription that follows is billed.

action.description: convert opens it in Zoom; ignore hides it and never files it; unignore lists it again.

name: resolve_unconverted_zoom_recording

description: Put one of a canvas's versions back, on the learner's explicit word, as Restore in the canvas's Versions… does: its cards, regions and arrows become the version's, written as one edit that undo_canvas takes back. A card, region or arrow the canvas holds now and the version lacks is taken off (the sources, pages and Ideas themselves are untouched), and one the version holds is put back where it was; the canvas's name, Trash mark and notebook stay as they are. What the canvas held before is kept as an automatic version first, so a restore can be undone from list_canvas_versions too. The canvas is opened on the Mac, since Undo lives there. Get version_id from list_canvas_versions. Returns the version, whether anything changed, and the version kept before the restore.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID from list_canvases. Defaults to the canvas open on the Mac.

name: restore_canvas_version

description: Make an earlier version of a Doc its body again — Restore This Version in the page's Page activity on this Mac. The version (from list_doc_versions) is written through the ordinary save over the page's current body, which is kept as a version first: the answer names it as replaced_body_version_id, and restoring that id undoes the restore. Pass expected_revision from read_doc or list_doc_versions to refuse the restore when the page changed since you looked; without it the restore goes over whatever the page holds now. Refused for a team's page and for a linked page (kind google_doc, claude_artifact, codex_site or foreverlm_site), as in the app, and for an audio overview or a mnemonic reading, whose Markdown write_doc does not change either. A published Doc's page is not re-rendered unless publish is true. Versions are this Mac's, so only the Mac that kept them can restore one. Confirm with the learner before restoring over their page.

expected_revision.description: Optional revision from read_doc or list_doc_versions' current: the restore is refused when the page no longer has it.

publish.description: When the Doc has a published page, update it with the restored body in the same call (same address, same readers). Ignored for a Doc that is not published. Defaults to false.

name: restore_doc_version

description: Let a step stopped with cancel_ai_work or in ForeverLM's background-work list run again: pass its task values from list_running_ai_work's stopped_steps (automatic_audio is automatic source audio), or all: true for every stopped step. A stopped step that runs on its own stays stopped on every Mac of the account until it is resumed; its queue then picks up where it left off, at the next library event or at once for automatic audio. Returns the steps resumed and those that were not stopped.

all.description: Resume every stopped step. Defaults to false.

name: resume_ai_work

description: Approve or reject sources that ForeverLM discovered for a Learning Companion goal. Approved sources enter the daily quiz rotation; rejected sources are tombstoned and never suggested again. Use after daily_quiz or list_learning_goals surfaces pending suggestions.

approve.description: Source IDs to approve into the pool.

name: review_suggested_sources

description: Run a scheduled task immediately, in addition to its normal cadence. The run starts on an open, signed-in ForeverLM client and appears as a new chat. While the run generates on this Mac, cancel_ai_work with the returned work_id stops it.
name: run_scheduled_task_now

description: Press one of the Settings window's one-shot buttons: sync_icloud_now (Data & Privacy › iCloud › Sync now), prepare_memory_review_now (make today's memory review ready now), draw_missing_meeting_icons (fill in missing meeting icons — billed when drawing is on), sync_x_bookmarks (Plugins › X › Sync), clear_usage_ledger_warning (AI Usage › Activity › Clear Warning), and Data & Privacy › iCloud's confirm_this_mac_holds_my_library (This Mac holds my library; only once the learner has said this Mac's library is the one to keep), upload_library_to_icloud_again, apply_old_library_removals and keep_old_library_removals (Apply and Keep for the question an older ForeverLM's removals raise). Some have no button in the window any more; this is where they are pressed. Returns what the button did. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

name: run_settings_action

description: Save an animation in ForeverLM: a moving explanation of how something in a source works — the flow of electrons through the electron transport chain, the intermediates of a cycle appearing in turn, which steps happen inside the mitochondrion and which outside, a mechanism with and without a drug — drawn as code you wrote (HTML with inline SVG or Canvas and JavaScript that plays, pauses, scrubs and toggles conditions) or rendered to a video file by a tool such as Manim. The animation is kept in the learner's library and syncs through their own iCloud, plays in the app's Animations section in a sandbox (scripts run; localStorage and cookies throw, so wrap storage in try/catch), and is linked to the sources it explains. Nothing is put on the web. This is the tool whenever the learner wants to see how something works, an animation, a walkthrough of a pathway, or a mechanism in motion: never answer with a Doc, a Site or a static figure instead. Pass html for a one-file animation or files for several (index.html at the root; paths relative). A file may carry content (text), content_base64 (bytes) or local_path (a file on this Mac — the way a video rendered here is saved without travelling through the call; an animation can be up to 45 MB in all, so it syncs with the record). Exactly one video file (mp4, webm, mov, m4v) with no index.html gets a player page written around it. Pass sources — the ids of the papers or articles the animation explains, from list_sources, search_sources_semantic or the chat's attached sources; a foreverlm://source/<id> link or a DOI, arXiv or publisher address the library holds also resolves — so the paper lists its animations and the animation opens its paper; a new animation whose sources resolve to nothing is refused with the tokens, and sources: [] saves an animation about no source. Pass description: two or three sentences on what it shows and how to read it, which becomes what chat, review and search know about it. Draw the mechanism the sources describe, label every step in words, use readable text sizes, prefer SVG with requestAnimationFrame or CSS animation, load nothing from the network unless the sources need it, and add controls (play/pause, a scrubber, a toggle for each condition compared). To show a source on the page, write a link to foreverlm://source/<id> standing alone in its p, li or div: ForeverLM draws it as the library's banner card and opens Reader in the app; never draw your own cards. To change an animation saved before, pass animation (its animation_id) and only the files that change; the other stored files are kept, remove_files drops named ones, replace_all makes the passed files the whole animation, and sources passed on an update replace the linked sources.

animation.description: Optional. The animation to update: its animation_id from an earlier save_animation or list_animations. Omit to save a new one.

description.description: Two or three sentences on what the animation shows and how to read it. Becomes the text chat, review and search know about it, together with the page's own text.

files.description: The animation's files, at most 200. Must include index.html at the root unless html is passed or exactly one video file is passed on its own.

content.description: The file's text (HTML, SVG, CSS, JavaScript, JSON). Pass exactly one of content, content_base64 and local_path.

content_base64.description: The file's bytes as base64, for a small image or font (at most 2 MB).

local_path.description: A file on this Mac to read the bytes from — a video rendered by Manim or another tool. The Mac reads it; the bytes never travel through this call.

path.description: The file's path inside the animation: index.html, krebs.js, styles.css, animation.mp4. Letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores; no dot segments. With local_path it defaults to the file's own name.

home_notebook_id.description: Optional. The Notebook the new animation's entry belongs to, from list_notebooks.

html.description: The animation as one complete HTML document (index.html): inline SVG or Canvas, styles and script. Use files when it has more than one file.

notebook_ids.description: Optional. Further Notebooks the entry is linked to.

remove_files.description: Optional, updates only. Stored files to drop, by path. Ignored when replace_all is true.

replace_all.description: Optional, default false. On an update, make the passed files the whole animation and drop every stored file not passed.

sources.description: The sources the animation explains: source ids (or unique prefixes), foreverlm://source/<id> links, or web addresses the library holds (DOI, arXiv, publisher, YouTube). Pass the attached paper's id when animating a paper. An empty list saves an animation about no source.

title.description: What the Animations list and the page call it. Required for a new animation; optional when updating one.

name: save_animation

description: Keep one of the learner's canvases as it is now as a named version, on their word ("save a version before you rearrange this"), as Save Version… in the canvas menu does. Nothing on the canvas changes. name is what the learner would call it; without one the date names it. The version stays on this Mac and is listed by list_canvas_versions, and restore_canvas_version puts it back. A canvas keeps at most 30 versions, the oldest automatic ones going first, so the learner's own are the last to go. Defaults to the canvas open on the Mac; pass canvas_id (list_canvases) for another. Returns the version.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID from list_canvases. Defaults to the canvas open on the Mac.

name.description: The version's name, on one line of at most 80 characters. Defaults to the date.

name: save_canvas_version

description: Save flashcards you drafted from the learner's sources as cards for them to check in ForeverLM: they wait in Memory's To Check (a notebook's Studio shows its count on its Cards row) until the learner keeps, edits or skips each one, and only a kept card is ever reviewed. Each card names its source_id, as list_sources or a search returns it (an id the library does not hold refuses the whole call), and a quote: words copied exactly from that source's text (get_source_content), the passage the card stands on. A card whose quote the source does not print is not saved and is listed under not_grounded. A card is about an idea, and an idea is often printed in more than one source: when other sources of the library state what the card asks, name each in also_from with its own quote (at most 5; find_card_sources finds them), and the card stands on all of them, its source chips in To Check and in review showing each. A link whose source's text does not print its quote is left off, the card still saved, and listed under not_grounded_links. Write front as the question to ask, back as the complete answer and no more, and why as one line on why the back is right. A card stands on its own: it is asked weeks later among cards from every source, so neither face may point at its source unnamed (“this lecture”, “the paper”, “the speaker”, “the authors”); ask about the subject itself, or name the source. Every card is checked for that before it is saved (a small background model call on the learner's Card Wording Check model): one that points at its source is reworded once and listed under reworded, or, when the rewording does not fix it, not saved and listed under not_standalone; when the check cannot run, the source's cards are not saved and sources_not_saved says why. Images are the default: when a relevant slide, paper figure, diagram or other durable ForeverLM picture materially supports recall, include it in front_images or back_images; omit imagery only when no useful picture is available. Each face takes up to four pictures; pass the exact Markdown image line returned by show_source_image, inspect_paper_figure or generate_image, or {target, alt}. Multiple images share a row in review. Local paths, web URLs, chat attachments and made-up image ids are refused. seed is optional: a short, stable key for what the card was drafted from (a walkthrough step, a highlight, a review-guide question), so the same seed is never drafted twice. A card whose seed or front its source's cards already hold is not saved again (already_drafted), whether it was kept or skipped. Pass kept_by_default true when the learner asked you for these cards; leave it false for cards you drafted unasked. Either way the learner keeps, edits or skips each one. A draft not gone through within 14 days stops being offered. Cards stay the learner's own: they never enter a team, whatever notebook they were made for. Returns each source's saved_card_ids and what was not saved, with why.

cards.description: The cards, one object each, at most 100 in a call.

also_from.description: The other sources the card also stands on, when they state what it asks: each with the passage that does, copied word for word from its text.

quote.description: The passage of that source that states what the card asks, copied word for word from its text (get_source_content).

source_id.description: Another source the card also stands on, from list_sources, a search or find_card_sources.

back.description: The complete answer, and no more.

back_images.description: Pictures shown with the answer after reveal. Include a relevant durable image by default when it materially supports recall. Two or more appear side by side when space allows. Each entry is the exact Markdown image line a ForeverLM image tool returned, or an object with its target and alt text.

alt.description: A short accessible description of the picture.

target.description: A foreverlm://image source or generated-image address.

difficulty.description: How hard the card is to answer.

front.description: The question to ask, on one line.

front_images.description: Pictures shown with the question before reveal. Include a relevant durable image by default when it materially supports recall. Each entry is the exact Markdown image line a ForeverLM image tool returned, or an object with its target and alt text.

alt.description: A short accessible description of the picture.

target.description: A foreverlm://image source or generated-image address.

quote.description: The passage of the source the card stands on, copied word for word from its text.

seed.description: A short, stable key for what the card was drafted from, so it is never drafted twice.

source_id.description: The source the card is about, from list_sources or a search.

why.description: One line on why the back is right.

kept_by_default.description: true when the learner asked for these cards. Defaults to false: drafted unasked.

name: save_card_drafts

description: Save a quiz you wrote into a course's structure, or replace one. kind practice is about one lecture and follows it; checkpoint covers several lectures and follows the last of them (a checkpoint closes a topic: it takes the parts of a lecture series such as "Ion Transport 1" to "4" whole, with any lone lecture beside them, about four lectures, never half a series); test covers the course (all lectures when lecture_ids is omitted) and ends it. Without quiz_id, a practice quiz, a checkpoint over the same lectures, or the course test replaces the one ForeverLM would write in that place. Work in two steps. First list the learning points, before writing any question: read each lecture video's whole transcript with get_source_content, first line to last, and each of the lecture's readings (get_course lists them; read a textbook reading's planned pages), and put every key point and fact worth remembering in learning_points, one short sentence each stating the point itself, in lecture order. A dense lecture teaches a point or more a minute, so a sixteen-minute lecture usually has fifteen or more; three is never all of them. Then write the questions from that list: every learning point gets at least one question, and each question names in points the learning points it tests. A quiz that leaves a point without a question is refused. Write it as a textbook's problem set, working up from recall through explain and apply to challenge problems that combine ideas, in that order. Questions are open: never multiple choice, each with one right answer. Tie each to the lecture source or reading it rests on with source_id so a miss can come back in Memory, give quote as the source's exact words (a quiz with a question on a source that has text and no quote the text contains is refused, naming each), and for a reading's question its page. Give a question a picture wherever seeing something makes its point clear — a slide's diagram, a structure, a graph, a pathway, an equation on the board, a figure of the reading — and the quiz shows it every time: look at the lecture video with show_source_image at the question's time, or at the reading's page, check it really shows the point (not just a title, the speaker, or a transition), crop to the part that matters, then pass the Markdown image line it returned as picture.image. Where nothing in the lecture or reading shows it, draw one with generate_image, or make it in another app and keep it with save_image, and pass its image_id; or pass brief and ForeverLM draws it later (add_course_quiz_pictures). show_with question puts it above the question, which may then point at it; show_with answer holds it until the learner has answered, for a picture that shows the answer. Leave pictures off questions a picture does not help. set_course_quiz_picture changes one question's picture without saving the quiz again.

after_lecture_id.description: Optional: the lecture the quiz follows in the course; defaults to the last of lecture_ids.

learning_points.description: Listed before the questions are written: every key point and fact worth remembering in the lectures' videos and their readings, one short sentence each stating the point itself ("Cardiolipin has four acyl chains, not two", not "Cardiolipin structure"), in lecture order, taken from the whole transcript. For a checkpoint or the test, each lecture's important points. Every point needs a question.

lecture_ids.description: The lectures the quiz is about (lecture ids from get_course): one for practice, several for a checkpoint.

questions.description: The questions, in the order to ask them (at most 60): at least one for every learning point.

answer.description: The reference answer: the short answer first, then at most one sentence why; for an apply or challenge problem, the result and then the reasoning in at most three sentences.

key_points.description: One to three things a complete answer mentions.

level.description: Optional: how far up the problem set the question sits — recall (what was said), explain (why or how), apply (an idea used on a new case), challenge (several ideas, more than one step).

page.description: Optional, for a question about a reading: the page of the source it rests on, counted from 1 within the source as get_source_content's [page N] lines count it, for Reread.

picture.description: The picture the question is shown with: give one of image, image_id, at, page or brief.

at.description: Instead: a time in the question's source video, seconds (265) or 4:25; the frame on screen then.

brief.description: Instead: what a picture ForeverLM draws for the question must show — the one idea it makes visible, what is drawn and how the parts relate, the few things labelled — with no invented data; add_course_quiz_pictures draws it on the learner's image model. With image_id, what that picture was made from.

caption.description: What the picture shows, in a few words that do not give the answer away.

crop.description: With at or page: the part of the frame or page to show, as fractions of it from its top-left corner.

image.description: The Markdown image line (or its foreverlm://image address) that show_source_image returned for a lecture's frame or a reading's page, after you looked at it and cropped it; or that generate_image, save_image or list_images returned for an image in ForeverLM's store.

image_id.description: Instead: an image in ForeverLM's store by the image_id generate_image, save_image or list_images gave — drawn by ForeverLM, or made in ChatGPT, Claude or another app and kept with save_image. Its latest version is shown.

page.description: Instead: a page of the question's source (a reading's PDF), counted from 1 within the source; crop it to the figure.

show_with.description: question: above the question, the learner needs it to answer. answer: shown with the grade, because it shows the answer.

points.description: The learning points the question tests, by their number in learning_points, counting from 1.

quote.description: The Memory anchor: eight to twenty-five words in a row copied from the source's text as get_source_content returns it. Required with a source_id whose source has text; a question without one, or quoting words the text does not contain, is refused, since a miss on it could never come back in review.

source_id.description: The lecture source or reading the question rests on.

start_seconds.description: Optional: where in the video to rewatch, for a source whose text carries no times. A question on a timed transcript is timed from its quote, where the lecture says it, and this is ignored.

quiz_id.description: Optional: replace this quiz of the course.

symbol.description: Optional SF Symbol name for the quiz's tile, suited to its topics, e.g. "bolt.heart" or "atom". A name this Mac does not have is ignored.

title.description: Optional title shown in the course: two to six words naming the topics the questions cover, e.g. "Cristae and Supercomplexes".

name: save_course_quiz

description: Save the targeted textbook readings you selected yourself, without asking a ForeverLM model to plan them. First inspect the course with get_course, find the book's chapter sources with list_sources or search_sources_keyword, and read the relevant chapters with get_source_content. Pass the complete reading set for this book: each lecture, chapter source, optional one-based page range within that chapter, a learner-facing title, and an optional reason. Omitting both page fields assigns the whole chapter. The call validates that every lecture belongs to the course, every chapter belongs to the book, and every page fits the chapter, then replaces only this book's prior readings; videos, quizzes, ordinary readings, and other books stay. It makes no model or media call and costs nothing.

book.description: The book: its title as the library shows it, its book id, or the source_id of any chapter.

readings.description: The complete replacement reading set from this book, at most three readings per lecture.

chapter_source_id.description: Exact source_id of a chapter belonging to the named book.

first_page.description: Optional first page within the chapter, one-based and inclusive. Give together with last_page; omit both for the whole chapter.

last_page.description: Optional last page within the chapter, one-based and inclusive. Give together with first_page; omit both for the whole chapter.

reason.description: Optional concise reason this reading belongs after this lecture, at most 400 characters.

title.description: The section or page-range title shown in the course. Required for a page range; optional for a whole chapter, whose chapter title is used by default.

name: save_course_textbook_readings

description: Keep a picture made elsewhere — by ChatGPT, Claude, an image model you called, or a file the learner has — in ForeverLM with the prompt it was made from, in the Notebook notebook_id names, so it can be found and used again. Always pass the prompt: a picture is never kept without one; a new image also needs a short title. Pass the picture as image_base64 (the bytes; a data: URL is accepted) or local_path (a file on this Mac, read by the Mac so the bytes do not travel through the call); PNG and JPEG are kept as they are, any other image format is kept as a lossless PNG. Pass revises when it is a new version of an image already kept — the learner iterating on the same picture — so that image is listed once, at its newest version.

image_base64.description: The picture's bytes as base64 (at most 20 MB decoded). Pass exactly one of image_base64 and local_path.

local_path.description: A picture file on this Mac to keep. Pass exactly one of image_base64 and local_path.

model.description: Optional. What made it, as the learner would say it: "ChatGPT (GPT Image 2)", "Claude", "Midjourney v8".

notebook_id.description: Optional. The Notebook (from list_notebooks) a new image lives in. The app lists a picture only in its Notebook's Studio, so pass the Notebook the learner is working in; an image kept in no Notebook is found only by list_images and wherever it is shown. A revision keeps its image's Notebook. Refused, before anything is made, for an archived Notebook or a team's the learner can only read.

prompt.description: The prompt the picture was made from, in full. For a picture made without one, a sentence saying what it shows.

revises.description: Optional. When this picture is a change to one already kept — "make it bluer", a second attempt at the same idea — the image_id (or any version's id) of that image. The picture is then stored as its next version, and the image is listed once, at this version. Omit for a new image.

title.description: Required for a new image: two to six words naming it, as a file is named — "Forward vs reverse electron transport", not the prompt's opening. Its Notebook's Studio lists the image under it. With revises, omit it to keep the image's title.

name: save_image

description: Save a mnemonic reading whose questions you wrote yourself: the learner reads the sources' own text in ForeverLM with each question right after the passage it tests, as in a reading generate_mnemonic_reading makes. Give sources in reading order, each with its source_id (as list_sources or a search returns it; an id the library does not hold refuses the whole call) and its questions in the order of its text. Each question has quote, the last sentence of the passage it tests copied word for word from the source's text (get_source_content), so ForeverLM can set the question after it; question, on one line, standalone, with one right answer, never yes or no; answer, the short answer first and at most one sentence of why; why, optional; and difficulty, easy, medium or hard. A question whose quote the source does not print is not saved and is listed under not_grounded. An answered question becomes a card, asked weeks later away from the text, so it never points at its source unnamed (“this chapter”, “the author”, “this lecture”): every question is checked for that before it is saved (a small background model call on the learner's Card Wording Check model), and one that does is reworded once or listed under not_saved; when the check cannot run, the source's questions are not saved and failure says why. Pass title (“<book> with questions” reads well) and notebook_id to file it in a Notebook, or reading_id to add questions to a reading that exists: a question already there is not saved twice. Returns reading_id and, per source, the saved question ids and what was not saved, with why.

notebook_id.description: The Notebook to file a new reading in, from list_notebooks.

reading_id.description: A reading to add these questions to, instead of making one.

sources.description: The sources in reading order, each with its questions in the order of its text.

answer.description: The short answer first, and at most one sentence of why.

quote.description: The last sentence of the passage the question tests, copied word for word from the source's text.

why.description: Optional: one line on why the answer is right.

source_id.description: The source, from list_sources or a search.

title.description: The reading's title, for a new reading.

name: save_mnemonic_reading

description: Save a website — HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images you wrote — in the learner's ForeverLM library, or change one saved before. This is how a chat makes an actual site rather than a Doc. The site is kept in the library and syncs through the learner's own iCloud; it opens in the app's Sites section as itself, and chat can read its text. Nothing is put on the web: ForeverLM keeps sites in the library and never hosts one. When the learner wants a public link, a Claude artifact is the way: make it there and link it with link_page. Pass html for a one-page site, or files for several (index.html at the root is required; paths are relative, e.g. css/site.css, and are referenced from the HTML with relative links); or pass repository (owner/repo, read through the learner's GitHub plugin, text files only) with repository_path and ref to save a folder of a repo — the commit is recorded. Every page runs in a sandbox: its own files and https resources load, scripts run, forms and links work, but localStorage, cookies and same-origin storage throw, so write pages that work without them (wrap storage in try/catch). To show a source from the learner's library, write a link to foreverlm://source/<source-id> (the id from list_sources or search_sources) with the source's title as its text, standing alone as the only content of its p, li, td or div. ForeverLM draws it as the library's banner card — the source's own thumbnail, its title, and author · venue · year: the Mac renders each source's thumbnail and stores it with the site under foreverlm/, together with the card script the pages load, so the cards are part of the site; in the app a card opens Reader beside the site. A source the library holds can equally be linked by its own web address — its DOI, arXiv, publisher, YouTube or podcast page — as an ordinary https link: ForeverLM matches every address the pages link against the library (by URL, DOI or arXiv id) and draws the same card for a match; an address the library does not hold is simply the page it names. Prefer that form for a paper or page with a web address, and foreverlm://source/<id> for a source with no web address (a local PDF, a book chapter, notes). The result's linked_addresses lists the addresses that matched. Never draw your own source cards, thumbnails or Open in Reader buttons, leave the foreverlm/ files alone (they are regenerated on every save), and check unresolved_sources in the result for ids no source answers to. To change a saved site, pass site (its site_id) and only the files that change: every other file is kept as it is, so never read back or re-send files you are not changing. read_site_file without a path lists the site's files; with a path it returns one file's current text. Pass remove_files to drop files, or replace_all true to make the passed files the whole site. A new site needs index.html; an update keeps the stored one unless a new one is passed. A site kept in the library can be up to 45 MB in all, so it syncs with the record. Returns the site_id and the site's library address.

files.description: The site's files, at most 200 and 10 MB in all, 2 MB each. Must include index.html at the root unless html is passed.

content.description: The file's text (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, JSON). Pass exactly one of content and content_base64.

content_base64.description: The file's bytes as base64, for an image or font.

path.description: The file's path inside the site: index.html, about.html, css/site.css, img/logo.png. Letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores; no dot segments.

home_notebook_id.description: Optional. The Notebook the new site's Sites entry belongs to, from list_notebooks.

html.description: The entry page (index.html) as a complete HTML document. Use this for a one-page site; use files when the site has more than one file.

notebook_ids.description: Optional. Further Notebooks the entry is linked to.

ref.description: Optional. The branch, tag or commit to read; defaults to the repository's default branch.

remove_files.description: Optional, updates only. Stored files to drop from the site, by path. Ignored when replace_all is true.

replace_all.description: Optional, default false. On an update, make the passed files the whole site and drop every stored file not passed. Off, an update keeps the stored files it does not name.

repository.description: Optional. Read the files from a GitHub repository instead of passing them: owner/repo, or a github.com URL, from list_github_repositories. Text files only; images in the repo are skipped and named in the result.

repository_path.description: Optional. The folder inside the repository that holds the site's index.html, such as site or docs/public. Defaults to the repository root.

site.description: Optional. The site to change: its site_id from an earlier save_site or the Sites list. Omit to save a new site.

title.description: What the site is called in ForeverLM. Required for a new site; optional when updating one.

name: save_site

description: Write a skill into ForeverLM. Without skill_id it creates one and needs name, description and instructions (or skill_markdown, a whole SKILL.md whose frontmatter gives the name and description); with skill_id it changes only the fields passed. The name becomes the /command in ForeverLM's chat: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and no two skills may share one. The description is what the chat reads to decide when the skill applies, so say when to use it, not only what it does. Write a skill only when the learner asks for one.

description.description: When the skill applies and what it does, in one paragraph (at most 1,024 characters).

instructions.description: Markdown: how to do the work.

name.description: Short name, typed after / in the chat.

skill_id.description: Skill ID from list_skills, to change an existing skill.

skill_markdown.description: A whole SKILL.md (frontmatter with name and description, then the instructions), instead of the three fields. A field passed alongside it wins.

name: save_skill

description: Save a pre-generated Source Review Guide for one source. First call get_source_content, generate a concise source-grounded guide with KEY IDEAS, REVIEW QUESTIONS AND ANSWER GUIDES (Question, Strong answer, Probe), and CONNECTION QUESTION, then pass the returned content_sha256 unchanged. The guide is bound to that exact canonical source revision, replaces any older guide, clears a pending preparation request, and syncs to the learner's other devices.

content_sha256.description: Exact content_sha256 returned by get_source_content. The save fails if the source changed after the guide was generated.

guide.description: Source-grounded plain-text review guide. Use the Source Review Guide sections described above; do not include a review-session transcript or learner score.

source_id.description: Source ID from get_source_content or a Schedule tool.

name: save_source_review_guide

description: Save a walkthrough you wrote for a paper, a book chapter, an article or a YouTube video, to be played by the chat beside it in the Reader one step at a time — the in-Reader form of a figure companion site: the source stays on screen and your explanation moves over it, so never build a separate site to explain a source's figures when this will do. Read the source first (get_source_content) and, for a paper or a chapter split from a PDF, look at its figures (inspect_paper_figure, which also gives each figure's panels), then pass title and either chapters — one per claim of the source's argument, three to seven, each with a title, the claim as one sentence the learner could say back (plain words, about twenty at most, one point), and its steps, ending on a question — or a flat steps list. Teach the argument's claims, not a tour of the figures, and meet the figures in the order the source prints them (Figure 1 before Figure 2, panel a before panel b) unless the argument cannot be taught that way; a step that outlines a figure ahead of a lower-numbered one the learner has not seen yet says why, and when the earlier figures come, in its first beat, and warnings name such a jump. Walk each figure in one run of steps, with at most one deliberate return to a panel later on, and bring back a figure already walked as a step's picture rather than another step outlining it. A figure that carries no claim is left out, but a figure the walk shows has every panel inspect_paper_figure lists addressed before the walk leaves it: a step for each panel that carries a claim, a beat naming each other one, and warnings name a panel left unaddressed. Steps come in reading order, one point a step — the learner presses Next between them, so each says what to look at, what it shows and what it means, and stops. Explain it the way a good textbook does, simply and step by step, for a learner who is bright and willing but new to the field; when their About you is set (get_app_settings, account.about_you), pitch it to them instead. Teach the terms and parts the argument needs in beats of their own, in plain words, before the step that uses them, never in a more chip alone; bring in at most one or two new terms or names a card and leave out a name the walk never uses again; start an abstract claim from a concrete case the learner can picture; translate the source's language into plain words rather than rewording it; let each beat say how it follows from the one before (so, because, but); keep what is established apart from what is the author's proposal. Beyond the opening and closing field context, your own knowledge enters only as textbook background you are certain of — what a term means, a well-established mechanism, a concrete example — never as the source's finding. Write each step as beats: every beat is dealt as a card of its own — one short sentence — and a beat can name the panel it is about so the Reader's outline moves with it. A step may offer up to three more chips ({label, text, from_paper}) for context a newcomer may want and the argument can do without; from_paper is true only for the source's own words. A step whose point rests on a work the source names or cites — a paper, a book, an article, a talk — names it in cites (up to three), and its cards show it under the point as a card that opens the work where the library holds it and its page otherwise, with Add: copy the title and authors as the source or its reference list prints them, and give a doi or url only when the source prints it or you opened the page yourself, never one recalled; pass source_id when the library holds the work. Each step has kind (explain, figure or quiz), a short title, body (one to three plain paragraphs, about 60 to 150 words, blank-line separated, no Markdown headings; a figure step reads the panel before it interprets it — what that panel's own x and y axes plot (never a neighbouring panel's) and in what units, what each trace, colour or symbol is, then what the data do, then what it means — since the learner reads the body beside a figure they may find daunting). A figure step is about one panel: figure_label exactly as the source prints it ("Figure 2") with panel_label ("a"), which the Reader outlines on the page; two or three adjacent panels share a step only when they make one point together (panel_label the first, the body naming each), and no step tours a whole multi-panel figure. An explain step is the chat talking and takes an anchor only when its point is in the source's own words: passage (eight to forty words, copied exactly), which the Reader marks or flashes; a step that sets up or sums up carries no anchor and the Reader stays where it is; page_number (one-based) is a fallback. Open by situating the source in its field — what was known or believed before it, the open problem or debate it enters, why the question matters beyond the system it studies — as a journal's editorial summary would, marking what is the source's own account and what is yours and adding only what you can vouch for, and close with what changes for the field if the authors are right; a learner who reads the source alone gets only its specifics. An article and an EPUB chapter are shown as text and have no figures: anchor the steps of theirs that are about particular words with a passage; a figure_label on one is refused and named in warnings, and get_walkthrough's figure_anchors says beforehand which kind a source takes. A YouTube video is walked through by its talk, and this is the one way to write its walk: read its transcript (get_source_content, whose [m:ss] markers time each block) and look at its slides or any moment's frame (show_source_image), then give each step at, the moment of the talk it is about ("12:34" or whole seconds) — the Reader seeks the video there and holds it paused while the step's cards are read, so the learner sees what the talk showed then and presses play to hear it; a step that quotes the talk (passage, copied from one transcript block) and leaves at out is placed where the talk says the quote, and a step with neither leaves the video where it is. A video has no figures: its steps are explain and quiz steps, and a figure_label on one is refused. A quiz step carries quiz: {kind, question, answer, key_points, target_panel} — an open question the learner answers in their own words, graded by the chat's tutor against your reference answer and key points; never multiple choice (the old {options, correct_index, explanation} shape is still accepted for one release, saved as an open question with the correct option as the answer, and warned about). kind is recall (the default, about what the cards just showed), think_first (asked before the evidence), predict (the step points at a panel with figure_label and panel_label whose data stay hidden on the card and the page until the learner answers; answer says what the data show; one pointing at no figure is asked as think_first) or find (the step points at a figure with figure_label and no panel_label, and target_panel names the panel that answers, one of the figure's printed panels; the learner picks it on the figure).
