Write questions the way quantum.country's essays do: right after the point they test, usually two or three together, and at each chapter's end; one detail each, with one right answer; an answer that leads with a word, number, direction or name the learner can check at a glance; never yes or no, never a card's sentence with a word blanked out; the central ideas asked from more than one side; aimed at the argument — what a panel or passage showed and what it means for the claim, what causes what, why a control was needed — with some why and a little application; a term only when the walk keeps using it, asked for its meaning, never "what does the author call X"; no trivia; each question standalone, since it is read again away from the cards. Most are recall; use think_first, predict and find once or twice each where they earn it. Every point card shows a picture: a figure step's figure, or a step's picture — a figure of the source shown without outlining it, or an image drawn with generate_image (pass its image_id) — and a step without one shows the picture of the step before it in its chapter, so draw a new one only where the point moves on; an article or an EPUB chapter has no figures, so its pictures are drawn ones. A step's animation is dealt as a card of its own after the step's points, with no figure above it. A step may carry animation_html: one complete HTML document (inline SVG or Canvas, CSS and JavaScript; nothing loaded from the network, no storage, under 24,000 characters) that plays on a card of its own after the step's points and enlarged on request — at most six per walkthrough — or animation_brief, a description ForeverLM may draw later. Better than inline HTML for anything drawn more than once: a step may show a SAVED animation (from save_animation / list_animations) by reference — animation (its id or address), animation_step (one-based step of the animation's own player) and animation_conditions (condition id → value, as the animation's page reads them) — and the chat's card loads the animation's page pinned to that step, with no size limit; a pane showing the animation beside the chat is pointed at the step instead. A walkthrough can also be OF an animation: pass animation in place of source_id, and every step's animation defaults to it, so the chat beside the animation plays the walk and the page follows step by step. Such steps take no figure or passage anchors. A kit animation's build writes these steps as walkthrough.json (mitochondria animations/kit/build.py --walkthrough); pass them through. Every figure label and passage is checked against the source's figure index and text; a step whose anchor is not found keeps its words and loses the anchor, and warnings name each. At most 40 steps besides the questions, and at most 20 questions. Replaces the subject's existing walkthrough. Refused when the source's text has not been read yet. A book is walked through one chapter at a time: save one walkthrough per chapter.

animation.description: Instead of source_id: a saved animation (its animation_id from list_animations). The walkthrough is then of the animation, played by the chat beside it, each step pinning the animation to one of its own steps.

chapters.description: Instead of steps: the walk in chapters, one per claim of the source's argument (three to seven, at most 10), each with a title, its claim as one sentence the learner could say back (its recap card), and its steps in reading order. The steps are one list underneath; at most 40 besides the questions, and 20 questions.

claim.description: One sentence the learner should be able to say by the chapter's end, specific enough to be wrong.

steps.description: The chapter's steps, shaped as the top-level steps are.

title.description: Two to five words naming the claim.

source_id.description: The paper, book chapter, article or YouTube video (from list_sources or a search), or a foreverlm://source/<id> link. Pass this or animation.

steps.description: The steps in reading order, one point each, at most 40 besides the questions, and 20 questions. Pass this or chapters.

animation.description: A saved animation this step shows (its animation_id or address). In a walkthrough of an animation it defaults to that animation.

animation_brief.description: A teaching plan for an animation of this step, for ForeverLM to draw later — not a scene. In order: the one sentence the learner should be able to say after watching; what in the figure or the text makes that hard to see; what is drawn and what moves, each motion standing for something; the conditions it compares and what changes between them; the measured values it should show.

animation_conditions.description: Condition id → value for the animation's page (a choice's option value; "1" or "0" for a toggle), as the animation's walkthrough.json lists them.

animation_html.description: A complete HTML document that animates the step's mechanism. Inline only; nothing from the network; under 24,000 characters.

animation_step.description: The one-based step of the animation's own player the card pins to. Defaults to 1.

at.description: A YouTube video's step only: the moment of the talk the step is about — whole seconds (754) or a clock reading (12:34, 1:02:03). The Reader seeks the video there and holds it paused while the step's cards are read. Left out, a step whose passage quotes the talk is placed where the talk says it.

beats.description: The step as the chat reveals it, one beat each time the learner presses Next: two to six single sentences of at most about 25 words — for a figure step, where to look, the axes, the legend, what the data do, and last the takeaway, which is what the step folds to once the walk moves on. Each beat is {text}, with panel_label (and figure_label for another figure) when it is about a different panel than the step's anchor; the Reader moves its outline there when the beat is shown. A bare string is taken as {text}. Without beats, the chat cuts body into sentences.

figure_label.description: A figure the source prints, when the beat is about another figure than the step's.

panel_label.description: The panel the beat is about ("b").

body.description: One to three plain paragraphs, about 60 to 150 words, separated by blank lines: what to look at, what it shows, what it means. No headings, lists or citations. May be left out when beats are given; it is then the beats run together.

cites.description: Up to three works the step's point rests on that the source names or cites — a paper, a book, an article, a talk — each shown under the step's point cards as a card that opens it: the saved copy when the library holds it, else its page, with Add. Never the source being walked.

authors.description: Its authors as printed, separated by semicolons ("Alexander Lerchner", "Hofmeyr J-HS; Cornish-Bowden A").

doi.description: Its DOI (10.x/y), only when the source prints it or you looked it up; never recalled.

source_id.description: The library source the work is, from list_sources or a search, when the library holds it.

title.description: The work's title in full, as the source or its reference list prints it.

url.description: An address of the work itself that the source prints or you opened; a foreverlm://source/<id> link names a library source.

venue.description: The journal, publisher, preprint server or site.

figure_label.description: The figure's printed label, exactly as in the source ("Figure 2", "Fig. 3"). Only for a paper or a chapter split from a PDF; an article or an EPUB chapter has no figures to outline, and a label on one is refused.

kind.description: explain for a passage or idea, figure for a figure or panel the Reader outlines, quiz for an open question.

more.description: Up to three Say more chips on the step's cards: context offered, never pushed — a term, a method, a why a newcomer may want and an expert would skip.

from_paper.description: True only when the words are the source's own; anything else is labelled general knowledge.

label.description: The chip's words ("What is ²³Na NMR?").

text.description: Two or three sentences shown when the chip is pressed.

page_number.description: The one-based page the step is about, used when no figure or passage anchors it.

panel_label.description: The one panel of the figure the step is about ("a"); every figure step sets it unless the figure's panels cannot be told apart.

passage.description: Eight to forty of the source's own words, copied exactly, for the Reader to find and mark — only when the step's point is in those words; a setup or summary step goes unanchored. The one anchor an article or an EPUB chapter takes.

picture.description: The picture the step's point cards show when the step outlines no figure; a figure step's cards show its figure, and a question card only its own step's figure. Either a figure of the source shown without outlining it (figure_label, panel_label — a paper or a PDF chapter only), or a picture: image_id of one drawn with generate_image or kept with save_image, or brief, a picture for ForeverLM to draw later. A step without one shows the picture of the step before it in its chapter, so give one only where the point moves on.

brief.description: What the picture must teach: the one idea it makes visible, what is drawn and how the parts relate, the few things labelled. No decoration and no invented data. Kept with the picture's image_id as what it was drawn from.

figure_label.description: The figure's printed label, as figure_label on a step.

image_id.description: A picture this Mac holds: its image_id from generate_image, save_image or list_images.

quiz.description: An open question the learner answers in their own words, or on the figure for find; the chat's tutor grades a typed answer against answer and key_points and then gives answer. No options.

answer.description: The reference answer, shown after grading: the short answer first (a word, a number with its unit, a direction, a name or one clause), then at most one sentence of why; for predict, what the data show; for find, what the target panel shows.

key_points.description: The one to three things a complete answer mentions; for a single-fact question often just the one.

kind.description: recall (default): about what the cards just showed. think_first: asked before the evidence. predict: the step's panel is hidden until the learner answers. find: the learner picks target_panel on the step's figure.

target_panel.description: find only: the letter of the panel that answers, one of the step's figure's printed panels.

title.description: A short title for the step, at most eight words.
A short title for the walk, without the word "Walkthrough".

name: save_walkthrough

description: Write one working note about how the learner works, when they ask you to remember something about it ("remember I want a review after every paper", "note that Berlin is October 21"). One sentence that stands on its own, naming the topic rather than saying "it", at most 400 characters. kind is one of: thread (work in progress), interest (a topic they keep returning to), preference (how they like to work), fact (something true about their situation), outcome (something finished or learned). A fact defaults. Do not write a note on your own initiative or a guess about the learner. A sentence that is already a note is not written twice.

kind.description: thread, interest, preference, fact or outcome. Defaults to fact.

source_ids.description: Source IDs the note is about, when it is about particular sources.

name: save_working_note

description: Read a web article's saved page for the sources its links point at — other articles and essays, papers, videos, podcast episodes, the author's earlier posts — and record each as a candidate the learner can add. This is how "find all the linked sources" is answered: call it with the article's source_id, show the learner the returned candidates (title, kind, site, context — what the article says about each), and import only the ones they pick with import_video_cited_paper. The links are read off the page deterministically; a model judges which of them the article uses as sources and describes each, and never invents or rewrites an address. Page plumbing (subscribe, share, profiles, tag pages, image files) is left out. An article with no saved page is fetched and archived first. By default an article that already has candidates is NOT rescanned — that would put back sources already imported or dismissed — and the existing candidates are returned; pass force to read the links again and merge, keeping every existing decision and adding only genuinely new sources. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

force.description: Rescan an article that already has candidates and merge the results, preserving existing statuses. Defaults to false.

name: scan_article_for_linked_sources

description: Read a meeting source's complete stored transcript and notes for academic papers participants explicitly mention, resolve each candidate against scholarly records, and save the results for import or dismissal. A recording-only meeting is transcribed on-device first. By default a meeting with existing candidates is not rescanned; pass force to scan again and merge genuinely new candidates while preserving every prior decision. Fails when the meeting has no readable material or recording. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

force.description: Rescan and merge while preserving existing statuses. Defaults to false.

name: scan_meeting_for_mentioned_papers

description: Read a library video's distinct captured slides for the papers they cite, and record what is found. Works on any YouTube video with a transcript: if it has no captured slide frames yet, they are captured first (this downloads storyboards and streams the video for frames, so it takes noticeably longer on the first pass) — or capture them beforehand with extract_video_slides. Neither capture nor scan runs automatically. Independent slides are read concurrently. The default scan is spend-bounded to 40 slides and reports any skipped slides; pass all_slides true to read the complete captured deck and fully resolve its citations. By default a video that already has candidates is NOT rescanned, because that would put back papers already imported or dismissed; pass force to re-extract the slides with current detection and merge, keeping every existing decision and adding only genuinely new papers. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

all_slides.description: Read every distinct captured slide and fully resolve its citations. Defaults to false, which reads at most 40 slides and reports how many were skipped.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

force.description: Rescan a video that already has candidates and merge the results, preserving existing statuses. Defaults to false.

name: scan_video_for_cited_papers

description: Take a picture of the learner's Canvas as the Canvas draws it: the whole plane, or just the bounds of item_ids, at scale times its size (1 by default, 0.1 to 4; a picture is held to 8,192 pixels a side), without the selection, handles or controls. The PNG is saved under Exports/ in ForeverLM's library folder and returned as file_path with its width and height, and attached as an image when it is small enough to send (4 MB). Needs the Canvas showing on the Mac (build_canvas, open_canvas and focus_map show it), and changes nothing on it. Look at it after laying cards out, with lint_canvas, to check what words cannot.

item_ids.description: Draw only the bounds of these cards (on the Canvas), by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them. Omit for the whole plane.

scale.description: How large to draw it, as a multiple of its size on the plane (default 1, 0.1 to 4).

name: screenshot_canvas

description: Search one GitHub repository's code live for words, an identifier or a phrase, returning each matching file's path with the matching fragments. GitHub indexes the default branch only, so this cannot see other branches; read a file at a branch with read_github_file instead. Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to GitHub.

limit.description: Most files to return. Defaults to 20, maximum 50.

query.description: Words, an identifier, or a quoted phrase. GitHub code-search qualifiers such as path: or language: are allowed.

name: search_github_code

description: Search the learner's Linear workspace live for issues by words, ranked by relevance, optionally within one team. This is how to find an issue by what it is about rather than by identifier. Each hit carries its identifier for get_linear_issue. Read-only: ForeverLM never writes to Linear.

limit.description: Most issues to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

team_key.description: Restrict to one team by its key (the ENG in ENG-123), from list_linear_teams.

term.description: Words from the issue's title or description, an identifier, or a name.

name: search_linear_issues

description: Search the life-science and biomedical literature in PubMed for free, with no model call; it answers in about a second. Returns each work's title, authors, journal, year, DOI, abstract, whether it is a review or a preprint, its free full text in PubMed Central when there is one, and whether the learner's library already has it. Use it to establish what is known and to find prior art and counter-evidence; read a paper before resting a claim on it. The query takes PubMed syntax: words are ANDed, OR between synonyms in parentheses, quotes for a phrase, [tiab] to require a term in the title or abstract, [au] for an author (Mootha VK[au]), review[pt] for reviews. Several searches may run at once.

limit.description: How many works, 1 to 25. Defaults to 10.

preprints_only.description: Optional: only preprints PubMed holds (it carries some from bioRxiv and medRxiv). Defaults to false.

query.description: What to search, e.g. "mitochondrial disease"[tiab] AND (hypoxia[tiab] OR HIF[tiab]).

name: search_literature

description: Search the Notion pages and databases the learner shared with ForeverLM live, by words in their titles, or list what changed most recently when no words are given. Each result carries kind (page or database), id, title, url, parent and last_edited_time; pass kind to search only pages or only databases. Call it first to find a page or database's id, then get_notion_page or query_notion_database. Notion tools are the only way into Notion: nothing from it is stored in the library, and only pages the learner shared with the ForeverLM connection are visible. Read-only: ForeverLM reads Notion as the learner through a read-only connection and cannot create, edit, move or comment.

kind.description: Search only pages or only databases. Omit for both.

limit.description: Most results to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

query.description: Words from page and database titles. Omit to list the most recently edited.

name: search_notion

description: Search across saved review sessions and their full chat transcripts. Matches session titles, summaries, and the question/answer text of every stored exchange, returning matching sessions with a snippet. Use get_review_session_transcript to read a full match.

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to return (default 10).

query.description: Text to search for across session titles, summaries, and transcript content.

name: search_review_sessions

description: Search messages and files live across every Slack channel the learner has enabled, in every connected workspace, as far back as Slack keeps. This is how to find a specific article, paper, PDF or message someone posted: one call replaces reading channels one at a time, and it reaches material older than any channel read carries. Slack matches whole words, so search a distinctive phrase, a surname, a journal name, part of the title, a URL or DOI fragment, or a file name; if nothing matches, try fewer words before concluding it was never posted. Each message hit carries channel_id and thread_ts: call read_slack_thread with them to read the whole thread, which is where a linked article's full text or PDF usually is. Files carry a download_url that ForeverLM fetches as the learner (attach_pdf_to_paper or import_paper_from_url). Hits from channels the learner has not enabled are counted, never shown. If the result says Slack must be reconnected for search, tell the learner exactly that and fall back to read_slack_channel for this turn. IMPORTANT: every item in library_matches is already in the ForeverLM library; call get_source_content with its source_id before discussing one. ForeverLM reads as the learner and never posts, replies, or reacts.

channel_id.description: Restrict the search to one enabled channel.

limit.description: Most message hits (and, separately, file hits) to return. Defaults to 20, maximum 50.

query.description: Words to search for. Slack search syntax such as from:@name or has:link is allowed.

since_days.description: Only messages and files newer than this many days. Omit to search everything.

sort.description: Order of hits. Defaults to relevance.

name: search_slack_messages

description: Search every highlight and reader note in the library, newest first. Use it to answer what the learner has been marking lately or what they noted about a topic, when the source is not known yet. Omit query to list the most recent marks.

limit.description: Maximum highlights to return. Defaults to 50, capped at 200.

query.description: Optional text to match against the highlighted passage, the learner's note, or the mark's since-publication update.

name: search_source_highlights

description: Find every source in the library whose title, author, or text literally contains the given word or phrase. This is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING match, not a topic search and not a tokenized index: "uncoupler" finds a paper that only ever says "uncouplers", and "uncouplers" does not find one that only says "uncoupler" — so prefer the shortest stem you actually mean. Results are every match, most mentions first, with passages showing the word in place; read those and drop the irrelevant hits yourself rather than trusting the order. Use this when the learner asks what mentions a specific term, name, gene, drug, or phrase, or wants an exhaustive sweep. Use search_sources_semantic instead when the question is about a topic or concept rather than a spelling. Several keywords are OR by default, which is how you sweep spellings and synonyms in one call; pass match all to require every one of them in the same source. When the question is about particular sources — the papers attached to this chat, "do these two papers both mention X" — pass their ids as source_ids so the sweep reads only those; each result lists the mentions of every keyword it holds, and the answer names the keywords no source contains.

keywords.description: Up to 30 words or phrases, each matched literally as a substring. A phrase matches only where those words appear together in that order. For more, split them across several calls.

limit.description: Maximum sources to return (default 50, maximum 200). The answer says when more matched.

match.description: Whether a source must contain any keyword (default) or every one of them.

notebook_id.description: Optional explicit Notebook ID. Restricts the sweep to that Notebook's approved sources.

show.description: Optional podcast show or YouTube channel name (from list_shows; part of the name also works). Restricts the sweep to that show's episodes.

snippets_per_source.description: Passages shown per source (default 2, maximum 5). Use 0 for a bare list of what matched.

source_ids.description: Optional source IDs (from the sources attached to this chat, list_sources or a search) to restrict the sweep to. Combines with the other scopes.

source_type.description: Optional. One family of sources to restrict the sweep to; omit it to sweep the whole library in a single call rather than one family at a time. article covers every saved web page, including manually added and still-unclassified ones.

name: search_sources_keyword

description: Search sources by semantic similarity, exact text, source type, and the local calendar day a source was added to the library. The only dates this tool knows are when a source was saved: use added_from/added_to plus source_type for requests about that, such as yesterday's meeting, resolving relative dates against the local date in the chat prompt rather than asking semantic similarity to infer time. There is no publication-date filter, so a work's own year — a 2021 book, a 2019 trial — is never an argument here; put it in query instead and leave added_from/added_to out. Query may be omitted when the added-date or type filters identify the requested sources. This is the required tool for any targeted paper, title, author, keyword, topic, or dated-source lookup. If a result looks plausible but its excerpt does not prove the match, inspect that candidate with get_source_content instead of calling list_sources or immediately widening to the web. Pass notebook_id to search only within one Notebook's approved sources. When looking for sources to ADD to a Notebook, pass exclude_notebook_id instead so sources already attached to that Notebook are filtered out. notebook_id and exclude_notebook_id are mutually exclusive. When the request names a podcast show or YouTube channel ("which Huberman episodes cover mitochondria"), pass show so the ranking runs inside that show instead of the whole library; to list every episode or paper matching a show, author or title, use filter_sources.

added_from.description: Optional. Earliest local calendar day the source was SAVED to the library, inclusive, as a full YYYY-MM-DD day. Never a publication year: a bare year is rejected, and a real one would search the wrong axis in silence.

added_to.description: Optional. Latest local calendar day the source was SAVED to the library, inclusive, as a full YYYY-MM-DD day. Never a publication year: a bare year is rejected, and a real one would search the wrong axis in silence.

exclude_notebook_id.description: Optional explicit Notebook (companion goal) ID. Sources already attached to that Notebook — approved, pending, or rejected — are omitted from the results, and the limit is filled from the remaining candidates. Use this when finding NEW sources to add to a Notebook.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 8)

notebook_id.description: Optional explicit Notebook ID. Restricts the search to that Notebook's approved sources. Cannot be combined with exclude_notebook_id.

query.description: Natural-language concept or topic query. Carries any publication year the request mentions. Optional when source_type, added_from, or added_to is supplied.

show.description: Optional podcast show or YouTube channel name (from list_shows; part of the name also works). Restricts the search to that show's episodes.

source_type.description: Optional. One family of sources to search; omit it to search the whole library in a single call rather than one family at a time. article covers every saved web page, including manually added and still-unclassified ones. Use meeting for a dated session lookup.

threshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity score from 0.0 to 1.0. Ranking is rank-fused, so leave this at the default 0 unless deliberately filtering; the contextual embedding is anisotropic and unrelated texts still score ~0.8.

name: search_sources_semantic

description: Change Settings › AI Models exactly as the pane's own controls do. target default_model sets the Default Model card (provider + model); docs sets the model Edit with AI in a Doc runs on, as the ForeverLM mark on the Edit with AI panel does (provider + model), and docs with neither goes back to following the Default Model; background_text and background_multimodal set Settings › Background's Text-only and Multimodal models, which every background task runs on unless it has a model of its own; task_model (task_id plus provider and model, or neither to go back to following) gives one task a model of its own, as its page under Background › Tasks does, and takes only a vision model for a task with requires_vision. Every selection must be a catalogue model on an offered provider, not retired — or a model from free_models for background_text or background_multimodal (reads_images for the latter), which moves only that setting and costs nothing, though its providers may keep and train on what is sent and it is often busy; background_multimodal takes only a vision model. target meetings records Setup's Meetings answer (meetings_may_use_free): false, the default, keeps meeting tasks on a paid model while their Background model is free (its first paid backup; with none the task waits, and ForeverLM picks no paid model for them); true lets them use the free one. Ask it before moving background_text to a free model. target data_privacy flips Settings › Data & Privacy's “Don't show models that train on my data” (hide_training_models): true leaves every model marked trains_on_inputs out of the pickers and the catalogue, false offers them again, labelled. target host chooses which of a model's OpenRouter hosts runs chat or a Background model's work (host_for, host, host_fallback), and whether only its hosts in the US may (host_region), as a chosen model card's ⋯ in Settings › Chat does. target backups sets the backup models chat's scheduled runs or a Background model moves its work to, in order, when its model is busy, fails or sends back nothing usable (backups_for, backups), as Use as Backup on a model card does; each backup is billed at its own price. Ask before calling this: it changes which model, and so which price, the learner's work runs on. Returns the resulting settings with changed.

backups.description: For target backups: the whole ordered list of backup models, at most 10, each a provider and model the same setting would accept as its selection (a free model from free_models too). [] removes them.

model.description: Model id from the catalogue, or a free model id from free_models (provider openrouter).

backups_for.description: For target backups: whose backups to set — chat (the Default Model's, used only by a scheduled task's runs), background_text or background_multimodal.

hide_training_models.description: For target data_privacy: true hides the models that train on what is sent to them (trains_on_inputs) from every picker, as the Data & Privacy switch does; false shows them, labelled.

host.description: For target host: automatic (the fastest host that caches prompts), cheapest, or an endpoint tag from OpenRouter's GET /api/v1/models/{slug}/endpoints, such as deepinfra/fp4.

host_fallback.description: For target host with a pinned host: true (the default) lets another host take over when it refuses; false fails the work instead.

host_for.description: For target host: whose host to choose — chat, background_text or background_multimodal.

host_region.description: For target host: us keeps the host choice to the model's hosts OpenRouter lists as running in the US, so no host elsewhere (such as in China) runs the work; any lifts it. Omitted, the stored region stays; with host omitted, only the region changes.

meetings_may_use_free.description: For target meetings: true lets meeting tasks run on a free Background model; false keeps them on a paid one while it is free, since a meeting's transcript holds private conversations.

model.description: Model id from the catalogue for that provider, or a free model id from free_models (provider openrouter). For target host: the model to choose a host for, defaulting to what host_for runs on now.

provider.description: Provider id from the catalogue (anthropic, openai, gemini, xai, meta, openrouter).

target.description: default_model, docs, background_text, background_multimodal, task_model, meetings, data_privacy, host, or backups.

task_id.description: For target task_model: the background task, an id from get_ai_task_settings' tasks (for example meeting_action_items). With provider and model it gives that task a model of its own; with neither it goes back to following background_text or background_multimodal.

name: set_ai_task_settings

description: Change one Settings control exactly as the pane does, through the pane's own setter, and return the setting with changed. setting is an id from get_app_settings; value is true/false for a boolean, a number within its range, one option's value for a choice, text, or the whole list for a string_list. A choice outside the pane's options is refused with the options. Model and voice pickers change what the learner's work is billed at, so ask before changing them unasked. For the panes listed under dedicated_tools use those tools instead.

value.description: The new value: boolean, number, string, or list of strings, per the setting's type.

name: set_app_setting

description: Switch an open or future Reader between the learner's reading view of an article and the original page. The reading view is kept either way, so switching back costs nothing.

shown.description: true to read the reading view, false to read the original

name: set_article_reading_view_shown

description: Change automatic audio — the only way to set it; the Settings window has no pane for it. Use it when the learner asks for audio to be made on its own: “always generate audio for articles from Martin Picard” is kind article with filter “articles where Martin Picard is an author” and enabled true, in one call. kind with enabled true switches automatic audio on for that kind — every source of it already in the library without audio starts generating now, and every later one follows — and is refused while the selected voice is not one automation may spend on; enabled false switches it off. kind with filter saves the kind's natural-language rule, judged from each source's title, author, journal, year, collection, URL and description: the rule is evaluated over the kind's pending sources first and saved only when that succeeds, an empty string clears it, and the response lists what matched. allow_paid_voices is the account's consent to let automatic audio use a priced voice; true is a spending decision, so read get_automatic_audio_settings first and put its paid_consent_quote to the learner before passing it, and false stops a paid run in flight. Turning a kind on with a priced voice is likewise something to confirm with the learner: the response's kind row carries the backlog and its price. Explainers is the switch for “always generate audio for explainers”: on, generate_explainer starts the audio without a quote. Returns the settings with changed. The choice follows the learner's account.

allow_paid_voices.description: true: automatic audio may run on the selected paid voice, billing the learner's own OpenRouter key for every source a switched-on kind narrates. false: revoke that consent; a paid run in progress stops.

enabled.description: true: generate audio automatically for every ready source of this kind, now and from then on. false: stop doing so for this kind.

filter.description: An optional natural-language rule narrowing which sources of this kind are narrated, such as “papers about mitochondria”. Checked against the kind's pending sources before it is saved; an empty string removes the rule.

kind.description: Which switch: article, paper, book, course or explainer, as get_automatic_audio_settings lists them. Required with enabled or filter.

name: set_automatic_audio_settings

description: Change the monthly spending limit in Settings › AI Usage › Spending exactly as the pane's picker does. monthly_spending_limit takes one of the picker's values: no_limit, or a dollar amount from monthly_spending_limit.options in get_billing_settings (5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 250). When the month's AI spend reaches the limit, AI pauses until the month resets; a limit below what has already been spent pauses AI at once. That changes whether AI keeps working, so ask the learner first. Paying for ForeverLM goes through Stripe Checkout, which only the learner can complete: use open_settings billing. The own OpenRouter key is set with set_own_router_key. Returns what get_billing_settings returns, after the change.

monthly_spending_limit.description: no_limit, or one of the picker's dollar amounts: 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 250.

name: set_billing_settings

description: Change Plugins › Calendar as its controls do, then return get_calendar_settings. apple_calendar_enabled: the pane's Turn On / Turn Off. Turning it on the first time makes macOS show its Calendar permission prompt on the learner's Mac, which only they can answer — tell them to look for it; if they refused before, it fails and they allow ForeverLM in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Calendars. Turning it off forgets the calendar choice; the macOS grant and every event stay. apple_calendar_ids: the whole list of calendars the day is read from (ids or titles from get_calendar_settings); every other calendar the Mac holds now is left off, and an account signed in afterwards (say Exchange, added in System Settings › Internet Accounts) has its calendars shown until a later list leaves them out. new_events_calendar_id: the calendar new events go to (an id or title of a writable calendar), or "" for the Calendar app's own default. Ask before removing calendars the learner did not mention.

apple_calendar_enabled.description: Optional: turn the Mac's Calendar on or off for ForeverLM.

apple_calendar_ids.description: Optional: every calendar to show, by id or title. Needs Calendar on.

new_events_calendar_id.description: Optional: the writable calendar new events go to, by id or title; "" for the Calendar app's default. Needs Calendar on.

name: set_calendar_settings

description: Turn the learner's Canvas display switches on or off on this Mac, as the buttons beside its caption toggle do: memory_layer (each card marked by how the kept Memory cards behind it stand: holding, due, fading), written_faces (source cards read as a few words, a sentence or their question, approach and finding, by zoom) and view_captions (a sentence or two on what is in view after the learner pauses; each caption is a call to their Canvas Summaries model, so turn it on only when asked). Omitted switches stay as they are. Returns all three as they now are.

view_captions.description: Write a caption for what is in view.

name: set_canvas_display

description: Offer a model in the chat picker or stop offering it — Settings › Chat › Models, the same as tapping the model's card. provider and model are as get_ai_task_settings lists them in catalogue (provider id such as anthropic, openai, gemini, openrouter; the model id). offered true ticks the card; a model OpenRouter's directory lists that the catalogue does not yet carry is added to the catalogue and offered, as the pane's directory browser does (it must accept tools, since chat always sends them). offered false unticks it; the Default Model cannot be unticked — pick another default first (set_ai_task_settings target default_model). remove_from_catalog true (with offered false) also removes a user-added model from the catalogue, the card's Remove from catalog. Changes the account's list, synced across the learner's devices; any open chat picker updates at once, and a chat currently on an unticked model goes back to the default. Ask before changing the list unasked. Returns the resulting offered list.

model.description: The model id, e.g. claude-sonnet-5 or deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro.

offered.description: true to offer the model in the chat picker, false to stop offering it.

provider.description: The provider id, e.g. anthropic, openai, gemini, openrouter.

remove_from_catalog.description: Only with offered false, and only for a user_added model: also remove it from the catalogue.

name: set_chat_model_offered

description: Enable or disable automatic import for the YouTube plugin.

enabled.description: true to auto-import, false to disable.

name: set_connector_auto_import

description: Pin a picture to one question of a course quiz, replace its picture, or take it away (remove true), without touching the question or the rest of the quiz: ids, scores and Memory items stay. The picture is one of: a lecture's frame or a reading's page or figure, as the Markdown line show_source_image returned (picture.image), or at a time (picture.at) or page (picture.page) of the question's own source with an optional crop; an image in ForeverLM's store by picture.image_id — drawn with generate_image, or made in ChatGPT, Claude or another app and kept with save_image; or a brief (picture.brief) for ForeverLM to draw, which add_course_quiz_pictures draws. show_with question shows it above the question, which must then not give the answer away; show_with answer holds it for the grade. The question's id is the one get_course_quiz lists in brackets. Returns the picture as the quiz now shows it.

picture.description: The picture the question is shown with: give one of image, image_id, at, page or brief.

at.description: Instead: a time in the question's source video, seconds (265) or 4:25; the frame on screen then.

brief.description: Instead: what a picture ForeverLM draws for the question must show — the one idea it makes visible, what is drawn and how the parts relate, the few things labelled — with no invented data; add_course_quiz_pictures draws it on the learner's image model. With image_id, what that picture was made from.

caption.description: What the picture shows, in a few words that do not give the answer away.

crop.description: With at or page: the part of the frame or page to show, as fractions of it from its top-left corner.

image.description: The Markdown image line (or its foreverlm://image address) that show_source_image returned for a lecture's frame or a reading's page, after you looked at it and cropped it; or that generate_image, save_image or list_images returned for an image in ForeverLM's store.

image_id.description: Instead: an image in ForeverLM's store by the image_id generate_image, save_image or list_images gave — drawn by ForeverLM, or made in ChatGPT, Claude or another app and kept with save_image. Its latest version is shown.

page.description: Instead: a page of the question's source (a reading's PDF), counted from 1 within the source; crop it to the figure.

show_with.description: question: above the question, the learner needs it to answer. answer: shown with the grade, because it shows the answer.

question_id.description: The question's id, as get_course_quiz lists it in brackets before the question.

remove.description: Take the question's picture away instead (default false).

name: set_course_quiz_picture

description: Change Settings › General › Day, exactly as the pane does; pass any of the three settings, or request_notifications. day_start_hour and day_end_hour set the hours the learner's day runs (the start 0–23, the end 1–24 with 24 midnight, the end after the start); they follow the account to the learner's other Macs. suggest_planning_the_day false: this Mac stops asking "Plan your day?" on a morning with nothing planned; true (the default) resumes. request_notifications true presses the pane's Allow Notifications: if macOS has never asked on this Mac, it shows its prompt there, and only the learner can answer it, so tell them to look for it; the call does not wait for the answer, and notifications_request says what happened. On a Mac that refused, nothing is shown: only the learner can allow ForeverLM again, in System Settings › Notifications. Returns the settings, notifications_status among them, and changed.

day_end_hour.description: The hour the learner's day ends, 1 to 24 (midnight), after day_start_hour. 24 unless set.

day_start_hour.description: The hour the learner's day starts, 0 (midnight) to 23. 6 unless set.

request_notifications.description: true: ask macOS to let ForeverLM notify on this Mac, as Allow Notifications in Settings › General does. Only a Mac never asked shows the prompt, and only the learner can answer it.

suggest_planning_the_day.description: true (the default): each morning today's calendar holds nothing the learner planned, ask "Plan your day?" with a card in the Studio window that waits until answered, and a notification once if ForeverLM is not in front. false: never.

name: set_day_settings

description: Turn a team's family plan on or off (team owner only). On needs this account to have paid for ForeverLM itself and makes its payment cover every member of the team; their Macs join by themselves. Off ends the coverage for every member of that team. The same switch as Pay for members' AI in the team's Members settings.
name: set_family_plan

description: Hide or unhide a course, video playlist, or meeting group. Hiding is visual only: its sources leave the Studio sources list and stay in knowledge for chat, search and reviews.

group_key.description: Course name, video-playlist id, or meeting group name.

hidden.description: true to hide, false to unhide.

name: set_group_hidden

description: Start or end the break a write-up earned. running=true starts it counting down on every one of the learner's devices; running=false ends it — and on a break that was never started, ends it as declined, which is the learner going straight back to work. A break cannot be started on a bout that has no write-up.

running.description: true starts the break, false ends or declines it.

name: set_learning_bout_break

description: Tick a meeting action item off, or reopen it. Pass item_id from list_meeting_action_items.

done.description: true marks it done (the default); false reopens it.

name: set_meeting_action_item_done

description: Give one meeting folder its own image in ForeverLM's sidebar, exactly as "Set Folder Image…" in the meetings context menu does — the group's own logo in place of the shared meetings icon. Pass group_id from list_meeting_groups. A web address follows the learner's account to their other devices; a path to a file on this Mac only renders on this Mac. The image is drawn to fill a small square tile, so prefer a square logo over a wide wordmark or a photo. Omit image_url to clear the choice and go back to the default icon.

image_url.description: An http(s) address of an image, or an absolute path to one on this Mac. Omit, or pass an empty string, to restore the default meetings icon.

name: set_meeting_folder_image

description: Set or clear when a recurring meeting series meets — what "Schedule…" in the meetings context menu does. A series with a schedule has each session's action items read out of its transcript as it lands (list_meeting_action_items). Pass group_id from list_meeting_groups; weekdays as 1 (Sunday) to 7 (Saturday); start as 24-hour HH:MM in the given IANA time zone; duration in minutes. Pass clear true to remove the schedule.

duration_minutes.description: How long the meeting is; at least 5.

start.description: 24-hour HH:MM in the time zone given.

timezone.description: IANA zone the clock is read in, e.g. America/Los_Angeles.

name: set_meeting_schedule

description: Change Settings › General › Memory review: budget_minutes, new_cards_per_day, auto_draft_cards, draft_nudges, prepare_review_questions, prepare_daily, ready_by_hour — one or several. Writes through the pane's own entry points, so the reminder and the runner follow. Returns the settings as get_memory_review_settings reads them plus `changed`.

auto_draft_cards.description: Draft cards into To Check in the background as the learner finishes sources (Mark as Read, read to the end, listening or watching complete), within the daily background AI limit. On by default. Follows your account.

budget_minutes.description: Minutes the daily memory review gets (5–120). Follows your account.

draft_nudges.description: Show the Cards to check corner card, and send the next morning's banner, while cards drafted in the background wait or finished sources have none. On by default; its Don't Ask Again turns it off. Follows your account.

new_cards_per_day.description: New cards a day's review introduces (1–100; 10 by default). Also sets how many sources are drafted in the background each day: one for every four new cards, at least one. Follows your account.

prepare_daily.description: Select the morning's cards at ready_by_hour and send the daily reminder on mornings that hold cards. Follows your account.

prepare_review_questions.description: Write review questions ahead of time for up to six sources a day a review is likely to be about (today's Schedule, then what was read in the last two days), so a review starts at once, within the daily background AI limit. A review without them still runs. On by default. Follows your account.

ready_by_hour.description: Hour (0–23, this Mac's clock) by which the morning's review should be waiting.

name: set_memory_review_settings

description: Choose which sources an explicitly identified Notebook's chats read — the checkboxes beside its sources in ForeverLM — and which of its context notebooks (the Notebooks in related_notebook_ids) they read too. Its own sources are ticked by default; a context notebook's sources reach its chats only once put in (context_notebook_ids), and taking it out keeps it linked. mode include ticks source_ids and puts context_notebook_ids in, as its box does: one that was out comes in with any of its sources the learner unticked still unticked, and one already in has every source of it ticked (ticking a source of a context notebook not in its chats puts that notebook in with that source alone); exclude unticks source_ids and takes context_notebook_ids out; only makes the chats read exactly source_ids and the context_notebook_ids; all ticks every source the chats draw on and none unticks them, leaving context notebooks in or out as they are. The choice is the learner's own (it follows their account, never a team's copy) and changes no Notebook membership or link: an unticked source stays where it is and any chat can still read it on request. New chats in the Notebook start with the ticked sources, and so does a chat not yet sent; a chat already under way keeps its own. What the Studio makes reads only the Notebook's own ticked sources. list_notebook_sources reports in_chat for each source and context_notebooks.

context_notebook_ids.description: Context notebook IDs (list_notebook_sources context_notebooks, or related_notebook_ids) to put into the Notebook's chats (include, only) or take out (exclude).

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

source_ids.description: Source IDs from list_notebook_sources: the Notebook's own or its context notebooks'. include, exclude and only take source_ids, context_notebook_ids or both.

name: set_notebook_source_selection

description: Store, replace, or remove the learner's own OpenRouter key — Settings › AI Usage › Your own key, exactly as pasting it into the pane does. Pass router and key to store or replace; pass clear: true (with router) to remove. The key goes to the learner's iCloud Keychain, never to a synced preference, a log, or the response; the response carries only the router and the key's last four characters. Ask before calling this with a key the learner did not just hand you.

clear.description: true removes the stored key; the AI features it was paying for stop until a key is stored again, apart from any leftover balance, which pays until it runs out.

key.description: The API key to store. Omit when clearing.

router.description: openrouter — the router the key belongs to.

name: set_own_router_key

description: Hide or unhide a podcast episode source. Hiding is visual only: the source leaves the Studio sources list and stays in knowledge for chat, search and reviews.

hidden.description: true to hide, false to unhide

name: set_podcast_episode_hidden

description: Show or stop force-showing a podcast episode when its show is hidden. A shown episode is back in the sources list and in knowledge for chat, search and reviews.

visible.description: true to force visible, false to remove the override

name: set_podcast_episode_visible_override

description: Hide or unhide all normal episodes for a podcast show by show name. A hidden show is muted: its episodes leave the Studio sources list and are excluded from chat, search, reviews and these tools, except an episode with a visible override (set_podcast_episode_visible_override), which comes back into both.

hidden.description: true to hide, false to unhide

show_name.description: Podcast show name as shown in Studio

name: set_podcast_show_hidden

description: Block or unblock a podcast show's future imports by show name — Studio's 'Never Import <show>'. A blocked show's episodes are never imported from Apple Podcasts again, however often they are played; episodes already in the library are untouched (use remove_all_from_podcast for those). This is about ingestion, not visibility: use set_podcast_show_hidden to mute a show whose episodes should stay.

blocked.description: true to stop importing the show, false to import it again

show_name.description: Podcast show name as shown in Studio

name: set_podcast_show_import_blocked

description: Write a study practice. Without practice_id it makes a new one: the learner's own, adopted at once, or with suggested true an assistant's suggestion, proposed for the learner to adopt or dismiss. With practice_id it changes that practice's title, why, rule, scope or status. rule is {kind, params}, kind one of reviewWindow, interleave, retrievalAfterReading, draftSeeds, newCardsPerDay or walkAfterReading. scope is all (the default), nb:<notebook id>, crs:<course id> or type:<source type>. A practice is the learner's own and never enters a team. Needs the Mac on ForeverLM's new iCloud sync.

practice_id.description: The practice to change, from list_practices. Omit to make a new one.

rule.description: What follows it once adopted: {kind, params}.

scope.description: all, nb:<notebook id>, crs:<course id> or type:<source type>.

suggested.description: True for an assistant's suggestion the learner has not agreed to: it waits as proposed. Defaults to false.

title.description: The practice in one sentence, as the learner would say it.

why.description: Why it helps, in a few sentences (at most 4 KB).

name: set_practice

description: Set how much of a memory review one source (source_id) or a whole kind of source (source_type, e.g. podcast) gets by default: quick is the contour only, standard adds a probe or two, deep works the full plan. Call it when the learner says so — "keep podcasts quick" — and confirm in half a sentence. Depth never skips the contour.

source_id.description: One source to set. Omit when setting a kind of source.

source_type.description: A kind of source to set the default for: article, paper, podcast, book, course, meeting, video, xPost.

name: set_review_depth

description: Plugins › Slack: flip one channel's switch — whether ForeverLM may read that channel (read_slack_channel, search_slack_messages). Stored on the gateway against the learner's account, so it holds on every device. In a workspace read through the ForeverLM bot, a channel can only be switched on after the learner invites @ForeverLM to it (visible to everyone in the channel); such a channel is refused with that explanation. Get team_id and channel ids from get_plugin_connections. Letting ForeverLM read a channel the learner did not name is their call: ask before switching one on.

channel_id.description: The channel's Slack id, e.g. C0123ABCD, or its name (#general).

enabled.description: true lets ForeverLM read the channel; false stops it.

team_id.description: The workspace's team_id (or name). Optional when only one workspace is connected.

name: set_slack_channel_enabled

description: Mark a Schedule source done or reopen it. Marking done records the source as reviewed on the completion date; linked/completed review sessions are reported separately.

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID that scopes the Schedule returned afterwards.

is_completed.description: true to mark done, false to reopen

name: set_source_completion

description: Hide or unhide a source in Studio. For podcast episodes this also updates the podcast episode hide state. Hiding is visual only: the source leaves the Studio sources list and stays in knowledge for chat, search and reviews.

hidden.description: true to hide, false to unhide

name: set_source_hidden

description: Mark an article, paper, or unclassified source as paywalled, or remove its paywalled status. Call this proactively whenever you discover a source is behind a paywall (e.g. fetching it returns a login, subscribe, or purchase page) so the app stops retrying it and shows the paywall recovery options.

is_paywalled.description: true to mark paywalled, false to clear

name: set_source_paywall_status

description: Mark a source read or unread — the reader's Mark as Read. Web articles, papers and videos track a read state; other source types are refused. Marking read stamps now; marking unread clears the stamp. For a video, read means watched, as in the sidebar's Mark as Watched and Mark as Not Watched: false clears its watch progress and any read stamp on every device, true finishes a video that has played in the Reader (its length is needed) and is refused for one that never has. The Schedule's completion state is separate: set_source_completion.

read.description: true to mark read (a video: watched), false to mark unread (a video: not watched). Defaults to true.

name: set_source_read

description: Change Settings › Sources for one source family, exactly as flipping its switches in the pane does. include_in_search_and_ai decides whether the family is part of what chat, search, reviews and the MCP library tools may draw on — false keeps a whole family away from the AI while its sources stay in the library and its tab stays pinnable. pinned puts the family's tab on the Studio tab bar or takes it off; the bar keeps at least one pinned family, so unpinning the last one is refused. Pass one switch or both. The choice follows the learner's account to their other devices.

family.description: The source family, as get_source_settings lists it.

include_in_search_and_ai.description: true: the family takes part in search, chat, reviews and the MCP library tools. false: it is left out of all of them.

pinned.description: true: the family's tab is on the Studio tab bar. false: it is taken off the bar; refused for the last pinned family.

name: set_source_settings

description: Hide or unhide every YouTube video from an uploader channel. A hidden channel is muted: its videos leave the Studio sources list and are excluded from chat, search, reviews and these tools, except a video with a visible override (set_youtube_video_visible_override), which comes back into both.

channel_name.description: YouTube channel name as shown in Studio

hidden.description: true to hide, false to unhide

name: set_youtube_channel_hidden

description: Show or stop force-showing a YouTube video when its channel is hidden. A shown video is back in the sources list and in knowledge for chat, search and reviews.

visible.description: true to force visible, false to remove the override

name: set_youtube_video_visible_override

description: Share a notebook with other people in one call, as its Share… in ForeverLM does. Without team_id: a Notebook already in one team uses that team, and a Notebook in no team gets a new team named after it (its title, emoji included). The team receives a copy of the Notebook with all its approved sources and their files, its Goals, Docs and chats, and from then on whatever is filed under the Notebook follows it into the team; the original stays in My Library. A Notebook two teams hold needs team_id. With team_id, the Notebook is shared into that team, or, when that team already has it, that team is used as it stands. Returns the team, whether it was made now, how many sources its notebook holds, the team's notebook (team_notebook_id), its members and invitations, and invitation_link: the link the team's Copy Invitation Link copies, which opens the team to anyone who has the link, with editing, when this account owns the team (link_opens_to_anyone is then true; a member's link is returned as it stands and it is false). Hand the link to the learner, saying so when it opens the team to anyone; null when iCloud has not shared the team yet, and message says why. Sharing gives the people invited copies of the notebook's sources, so the learner affirms once, in ForeverLM or here, that they may share them; until they have, this is refused with the question to ask: "Do you have the rights to share these sources with the people you invite, in line with copyright and each source's terms?" Pass rights_affirmed_by_learner: true only after asking the learner exactly that and hearing yes; their answer is recorded and not asked again. Refused when this account can only read the team, naming its owner to ask. Inviting named people is Apple's sharing sheet, in ForeverLM.

notebook_id.description: The notebook's Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

rights_affirmed_by_learner.description: true only after the learner, asked whether they have the rights to share these sources with the people they invite, in line with copyright and each source's terms, said yes. Needed while the learner has not yet affirmed; ignored once they have.

team_id.description: Share into this existing team (list_teams) instead of the team that holds the Notebook or a new one named after it.

name: share_notebook

description: Copy sources, Notebooks, Docs, chats or courses into a team. Sharing copies: each item gets a team-scoped copy in the team's library and the original stays exactly where it is, so nothing leaves My Library. Two members sharing the same paper produce one team copy, and sharing an item again updates its copy. A Notebook travels with its instructions, research questions and nested Goals, and by default with its sources, Docs and chats; from then on whatever is filed under the Notebook later (a source, a Goal, a Doc, a chat and its later turns) follows it into the team. A chat shares as a read-only transcript with the learner's scores, ratings and reading context stripped. A course shares with its lectures, readings, quizzes and every source on its path (copied into the team, files included), so each member takes it with their own watched lectures, completed quiz sittings, scores and gate; the learner's own progress stays behind, and sharing it again brings the team's copy up to date. A Doc, site or animation travels with its sources: the sources its record links (an animation's sources, a site's source_ids) are copied into the team and the team copy names the team's copies, and the web sources its body cites that only My Library holds (papers and books, or anything with a file here) come along unless include_cited_sources is false; the result lists them under linked_sources_shared, cited_sources_shared and sources_not_shared. Every kind but chat gives the team's members copies of sources, so the learner affirms once, in ForeverLM or through share_notebook or here, that they may share them; until they have, this is refused with the question to ask: "Do you have the rights to share these sources with the people you invite, in line with copyright and each source's terms?" Pass rights_affirmed_by_learner: true only after asking the learner exactly that and hearing yes; their answer is recorded and not asked again. A chat's transcript carries no source and asks nothing. Refused when the team is read-only for this account. Returns the team copy id for every original. To share a notebook with people in one step, team made and invitation link included, use share_notebook.

ids.description: IDs of the items to share: source IDs, Notebook IDs from list_notebooks, Doc IDs from list_docs, chat IDs from get_review_sessions, or course IDs from list_courses.

include_chats.description: kind notebook only: copy the Notebook's chats into the team as read-only transcripts too. Defaults to true.

include_cited_sources.description: kind doc only. Defaults to true: the web sources the Doc cites that My Library holds and the team does not — papers and books, or anything with a file here — travel with it, so teammates can open them from the Doc's cards; the result lists them under cited_sources_shared. Pass false to keep them behind. The sources the record itself links always travel (linked_sources_shared), because the team copy names them by the team's ids.

include_docs.description: kind notebook only: copy the Notebook's Docs into the team too. Defaults to true.

include_sources.description: kind notebook only: copy the Notebook's sources into the team too. Defaults to true.

rights_affirmed_by_learner.description: true only after the learner, asked whether they have the rights to share these sources with the people they invite, in line with copyright and each source's terms, said yes. Needed while the learner has not yet affirmed; ignored once they have, and for kind chat.

name: share_with_team

description: See a picture from a source in the learner's library, returned as an image rendered on the learner's Mac: a figure, diagram, photo or illustration from a paper, a book chapter or an article, or a slide from a video or meeting recording. Pass query with the printed figure label (Figure 3-4) or caption words to find one picture; pass page for a PDF page an earlier listing named, never a guessed number; pass neither to list the source's captioned pictures. Only pages that actually carry a picture are shown, so a page of prose and a paper's title page are refused: list the pictures first when you do not know which page holds the one you mean. A paper's figures come back cropped to the figure. Up to four matching pictures are attached as images, in the order listed; a longer listing is text only, and a second call with query or page narrows it to the picture wanted. For a video or recording the pictures are its captured slides, each listed with the stretch of the talk it was on screen for and the words spoken meanwhile: pass query with words from the slide or what was said over it, or slide with a number from an earlier listing; a video whose slides were never captured is refused and names extract_video_slides, which captures them. To see any moment of a video, slide or not, pass at with the time: the frame on screen then is captured from the video and attached, and crop zooms in on part of it or of a slide. Each entry also carries a Markdown line (foreverlm://image/…) that renders the picture inside ForeverLM — include it verbatim in a review transcript or Doc, not in an answer shown only in this client. Call it whenever the learner asks to see, show or display a figure, picture or slide, or asks what one looks like; for a paper figure with an explanation, prefer inspect_paper_figure. Needs the learner's Mac open and connected.

at.description: Video and recording sources only: capture and show the frame on screen at this time — seconds (265) or a clock reading (4:25, 1:02:03). Any moment works, not only captured slides: use it for a diagram being drawn, an animation, or a time the transcript names.

crop.description: Zoom in on part of one slide or frame: fractions of the picture from its top-left corner, each between 0 and 1. Look at the uncropped picture first, then crop to the part that matters.

page.description: PDF sources only: show this one-based page.

query.description: Figure label or caption words to match, for example Figure 3-4 or lactate dehydrogenase.

slide.description: Video and recording sources only: show this slide, by the number an earlier listing gave it.

source_id.description: Source ID from list_sources or a search result.

name: show_source_image

description: Split a Notebook into focused child notebooks by moving sources (and linked open questions) out of the parent pool. Each source moves to exactly one child — sources are not copied. The children are in the parent's library: a team's Notebook splits into that team. Use when a broad research thread naturally breaks into subfields.

keep_parent.description: Keep the parent notebook with remaining sources. Defaults to true. When false and the parent has no sources left after the split, everything else it holds (chats, Goals, tasks, Docs, courses, open questions, files) moves to the child that took the most sources and the parent is deleted.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

splits.description: Child notebooks to create. Each entry needs title and source_ids; gap_ids is optional.

gap_ids.description: Optional open-question IDs to move. Gaps linked to moved sources move automatically.

source_ids.description: Sources to move into this child.

title.description: Child notebook title.

topic.description: Optional discovery topic. Defaults to title.

name: split_notebook

description: Put a clock on a stretch of learning. Pass event_id (from get_calendar_events, with occurrence_date for one occurrence of a recurring event) to run one of the day's events, which gives the bout the event's title and what is left of its time; otherwise give a title. Only one bout runs at a time. The clock never ends the bout and never marks anything done — it is the learner who stops, and the write-up that finishes it.

event_id.description: Optional calendar event from get_calendar_events to run. The bout takes its title and length.

minutes.description: How long to run, 5 to 480. Defaults to what is left of the event, or 90.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook, from list_notebooks.

occurrence_date.description: With event_id, for one occurrence of a recurring event.

source_ids.description: Optional sources the bout is for.

title.description: What the bout is for, in the learner's words. Required when there is no event_id.

name: start_learning_bout

description: Start a review session on a topic. Returns relevant sources and cards for context, plus a Session ID. Keep that Session ID — you must pass it to end_review_session when the review is done (along with the transcript) to save the review. If reviewing a specific source, pass source_id or source_ids so the completed session is linked to that source. Pass notebook_id only when the learner explicitly asked to review within that Notebook; source_id or source_ids is then required and must belong to the Notebook. Notebook selection is never inherited implicitly. Do not use this for plain summary requests; call get_source_content and summarize directly instead. Begin the chat review by listing a compact, dynamic checklist of core concepts you plan to cover, then ask one deep question at a time.

notebook_id.description: Explicit Notebook ID (list_notebooks) or Goal ID (list_goals) to link this review to. Use only when the learner asked to work in that Notebook or on that Goal; requires source_id or source_ids from its approved pool. A review linked to a Goal counts toward it.

operation_id.description: Optional caller-generated idempotency key. Retry the exact same request with the same key to reuse its session; changed arguments fail closed.

source_ids.description: Optional source IDs being reviewed

name: start_review_session

description: Take cards off the learner's Canvas, as the inspector's Take Off Canvas does: each waits in the canvas's Library again (a notebook's source is drawn flat in its notebook's frame again when the frame is on the Canvas), and the arrows drawn to it go with it. Nothing is deleted from the library. Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Returns the cards taken off and those that were not on the Canvas.

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id> (a Doc, site, animation, audio overview or reading), idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id> (a shortcut to another canvas), chat:<session_id> (a chat) or picture:<image_id> (an image from list_images). A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

name: take_off_canvas

description: Transcribe a meeting session's recording with managed OpenAI speech-to-text and attach the transcript to the session. Downloads the recording from Drive, splits long audio into bounded sequential chunks, and sends them through ForeverLM's managed proxy; the OpenAI key stays server-side. Use get_meeting_group to find session source ids. A long recording takes minutes; cancel_ai_work stops it. Paid assistant work has a $3 per-operation ceiling by default. To continue beyond it, show the learner the estimate, obtain explicit approval, and pass that total as approved_spend_usd.

approved_spend_usd.description: Maximum USD the learner has approved for this one operation. Omit for the $3 default ceiling. Pass more than 3 only after showing the learner the estimate or published maximum and receiving explicit approval. The operation stops after the request that reaches the ceiling and starts no further paid request; completed work is kept.

source_id.description: Meeting session source id (from get_meeting_group) that has a recording artifact.

name: transcribe_meeting_recording

description: Go through the learner's cards to check, as Memory's To Check does, and only on the learner's word: each decision is theirs. action keep makes a card a Memory card, first asked the day after it is kept; keep with front, back, why, front_images or back_images keeps it with those changes (Edit, then Keep). Image arrays replace that face's pictures and [] removes them. also_from (draft cards only) chooses the other sources the card is kept on, replacing the ones it was drafted with: [] keeps it on its own source alone, and a list keeps it on each source named with its quote, copied word for word from that source's text (a source whose text does not print its quote refuses the keep). A kept card stands on those sources for good; changing them later means starting the card over. For a card from before cards (kind from_before), which is kept already, a new front alone rewords it, and a new back, why or image list starts it over as a new card. action skip drops a draft for good, so its seed is never drafted again, and retires a card from before cards, never asked again. decisions name cards by the card_id list_cards returned; keep_source_ids and skip_source_ids keep or skip every card to check on those sources at once. Returns what was kept (with item_id), skipped, refused (with why) and not found (decided already, expired, or not a card to check), and how many cards still wait.

also_from.description: With keep, on a draft: the other sources to keep the card on, replacing those it was drafted with; [] keeps it on its own source alone.

quote.description: The passage of that source that states what the card asks, copied word for word from its text (get_source_content).

source_id.description: Another source the card also stands on, from list_sources, a search or find_card_sources.

back.description: With keep: the answer in the learner's words.

back_images.description: With keep: pictures shown with the answer; pass [] to remove them. Each entry is the exact Markdown image line a ForeverLM image tool returned, or an object with its target and alt text.

alt.description: A short accessible description of the picture.

target.description: A foreverlm://image source or generated-image address.

card_id.description: A card_id from list_cards status to_check.

front.description: With keep: the question in the learner's words.

front_images.description: With keep: pictures shown with the question; pass [] to remove them. Each entry is the exact Markdown image line a ForeverLM image tool returned, or an object with its target and alt text.

alt.description: A short accessible description of the picture.

target.description: A foreverlm://image source or generated-image address.

why.description: With keep: why the answer is right, in the learner's words.

keep_source_ids.description: Keep every card to check on these sources.

skip_source_ids.description: Skip every card to check on these sources.

name: triage_cards

description: Restore an archived source to active. This also reverses remove_source by clearing the source URL's dismissal, preventing sync or discovery from immediately archiving it again. For sources backed by a local file (book chapters, saved article HTML) this also rebuilds the cached text content that archiving removed, so the source is immediately readable and reviewable again. Does not restore Schedule assignments — re-add to a day with the Schedule tools if needed.
name: unarchive_source

description: Undo the learner's last edit of their Canvas on this Mac, as ⌘Z there does, whether they made it by hand or asked for it here; with redo true, do again the edit last undone. Edits made within a moment of each other are one step. Returns whether there is more to undo and to redo.

redo.description: Redo instead of undo. Defaults to false.

name: undo_canvas

description: Plugins › YouTube › Followed channels › Stop Following: stop importing a followed channel's new uploads. The videos already imported, and the group holding them, stay. group_id comes from get_plugin_connections (youtube.followed_channels); the channel's name works too. The liked-videos / ForeverLM-playlist import source is not a channel: switch it with follow_youtube_liked_videos or follow_youtube_foreverlm_playlist.

group_id.description: The followed channel's group id, or its name.

name: unfollow_youtube_channel

description: Forget one passage-to-chat link from list_doc_chats. The Doc and the conversation both survive; only the claim that they are related is removed.
name: unlink_doc_chat
