description: The same call as unlink_page, kept for callers that learned it first. Prefer unlink_page.

doc_id.description: Doc ID from list_docs, with a linked kind.

name: unlink_google_doc

description: Take a link off an Idea. The record it pointed at is untouched — only the Idea stops naming it.

kind.description: The link's kind: source, artifact, chat, goal or notebook.

target_ids.description: The linked ids to take off.

name: unlink_idea

description: Make a linked page an editable Markdown Doc again — the inverse of link_page. ForeverLM's stored text copy becomes the Markdown body; the Doc keeps its id, title and Notebook links, and write_doc accepts it from then on. The page itself is not touched. Refused for a Doc that is not a linked page.

doc_id.description: Doc ID from list_docs, with kind google_doc, claude_artifact or codex_site.

name: unlink_page

description: Take down a Doc's page on foreverlm.com so its link stops working — the app's Unpublish. The Doc itself stays in the library. A Doc that is not published is not an error.
name: unpublish_doc

description: Take sources off the Schedule. With goal_id (a Goal or a Notebook) only that goal's tag comes off, and a source it shares with another goal stays scheduled for that one; without goal_id the sources leave the Schedule entirely. The sources stay in the library and their activity history is kept.

goal_id.description: Optional Goal or Notebook ID whose tag comes off. Omit to take the sources off the Schedule entirely.

source_ids.description: Source IDs on the Schedule

name: unschedule_sources

description: Move, retitle or rewrite an event in the Mac's Calendar that the learner owns alone (editable in get_calendar_events): pass event_id and what changes. date moves it to another day at the same time; start moves it and keeps its length unless end or duration_minutes is passed; end or duration_minutes alone changes its length. notes, location and url replace the field; pass "" to clear one. calendar_id moves it to another calendar. For one occurrence of a recurring event pass occurrence_date too; span future changes that occurrence and every one after it. An event with other people on it (has_other_people) is refused: changing it would send them an update, so the learner changes it in the Calendar app. Returns the event as the calendar now holds it.

calendar_id.description: Move it to this calendar (id or title).

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, "today" or "tomorrow": the day to move it to.

duration_minutes.description: New length in minutes, instead of end.

occurrence_date.description: For one occurrence of a recurring event: its occurrence_date from get_calendar_events.

span.description: For a recurring event: this occurrence (the default) or this and every later one.

name: update_calendar_event

description: Change one of the learner's canvases on their word, as its menu in the Space does: rename it (name), file it in one of their spaces (space_id from list_spaces) or take it out of every space (space_id ""), file it in a notebook (notebook_id) or take it out of its notebook (notebook_id ""), pin or unpin it in the Space sidebar (pinned), or move it to Trash or restore it (in_trash). Pass only what changes. Nothing placed on it moves. Returns the canvas as it is now.

in_trash.description: Move it to Trash (true) or restore it from Trash (false).

notebook_id.description: A notebook ID from list_notebooks to make it that notebook's canvas, or "" to take it out of its notebook.

pinned.description: Pin it in the Space sidebar (true) or unpin it (false).

space_id.description: A space ID from list_spaces to move it into, or "" to take it out of every space.

name: update_canvas

description: Change an arrow on the learner's Canvas, named by its edge_id (get_knowledge_map lists it under arrows) or by its ends (from and to: cards, or regions as region:<region_id>): relabel it (label; an empty label clears it), set its route (curve, straight or elbow), dashed, heads (end, both or none) or color (#RRGGBB; an empty string gives it the usual one), put it on a side of an argument (stance: supports draws it green, contradicts red, an empty string takes it off), or turn it into a mind-map branch or back into an arrow (tree). Pass only what changes. Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back.

color.description: The arrow's color as #RRGGBB, or an empty string for the usual one.

dashed.description: Draw the line dashed (true) or solid (false).

from.description: Instead of edge_id: where the arrow starts, a card by item_id or a region as region:<region_id>.

stance.description: supports (drawn green) or contradicts (red), or an empty string to take the stance off.

to.description: Instead of edge_id: where the arrow points to, a card by item_id or a region as region:<region_id>.

tree.description: Make it a mind-map branch (true), or a plain arrow again (false).

name: update_canvas_arrow

description: Change how cards already on the learner's Canvas look, as their right-click menu and handles do: tint them (color), fold them to their title line (folded true; false opens them), give them a width or height of their own (w from 160 to 720 and h from 56 to 2000, in the Canvas's own units; a card is 240 by 120 unless its kind says otherwise), or give them back the size their kind has (fit_to_content true: the width and height they were given are cleared). Beyond the look: show a source as a page of its PDF (page, one-based, drawn as the card with its title and authors under it, as a paper placed for the first time is; 0 shows the usual card again; a page past the PDF's end is its last; sources only), write the learner's words about why a card is on this canvas under it (annotation, at most 600 characters, an empty string takes it off; any card but an Idea, whose own note holds its words, so change an Idea's with update_idea), draw an Idea as plain words with no sticky note (plain true; false brings the note back; Ideas only) and mark a question, an Idea whose title ends with ?, answered or open again (answered; questions only). One call changes every card named; a region that holds a card made wider or taller than it is grows to hold it. Cards not on the Canvas are listed and left alone (place_on_canvas sets them down first). get_knowledge_map gives each card's rect and what it has been given. Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Returns the cards as they now are.

annotation.description: The learner's words about why these cards are on this canvas, drawn under them: at most 600 characters. An empty string takes them off. Not for an Idea.

answered.description: Mark these questions (Ideas whose title ends with ?) answered (true) or open again (false). Questions only.

color.description: A tint as #RRGGBB (the Canvas's own eight: #7F77DD, #1D9E75, #D85A30, #D4537E, #BA7517, #378ADD, #639922, #888780), or an empty string to give the card its kind's own tint again.

fit_to_content.description: Clear the width and height the cards were given, so each is the size its kind has (an Idea grows with its text, a clip, page or picture is as tall as its picture). Not with w or h.

folded.description: Fold the cards to their title line (true) or open them again (false).

item_ids.description: Cards by item_id as get_knowledge_map gives them: source:<source_id>, doc:<doc_id>, idea:<idea_id>, canvas:<canvas_id>, chat:<session_id>, picture:<image_id>, clip:<id> or page:<source_id>:<n>. A bare source, Doc or Idea id is accepted too.

page.description: Show these sources as this page of their PDF (one-based), or 0 to show the usual card again. Sources only; a page past the end of the PDF is its last.

plain.description: Draw these Ideas as plain words with no sticky note (true), or as notes again (false). Ideas only.

name: update_canvas_card

description: Change a region on the learner's Canvas, as its inspector and its handle do: rename it (name; a notebook's frame takes its notebook's name, so rename the notebook with update_notebook), recolour it, move it (x, y: its top left, carrying the cards inside it), resize it (w, h), link it to a notebook as its frame (notebook_id; an empty string unlinks it), fold it up (collapsed true: it draws as its name and the count of its cards, which stay placed where they are but are not drawn, and arrows to them wait; false opens it again), lock it (locked true: its cards cannot be dragged, nor it moved or resized by hand, until it is unlocked; a locked region refuses the changes to its geometry and layout below unless the same call unlocks it), set its layout (layout tree: a mind map, its cards laid out once from the tree edges among them (draw_canvas_arrow with tree) and then kept a tree by the Canvas; free: its cards stay where they are), fit it to what it holds (fit_to_content true: its cards and the regions inside it, with room for its name, never below 200 by 120) or grow it to hold cards (grow_to_hold: item_ids on the Canvas, with 24 to spare; it never shrinks). Positions are in the Canvas's own units, as get_knowledge_map gives each region's rect; a card is 240 by 120. Only on the learner's word: the Canvas is where they think, so never arrange it on your own initiative; to suggest an arrangement, show a lens (apply_map_lens) or ask_canvas. Each call is one edit of theirs, which Undo (⌘Z, or undo_canvas) takes back. Returns the region as it now is.

collapsed.description: Fold the region up (true) or open it again (false).

color.description: The region's tint as #RRGGBB. The Canvas's own: #7F77DD, #1D9E75, #D85A30, #D4537E, #BA7517, #378ADD, #639922, #888780. Omit for the next one.

fit_to_content.description: Fit the region to its cards and the regions inside it.

grow_to_hold.description: Grow the region to hold these cards (item_ids on the Canvas) whole, with 24 to spare.

layout.description: tree: a mind map, laid out once from the tree edges among its cards; free: its cards stay where they are.

locked.description: Lock the region (true) or unlock it (false).

notebook_id.description: Make it this Notebook's frame (a Notebook id from list_notebooks), or an empty string to unlink it.

region.description: A region's name (as get_knowledge_map lists it; a notebook's frame by its notebook's name) or its region_id.

name: update_canvas_region

description: Change one of the learner's kept cards, as Memory's All Cards does, and only on the learner's word. front alone rewords the card: it is asked in the new words from then on, its schedule untouched (the words it was kept with clear the rewording). A new back, why, front_images or back_images, or start_over true, starts the card over: the old card is retired with its answers and a new card is kept on the same passages, first asked the next day, returned as card_id beside previous_card_id. Image arrays replace that face's pictures and [] removes them. always_ask true asks the card in its own words every time, never a rewording; false lets its wording vary again. retire true retires the card, never asked again, its answers kept; it takes no other change. Pass card_id (or item_id) as get_due_cards or list_cards status kept returns it; a card still to check is changed with triage_cards. New words are checked first, as save_card_drafts checks a draft: words that point at the source unnamed (“this lecture”, “the paper”) are reworded once (the message says so), or the change is refused with the reason. Returns the card's card_id, item_id, ask and always_ask after the change.

always_ask.description: true: always ask it in its own words; false: let its wording vary again.

back.description: A new answer: starts the card over.

back_images.description: Replacement pictures for the answer face; starts the card over. Pass [] to remove them. Each entry is the exact Markdown image line a ForeverLM image tool returned, or an object with its target and alt text.

alt.description: A short accessible description of the picture.

target.description: A foreverlm://image source or generated-image address.

card_id.description: A card_id from get_due_cards or list_cards status kept.

front.description: The question in the learner's new words.

front_images.description: Replacement pictures for the question face; starts the card over. Pass [] to remove them. Each entry is the exact Markdown image line a ForeverLM image tool returned, or an object with its target and alt text.

alt.description: A short accessible description of the picture.

target.description: A foreverlm://image source or generated-image address.

item_id.description: The card's item_id, instead of card_id.

retire.description: Retire the card: never asked again.

start_over.description: Start the card over as it is asked now: a new card, first asked tomorrow.

why.description: A new line on why the answer is right: starts the card over.

name: update_card

description: Update an existing course's display metadata, or make a Notebook follow it (or stop following it). A course lives in no Notebook: it stands beside Notebooks, and a Notebook may follow it so its sources, and every source the course gains, join that Notebook. Requires the exact stable course_id from list_courses. Omit fields to keep them unchanged; pass an empty course_code, institution, instructors, or playlist_url to clear that field.

course_code.description: Course code, e.g. CS336 (optional; empty clears).

course_id.description: Exact stable course ID from list_courses.

notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks that follows the course from now on: it gains the course's sources and every source the course gains later. Other Notebooks keep following it; the course itself lives in no Notebook.

playlist_url.description: Official course playlist URL (optional; empty clears).

title.description: New non-empty course display title (optional).

unlink_notebook_id.description: Optional Notebook ID from list_notebooks that stops following the course. It keeps the sources it holds; later lectures no longer join it.

name: update_course

description: Record the learner's answer to a direction — pursued or set_aside, with their reason in their own words — or change it after a deeper look: reword it, rewrite its rationale, objection or next step, add evidence. The answer is the app's Pursue or Set aside; the next search reads it first, so pass the reason whenever the learner gave one. status proposed takes an answer back.

add_evidence.description: One to five papers or pages you actually opened. Never invent one.

citation.description: How the learner would cite it: "Jain et al., Science 2016".

doi.description: The DOI (10.xxxx/…), when it has one. Preferred: it is what the library matches on.

finding.description: The one thing it shows for this direction, in a sentence.

title.description: The paper's or page's title.

url.description: The page's address, when there is no DOI or the page itself is the evidence.

direction_id.description: Direction ID from list_directions or propose_directions.

next_step.description: The cheapest test. An empty string clears it.

objection.description: The strongest case against it. An empty string clears it.

rationale.description: New reason it is worth a look.

reason.description: The learner's reason for the answer, in their words.

title.description: New wording of the direction's sentence.

name: update_direction

description: Rename a Doc, change Draft/Production status, archive or restore it, hide or show it, change its optional home Notebook, or replace its complete Notebook-link set without copying the document. Omit a field to keep it unchanged; pass an empty home_notebook_id to clear the home. Archiving keeps the Doc or Site whole — body, page and Notebook links — and only takes it off the Docs and Sites lists, which show it again under Archived. Hiding is the learner's view rather than the record's state: the record does not change and no teammate sees it, but every Mac signed into the account hides it; the lists show it again only under Hidden.

home_notebook_id.description: Optional new home Notebook; empty clears it.

is_archived.description: Optional: true archives the Doc or Site, false restores it to the list. Nothing else about it changes.

is_draft.description: Optional Draft status. False marks the Doc as Production.

is_hidden.description: Optional: true hides the Doc or Site from the Docs and Sites lists on every Mac signed into this account, false shows it again. The record, its page and its team copies are untouched; only the hide itself syncs.

title.description: Optional new title.

name: update_doc

description: Change one comment on a Doc: body rewrites its words (only when the learner asks, for a comment that is not the assistant's own), resolved true resolves its thread and false reopens it (a resolved thread is no longer marked in the page and moves under Resolved in Comments). Pass body, resolved, or both. A team's page is refused.

body.description: Optional new words for the comment.

resolved.description: Optional: true resolves the comment's thread, false reopens it.

name: update_doc_comment

description: Change an Idea after it was jotted down: reword it, write or clear its note, put it away or bring it back. Every field is optional and an omitted one is left alone. Rewording is the learner's call — do not rewrite their sentence unless they asked. To put an Idea away and keep it, pass status "archived"; deleting is delete_idea and is not undoable.

notes.description: The note. Pass an empty string to clear it.

title.description: New wording. Cannot be emptied.

name: update_idea

description: Update a timebound Goal after creation: retarget its deadline, rename it, change its topic/description, adjust the daily target or discovery, tag it to another Notebook or untag it, link it to the Doc, Site or animation it is for (artifact_id) or unlink it, or mark it done/archived. Every field is optional — omitted fields keep their current value. Use this rather than deleting and recreating a Goal, so its sources, review history, and open questions survive. IMPORTANT — when the user sets or changes a deadline and hasn't named a date, do not guess silently: look at how many approved sources the Goal has and its daily target, propose a specific date with your reasoning ('12 sources at 3/day is ~4 days of reading, plus 3 days to draft — I'd suggest the 29th'), and confirm with the user before calling this. After changing a deadline, re-pace the remaining sources with assign_sources_to_day.

artifact_id.description: The Doc, Site or animation this Goal is for, by id (from list_docs, list_animations or a save_site result): the Goals tab opens it from the row. Pass an empty string to unlink. Refused when no record has the id.

daily_target.description: Sources to cover per study day.

description.description: New free-text description. Pass an empty string to clear it.

discover.description: Whether to auto-discover related sources by topic.

end_date.description: New deadline as YYYY-MM-DD. Must be in the future.

notebook_id.description: Notebook to tag the Goal to. Must name a top-level Notebook; pass an empty string to untag it and let the Goal stand on its own.

status.description: Lifecycle state: 'active', 'done', or 'archived'. Mark 'done' when the deliverable is finished. A Goal past its deadline that is still 'active' is reported as overdue, not complete — only set 'done' when the work is actually finished.

title.description: New title. For an outcome Goal this is the deliverable, e.g. 'Write article about mitochondrial transplantation'.

topic.description: New natural-language topic used for source discovery.

name: update_learning_goal

description: Update an explicitly identified Notebook's settings or archive/restore it. Omitted fields keep their current value; pass instructions "" to clear them, or repository "" to unlink the GitHub repository. Archiving hides the Notebook from normal lists without deleting its sources, Goals, chats, notes, or review history.

discover.description: Enable or disable auto-discovery of related sources by topic. Enabling it, or changing the topic while enabled, runs a discovery pass.

instructions.description: The learner's standing instructions for this Notebook — guidance to follow in every chat that works in it (the app's Instructions field). Pass "" to clear.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

related_notebook_ids.description: Replaces the complete directional set of this Notebook's context notebooks: the related Notebooks whose sources and synthesis it can draw on. Linking alone puts nothing into its chats: the learner puts a context notebook in with its box in the Sources column, or set_notebook_source_selection does with context_notebook_ids. A Notebook unlinked leaves its chats too. Pass [] to clear; omit to keep current links. Use list_notebooks for IDs.

repository.description: The GitHub repository this Notebook is about, as owner/repo (owner/repo.git and github.com URLs are accepted). Only the name is stored; chats read it live through the GitHub tools. Pass "" to unlink; omit to keep the current repository.

research_questions.description: Replaces the Notebook's defining research questions wholesale, in priority order. Pass [] to clear; omit to keep the current list.

status.description: Set archived to hide the Notebook without deleting anything; set active to restore it.

summary.description: A short description shown under the title on the Notebook's card (the app's Description field): one line of display copy, not guidance for the model. Pass "" to clear.

think_first.description: This Notebook's own Think first level, over the library's (set_app_setting think_first.level): off; summariesAndStudio asks for the learner's own line before a source's gist, a Studio report and Find directions; alsoChat also asks for a guess before a question in the Notebook's chat. library takes the Notebook's own level away so the library's applies. It is the learner's own, never a teammate's. Ask the learner before changing it.

title.description: New notebook title.

topic.description: Natural-language topic for discovery. Pass "" to reset to the title.

name: update_notebook

description: Change the learner's collections of Notebooks, the Collections ForeverLM groups its Notebooks by (list_notebook_collections lists them). action create makes a collection called name, with notebook_ids in it when given, and answers its id; rename gives collection_id the name; delete deletes collection_id, and the Notebooks in it stay as they are; add_notebooks and remove_notebooks put notebook_ids in collection_id or take them out. A collection changes nothing about a Notebook, and the change follows the learner's account to their other devices.

collection_id.description: Collection ID from list_notebook_collections. Required for rename, delete, add_notebooks and remove_notebooks.

name.description: The collection's name, for create and rename. A leading emoji is its icon.

notebook_ids.description: Notebook IDs from list_notebooks: the Notebooks to put in (create, add_notebooks) or take out (remove_notebooks).

name: update_notebook_collection

description: Replace a Notebook's synthesis notes (markdown) — the accumulated record of what the learner understands. Use append_notebook_notes to add without replacing.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

name: update_notebook_notes

description: Change a task. Omitted fields keep their value. Pass assignee_record_name "" to unassign and due_date "" to clear the due date. Setting status to done stamps the completion; moving it back clears it. Refused when the Notebook's team is read-only for this account.

assignee_record_name.description: A member's user_record_name, "me", or "" to unassign. Team Notebooks only.

doc_id.description: Doc the task is about; pass "" to clear.

source_id.description: Source the task is about; pass "" to clear.

title.description: New title.

name: update_notebook_task

description: Update an existing open question on a Notebook (status, summary, linked source, severity).

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

source_id.description: Link to a source in this Notebook's pool

name: update_open_question

description: Rename a review session or chat, file it under a Notebook, pin it, or hide it from the sidebar — what the chat's sidebar row offers. Omit a field to keep it; pass notebook_id "" to move the chat out of its Notebook into the ungrouped Chats list. Linked sources are changed with update_review_session_sources.

is_hidden.description: Optional: true hides the chat from the sidebar on every Mac signed into this account (the Hidden fold under Chats lists it again), false shows it. The chat, its transcript, its Notebook and its team copies are untouched, and search and get_review_sessions still find it; only the hide itself syncs.

is_pinned.description: Optional: true pins the chat, as its row's Pin Chat does: Home's sidebar lists it under Pinned, newest pin first, on every device signed into this account; false unpins it. Only the pin syncs, never the chat's record; a day's memory review is never pinned. get_review_sessions marks pinned chats [pinned].

notebook_id.description: The Notebook (from list_notebooks) or the Goal (from list_goals) to file the chat under — a chat clearly about a Goal's sources belongs on that Goal, where its row and editor list it and its reviews read it as history; "" removes it from its Notebook or Goal.

title.description: New title. Must not be empty.

name: update_review_session

description: Replace the set of sources linked to a review session. On a day's memory review (id memory-YYYY-MM-DD) a source left out of the set is removed from the day, as the × on its chip does: the tutor stops asking about it when the review is next opened, and a reopen on any device leaves it out.

source_ids.description: Source IDs to link (replaces the current set).

name: update_review_session_sources

description: Change a scheduled task. Omitted fields are left alone; pass clear_notebook to detach its Notebook, and a complete source_ids list to replace its attachments.

clear_notebook.description: Detach the Notebook instead of setting one.

source_ids.description: Replaces the attached sources entirely.

name: update_scheduled_task

description: Update metadata of an existing source (title, author, type, paper venue/year/DOI, parent_group, content, paywall status).

parent_group.description: New course/book display title or stable group ID (optional)

title.description: New title (optional)

name: update_source

description: Replace the stored text content (and optionally title/author) of an existing source, matched by source_id or canonical url. Reviews, schedule placements, and other metadata are untouched. Ingest-scoped plugin clients can only update sources they added themselves.

source_id.description: Source ID to update. Provide this or url.

title.description: New title (optional).

url.description: Canonical URL of the source to update. Provide this or source_id.

name: update_source_content

description: Rewrite the note or the since-publication update, change the color, link the chat the update came from, or set the papers it cites on an existing highlight. Pass an empty note to turn it back into a bare highlight. The passage itself is not editable — mark a different passage with create_source_highlight instead.

color.description: New marker color: yellow, green, blue, pink, or purple.

highlight_id.description: Highlight ID from list_source_highlights or search_source_highlights.

note.description: New note text, in the learner's own words. An empty string clears the note and leaves a bare highlight.

publication_update.description: What has been learned since the source was written, shaped as in create_source_highlight, replacing the update the mark has. An empty string clears it.

references.description: The papers or pages the update (or note) cites, replacing the list; an empty array clears it. At most 20, each shaped as in create_source_highlight.

citation.description: How the note names it, such as "Vozza et al., PNAS 2014".

title.description: The paper's title, if known.

url.description: The paper's or page's address, for one without a DOI.

session_id.description: The chat the note came from, by its id from import_review_chat or get_review_sessions (or a foreverlm://chat/<id> link); the reader opens it from the mark. An empty string unlinks it.

name: update_source_highlight

description: Change the learner's spaces of pages, the Spaces in the sidebar of ForeverLM's Space (list_spaces lists them). action create makes a space called name, moves doc_ids into it when given, and answers its id; rename gives space_id the name; trash puts space_id in the Space's Trash, where it leaves the sidebar and its pages stay in All, in no space, and restore brings it back with them; delete deletes space_id for good, and the pages in it stay, listed in All; move_docs moves doc_ids into space_id, each out of the space it was in, since a page is in one space at a time; remove_docs takes doc_ids out of whatever space each is in. Only the learner's own pages, linked Google Docs, sites and readings in no notebook can join a space, not a team's record, an animation or an audio overview. A space changes nothing about a Doc, and the change follows the learner's account to their other devices.

doc_ids.description: Doc IDs from list_docs: the pages to move in (create, move_docs) or take out of their space (remove_docs).

name.description: The space's name, for create and rename. A leading emoji is its icon.

space_id.description: Space ID from list_spaces. Required for rename, trash, restore, delete and move_docs.

name: update_space

description: Change one of the learner's lists in their Space on their word, as its menu does: rename it (name), file it in one of their spaces (space_id from list_spaces) or take it out of every space (space_id ""), pin or unpin it in the Space sidebar (pinned), move it to Trash or restore it (in_trash), put goals or ideas in it (add_item_ids, each moved out of any list it was in) or take them out (remove_item_ids). A goal goes only in a goals list and an idea only in an ideas list. Pass only what changes; the goals and ideas themselves are not changed. Returns the list as it is now.

add_item_ids.description: Goal IDs from list_goals for a goals list, or Idea IDs from list_ideas for an ideas list.

in_trash.description: Move it to Trash (true) or restore it from Trash (false).

pinned.description: Pin it in the Space sidebar (true) or unpin it (false).

remove_item_ids.description: Goal IDs from list_goals for a goals list, or Idea IDs from list_ideas for an ideas list.

space_id.description: A space ID from list_spaces to move it into, or "" to take it out of every space.

name: update_space_list

description: Dismiss a candidate from list_video_cited_papers, or restore one that was dismissed. Pass status 'dismissed' to wave a candidate off, or 'pending' to put it back in play (a candidate with neither a DOI nor a url is restored as 'unresolved'). An imported candidate cannot be changed here — remove its library source instead.

status.description: 'dismissed' to wave the candidate off, 'pending' to restore a dismissed one

name: update_video_cited_paper_status

description: Correct one working note: change its sentence, its kind or both. Pass the whole note_id from list_working_notes, or the first eight characters or more of it. Do it when the learner says a note is wrong or out of date; to remove one, use forget_working_note.
name: update_working_note

description: Revision-safely replace a Doc's canonical Markdown — the whole body, so only for a short Doc or a complete rewrite. To change parts of a Doc, especially a long one whose body would not fit in a tool call, use edit_doc instead. Every linked Notebook immediately sees the same edit. A published Doc's page is not re-rendered unless publish is true: without it the result says the page is stale and publish_doc updates it; with it a Doc that already has a page gets the page updated in the same call, at the same address with the same readers (a Doc with no page is not published by it). Refused for a linked page (kind google_doc, claude_artifact or codex_site), whose text is edited where it lives — the refusal says how to refresh ForeverLM's copy (link_page with text), make it an editable Doc (unlink_page), or make it ForeverLM's own published page (adopt_page). Markdown may link to another Doc as [Title](foreverlm://doc/<doc_id>) and to a notebook as [Title](foreverlm://notebook/<notebook_id>); ForeverLM opens those in place. Write each reference to the web — a paper, an article, a page — as its own line or list item holding one link, optionally followed by a short detail after a dash: `- [Title](https://doi.org/10.1038/…) — Nature, 2024`. ForeverLM draws such a line as a source card, marks it with a check when the source is already in the Doc's library (by URL, DOI or arXiv id — a team Doc's cards ask the team library, a Doc in My Library asks My Library) and offers Add to Sources when it is not. A link inside a sentence stays a plain link in the prose and gets the same card in the margin beside its paragraph, so citing a source where a claim is made is as good as listing it. So cite as a link, never as text: `([Sgarbi et al., 2006](https://doi.org/10.1042/BJ20051748))`, not `(Sgarbi et al., Biochem J, 2006, doi:10.1042/BJ20051748)` — a DOI or PMID typed into the sentence earns no card and leaves the journal, year and identifier in the prose, where the card would have carried them.

publish.description: When the Doc has a published page, update it with this body in the same call (same address, same readers). Ignored for a Doc that is not published. Defaults to false.

name: write_doc

description: Create or replace a Markdown artifact in a Notebook's Other files workspace. To create a new file, omit expected_revision. To edit an existing file, first call read_notebook_markdown_file and pass its exact revision; a stale or missing revision fails instead of overwriting newer work.

expected_revision.description: Exact SHA-256 revision returned by read_notebook_markdown_file. Required when the path already exists; omit only when creating.

notebook_id.description: Notebook ID from list_notebooks.

path.description: Relative .md or .markdown path inside the Notebook.

name: write_notebook_markdown_file

description: File what a bout produced, which is what earns its break. Ask the learner two questions first and file their own words, never a summary you wrote for them: what did you learn, and what do you not understand yet. The second is the more valuable half — it is what the next bout is for — so ask it even when they only volunteer the first. Stops the clock if the bout is still running.

break_minutes.description: Override the earned break, 5 to 20. Defaults to a minute of rest for every nine learned.

learned.description: What the learner says they learned, in their words. Required.

unclear.description: What they say they still do not understand, in their words.

name: write_up_learning_bout
